search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: Write through createComplaint. A new door that raises complaints should call createComplaint (passing its transaction) rather than insert — that is how the deadline and the opening history line are guaranteed. Labels in, values stored, labels out. Categories a person picks are configuration ( complaints.categories ); stored values are the enum. Map with categoryValue and back with categoryLabel — never show a stored enum. Finishing needs the capability, both ways. Keep the FINISHED COMPLAINT check in changeComplaintStatus for any new status. Photographs through the picker. ACCEPTED IMAGE TYPES and attachments.maxPerComplaint ; never a literal accept list.

The Complaints screen is where every complaint a customer has raised waits until somebody has dealt with it. You can raise one in the middle of a call , from a customer's record , or straight from this screen — all three write the same kind of record, with the same deadline and the same history. Whoever resolves it writes down what was done, and that note is what the customer record shows afterwards. The limits on this page — how many photographs, how long before a complaint is overdue — are the settings your CRM is using right now, read live.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: The Complaints screen, for a manager viewing the team. Complaints Log complaint Open. 4 In progress. 3 Resolved. 21 Oldest open. 9 days Customer told. 18/21 Open complaints by age 2 under 3 days 3 3 to 7 days 2 over 7 days Oldest open: Customer A · 9 days The list is sorted by deadline , soonest first, so the complaint most at risk of going overdue is at the top. You see complaints on customers in your own book; a manager sees the team's.

search.heading: Raising a complaint
search.text: There are three doors, and they ask nearly the same questions.

search.heading: From a call
search.text: When the customer complains while you are on the phone, choose the outcome Complaint in the call panel. The panel then asks: Field What to put in it What they are asking for A replacement, a credit note, a technical visit, a sales visit, a transport check, an accounts check, or management intervention. This decides which desk the complaint goes to — see below. Required. Complaint category What kind of problem it is. Complaint description The complaint in the customer's own words. If you leave it empty, your call notes are used instead — but one of the two must say something. Upload picture Photographs of the damaged or short goods, if the customer sent any. Request CN Yes if the customer asked for a credit note. Nothing else is asked. Saving the call saves the complaint in the same go. If the customer already has an open complaint in the same category , nothing new is raised: the call is added to that complaint's history as Raised again on a call: … , and if they asked for a credit note this time, the request is added to it. The confirmation tells you which happened. A complaint raised on a call always starts at Normal priority. If it is more urgent than that, open it on the Complaints screen afterwards and raise the priority — the deadline moves with it.

search.heading: From the Complaints screen or a customer's record
search.text: The Log complaint dialog. Log complaint. Product Quality ▾ Normal ▾ Urgent and Critical shorten the deadline Choose files JPG, JPEG or PNG - photos of the damaged or short goods, if any. No Yes Cancel Save Press Log complaint. On the Complaints screen it is top right. On a customer's record it is the Complaint button in the header. Pick the customer. Search by company, name or mobile number. The mobile number fills itself in from the customer and goes on the complaint, so whoever resolves it knows which number to ring back. Choose the category and the priority. Normal is right for almost everything. Choose Urgent or Critical only when the customer is genuinely held up — a line stopped, an order unusable. Describe it in the customer's words. Write what the customer said, not your summary of it. The description is required — Describe the complaint in the customer's words appears if you leave it empty. Add photographs, and answer Request CN. Both are optional. Then press Save . The message says Complaint logged , or Complaint logged — 2 of 3 files attached if a picture did not make it.

search.heading: Categories
search.text: The categories you can pick from are a list a manager keeps on the Settings screen, so the same list appears in the call panel, the Complaints dialog and the customer record. As shipped it is: Category Use it for Product Quality The product itself is wrong — drying, finish, consistency Short Quantity Fewer cans or less in the can than billed Leakage / Packaging Leaking, dented or broken containers Wrong Product Goods arrived that are not what was ordered Delivery Delay It came late Price Issue The rate or discount is disputed Billing Issue The bill is wrong Transport Issue A problem with the transporter or the delivery itself Sales Service A complaint about how they were served by our people Other Anything else

search.heading: Photographs
search.text: - You can attach up to pictures to one complaint. The picker counts them — 3 of 6 pictures — and stops at the limit, telling you how many it left off. - Only JPG and PNG photographs are offered. Each file can be up to MB. - A file is checked by what it actually is , not what it is called. A document renamed photo.jpg is refused. - Choosing the same picture twice adds it once. - A picture that fails to upload never loses the complaint. The complaint is saved and the message says how many files made it. Anybody who can see the complaint can open its photographs: they are thumbnails in the complaint's drawer, and clicking one opens it full size.

search.heading: Asking for a credit note
search.text: Request CN is a yes-or-no question, and that is all you answer. You do not need to find the bill or work out an amount — accounts hold the ledger, and they pick up the bill and the amount from the request. When you choose Yes, the dialog says Accounts take it from here - they pick up the bill and the amount. In the complaint's drawer the Credit note line then reads Requested , and later shows how far it has got ( Under review , Approved , Rejected , Issued ), the amount and the credit note's reference once accounts have issued one. If nobody asked, it reads Not asked for .

search.heading: Where a complaint goes
search.text: On a call, what the customer is asking for decides the desk: They are asking for It goes to Replacement Dispatch Credit note Accounts Technical visit Technical Sales visit Sales Transport check Logistics Accounts check Accounts Management intervention Management A complaint raised from the Complaints dialog or a customer's record does not ask this, so it starts with Operations . The desk is shown in the Assigned to column. You can move a complaint to a different desk with Reassign (see below).

search.heading: Working a complaint
search.text: Click any row to open it. A complaint, opened. Customer A. Open SLA breached Normal ▾ Leakage / Packaging · open 9 days Raised by · Raised · Category · Mobile · With · Goods · Credit note Two drums dented on arrival, one leaking. Open · Logged on a call by a telecaller ☐ The customer has been told the outcome Mark resolved Reassign

search.heading: Changing the priority
search.text: While a complaint is open, the priority is a drop-down at the top of the drawer. Changing it moves the deadline , counted from when the complaint was first raised — so a complaint three days old that you mark Critical shows as overdue straight away. That is deliberate: the customer has already been waiting three days. The change is written into the status history.

search.heading: Reassigning
search.text: Press Reassign , pick a desk (Operations, Accounts, Dispatch, Quality or Management) and confirm. The complaint moves to In progress and the history says who moved it where.

search.heading: Resolving
search.text: Write what was done. The resolution notes are required. Without them you see Write what was done before closing - this is what the customer record will show. Tick whether the customer has been told. Be honest — an unticked box shows on the resolved complaint as The customer has NOT been told the outcome. Press Mark resolved. The complaint moves to the Resolved tab. Its drawer then shows How it was resolved : your note, when, and whether the customer was told. If Mark resolved is greyed out, hovering over it says why: Closing a complaint needs the right to resolve complaints , or Already resolved .

search.heading: Statuses
search.text: Status Tab What it means Open Open Raised, nobody has moved it yet In progress In progress Somebody is working it — reassigning sets this Awaiting customer In progress Waiting for something from the customer Resolved Resolved Closed with a resolution note Closed Resolved Finished Rejected Resolved Not upheld

search.heading: Deadlines
search.text: Every complaint gets a resolution deadline the moment it is raised, set by its priority: Once a complaint passes its deadline unresolved, its age turns red on the list, the drawer says SLA breached , and managers get a notification: Complaint past its SLA . A complaint still open after days is also counted on the manager's dashboard red-flag strip.

search.heading: On the customer record
search.text: Every complaint appears on the customer's record under its own tab. While a complaint is open, the record's alert line says so — Open … complaint - mention it before anything else. — and the call panel shows Open complaint at the top, so whoever rings the customer next raises it first.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I logged a complaint on a call, but no new row appeared.. The customer already had an open complaint in the same category. Your call was added to that one's history instead of creating a duplicate. Open it and look at the status history. Can I log a complaint without a call?. Yes — Log complaint on this screen, or Complaint on the customer's record. Neither counts as a call. My photograph did not attach.. Check it is a JPG or PNG under MB, and that you have not reached the limit of . The complaint itself is always saved. Do I need to know which bill the credit note is against?. No. Answer Yes to Request CN and accounts find the bill and the amount. Why can't I press Mark resolved?. Resolving a complaint is a manager's decision. Ask your manager, or reassign the complaint to the desk that should deal with it. The category I need is not in the list.. Ask a manager — the list is on the Settings screen and can be changed without waiting for a release. Until then, choose Other and describe it. I made it Critical and it immediately said SLA breached.. The deadline is counted from when the complaint was raised, not from when you changed the priority. If it has already been open longer than the Critical deadline, it is overdue — which is true.

A complaint is the customer's account of something that went wrong, written down at the moment they said it, given a deadline, routed to a desk, and closed only when somebody writes down what was done. This tab explains the rules behind each of those steps, why each rule exists, and the settings that change them. Every value quoted is the one your CRM is using right now.

search.heading: The life of a complaint
search.text: From the customer's words to a resolved complaint.

search.heading: One record, whichever door it came through
search.text: A complaint raised on a call, from the Complaints screen, from a customer's record, from a collections call or from a salesman's handset is the same record : the customer, a category, the customer's words, a priority, a deadline, a desk, a status, and a history line saying who raised it. The customer record used to have its own, smaller complaint form — category and description and nothing else. So a telecaller standing on the customer's record while the customer described a damaged can could not attach the photograph or record that they asked for a credit note. The two forms had drifted because nobody went back to the small one when the big one grew. There is now one dialog, and the only thing that differs between the screen and the record is whether it asks who the complaint is about. A complaint raised on a call does not duplicate an open one. If the customer already has a complaint in the same category that is Open, In progress or Awaiting customer, a call that raises it again adds a line to that complaint's history — Raised again on a call: … — instead of opening a second one. If the customer asks for a credit note this time and had not before, the request is added to the existing complaint. A request already made is never withdrawn by a later call: withdrawing it is the resolver's decision. A complaint is never refused for its heading. A category that does not match a known one is stored as Other rather than refused. A complaint filed under the wrong heading is still a complaint; one refused at the door is a customer nobody rings back. Raising a complaint is not a call. A complaint logged from the Complaints screen or the record does not create a call. The dialog does not ask how the complaint reached us, and inventing an inbound call would inflate the call counts. A complaint raised on a call is linked to that call.

search.heading: Categories: words people use, values the system stores
search.text: The list a person picks from is configuration — complaints.categories on the Settings screen (currently ) — so the call panel, the Complaints dialog and the customer record all offer the same list, and a manager can change it without a release. What is stored is a fixed set of ten values. Several words people use land on the same stored value: "Leakage / Packaging", the older "Packaging Damage" and "Leakage" are all stored as packaging damage. Because of that, neither direction can be worked out from the other, so both are written down once: Offered as Stored as Shown as Product Quality product quality Product Quality Short Quantity shortage Short Quantity Leakage / Packaging packaging damage Leakage / Packaging Wrong Product wrong product Wrong Product Delivery Delay dispatch delay Delivery Delay Price Issue pricing Price Issue Billing Issue billing issue Billing Issue Transport Issue delivery Transport Issue Sales Service service Sales Service Other other Other Older words the app has offered or received (Packaging, Staff, Transport, Rate Dispute, Late Delivery and more) still resolve to the right stored value, so a deployment whose list was curated before the current wording keeps working. Adding a category. A new word added on the Settings screen is stored correctly only if its name, lower-cased with spaces turned into underscores, is already one of the ten stored values . Anything else is stored as Other . Adding a genuinely new kind of complaint needs a release.

search.heading: Priority and the deadline
search.text: Every complaint has a priority — Normal , Urgent or Critical — and the priority decides how long it has to be resolved: A complaint whose priority nobody chose takes (Normal is stored as medium ). That applies to complaints raised on a call, on a collections call and from the handset — none of those ask. Changing the priority moves the deadline, measured from when it was raised. When somebody changes an open complaint's priority, the deadline is recalculated as raised time + the new priority's hours — not from now. A three-day-old complaint reclassified Critical reads as breached at once. The deadline is a promise about how long the customer waits, not about how long we have left once we notice. Measuring from now would hand a fresh eight hours to the complaint that has already had seventy-two, and the deadline figures would flatter exactly the cases that went worst. The change is written into the complaint's history so the resolver can see why the deadline under their nose moved. Breaching the deadline. Once an hour, every unresolved complaint past its deadline that has not been escalated before is marked escalated, and every manager and admin gets a notification: Complaint past its SLA . Each complaint escalates once . On the list, the complaint's age turns red; in the drawer the badge reads SLA breached . A complaint still open after days is counted on the manager's red-flag strip on the dashboard.

search.heading: Routing: what the customer asks for decides the desk
search.text: Who deals with a complaint is not a second question for the telecaller; it follows from what the customer is asking for , which the call panel requires: Asking for Desk Replacement Dispatch Credit note Accounts Technical visit Technical Sales visit Sales Transport check Logistics Accounts check Accounts Management intervention Management Every complaint used to be assigned to "Operations", which is not a routing decision — it is the absence of one. A replacement is the godown's, a credit note is accounts', a technical visit is technical's. The telecaller knows what the customer asked for; they cannot know which desk handles it. So the desk is derived. The desk is a name , not a person. Nobody is notified when a complaint lands on a desk, and nobody is notified when its priority changes — there is no single person behind "Dispatch" to tell.

search.heading: Photographs
search.text: Validated on the bytes, never the name. A file is checked by reading its first bytes — the signature every JPG, PNG or PDF begins with. The file name and the type the browser reports both come from the person's phone and prove nothing; anybody can rename a file .jpg . A refused file is named precisely: … is not a JPG, PNG or PDF, whatever it is named. - Accepted types are configuration (currently ). The complaint picker offers only JPG and PNG photographs. - Each file may be up to MB. - One complaint carries at most . The picker refuses the extras on the screen, by count, so nothing silently disappears after Save. A photograph never blocks the complaint. The complaint is written first. Each photograph is then stored and attached on its own; one that fails does not stop the others, and the message says 2 of 3 files attached rather than pretending all or nothing. Whoever can see the complaint can see its photographs. A photograph is read only through the CRM itself, which checks that the person asking can see the customer the complaint belongs to. A file you may not see and a file that does not exist answer the same way, so the photographs cannot be used to find out which customers exist. Files uploaded for a form that was then abandoned belong to nothing and are swept after hours.

search.heading: Credit notes: the telecaller answers yes, accounts do the rest
search.text: A credit-note request is a yes, and nothing more. The telecaller answers one question — did the customer ask for a credit note? Which bill it is against and what it is worth are accounts' work, because they hold the ledger. A request starts as Requested and appears on accounts' list of credit notes to issue. The form used to ask for the bill mid-call, three fields deep behind a radio button, with the customer waiting. It produced either the wrong bill or no request at all. Asking only for the yes means every request made is recorded, and the person who knows the ledger fills in the rest. An amount without a request is refused. If a credit-note amount arrives on a complaint with no request, the save is refused: There is a credit note amount but no credit note request. A figure sitting on a complaint nobody asked a credit note for would read as an approved amount to whoever opened it next. Issuing or refusing the credit note is the accounts desk's decision (see the capabilities below). The complaint's drawer shows where the request has got to, the amount and the reference once issued.

search.heading: Statuses and history
search.text: - Moving an open complaint along — to In progress, or Awaiting customer — is anybody's who works that customer. - Finishing one (resolved, closed, rejected) or re-opening a finished one needs the right to resolve complaints. Otherwise it would be the same decision through a side door. - Resolving requires a note. The resolution note is what the customer record shows afterwards. A complaint closed with nothing written explains nothing to the next person who rings. - "Customer told" is recorded separately. Resolving a complaint and telling the customer are two different things; the screen counts how many resolved complaints the customer actually heard about. Every change — raised, raised again on a call, reassigned, priority changed, resolved — is a line in the complaint's status history , with who and when. Nothing is edited or deleted.

search.heading: Who can see and do what
search.text: Action Who See the Complaints screen Anybody holding the module See a complaint Anybody whose book (or team) the customer is in Raise a complaint Any CRM user Change priority, reassign Anybody who can work the customer Resolve, close, reject or re-open Holders of complaint.resolve — managers Issue or refuse a credit note Holders of creditnote.issue — the accounts desk

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Four writers, not one. The complaint writer describes itself as "the one way it is done", but the call path, the collections "dispute" path and the handset each insert complaints themselves. They agree on the essentials today; they can drift. - A complaint raised on a call cannot be given a priority. It always takes the default, though the dialog on the Complaints screen asks. - Reassign offers five desks; routing writes seven. The Reassign list (Operations, Accounts, Dispatch, Quality, Management) has no Technical, Sales or Logistics — the desks the call panel routes to — and no Quality desk is ever routed to. - Reassign is offered on a resolved complaint, and re-opens it. For somebody holding complaint.resolve , reassigning a resolved complaint moves it back to In progress. - Awaiting customer, Closed and Rejected cannot be set from any CRM screen. Only Resolve and Reassign are offered. - The deadline checks look at "resolved at", not the status. A complaint moved to Closed or Rejected by any other route would still read as breached and still escalate. - Every manager and admin is notified of every breach , whatever their team. - Raising from the Complaints dialog does not check the customer is in your book. The search narrows who you can pick; the save does not check again. - Large photographs. Photographs travel with the form's save, which has a 1 MB body limit by default; a phone photograph over that may fail to arrive with no clear message. - The record's "open complaint" alert treats a Closed or Rejected complaint as still open.

The record is src/app/crm/customers/[id] , a server page assembling a dozen reads into RecordScreen .

Customers is the list of every account we invoice or deliver to in your book, with the figures you need mid-call, and the door to each customer's record — one page with everything about them: who they are, who looks after them, what they buy, what they owe, and every call, order, bill and message. Leads are not on this list. A lead is an account that has never ordered, and it is worked in Lead Management.

search.heading: The list at a glance
search.text: The customers list, filtered to one salesperson. Customers Export Import CSV Transfer sales manager Customers. 412 Direct customers. 360 Third-party customers. 52 Outstanding. ₹9.4L Slow payers. 14 With open complaints. 6

search.heading: Three kinds of account
search.text: Type Means Direct customer We sell to them and we invoice them. Third-party customer A shop we deliver to but do not bill — a distributor buys the goods and sells them on. Never asked for a first order on the Call Log. Lead Has never ordered. Not on this list; open it from Lead Management. The type filter also offers two working lists: Delivered to on another's bill — accounts the order sheet shows receiving goods somebody else was invoiced for, whether or not anybody has converted them yet — and Third party, nobody billing , which should be empty.

search.heading: Status words
search.text: Status Means Active Buying New Has never ordered Slow payer Has paid several bills well past their due date recently Inactive Has gone well past their own buying cycle without an order Deactivated Closed deliberately by a manager

search.heading: The customer record
search.text: A customer record. Customer A Active Phone Reminder Complaint WhatsApp Log a call Outstanding. ₹42,300 · See all bills → Last order. 8 Aug Pays on average. 34 days Next call. 20 Aug · Scheduled Activity. All 1,204 Call 310 Order 280 Bill 290 Payment 300 Buying pattern · Account managers · Details. Buying cycle 30 days · Order expected 7 Sep Sales: Telecaller A · Sales manager: Manager A · Back office: Clerk A · Relationship: Not handed over GSTIN · Credit terms · Billed by Every panel on the record is the same height and scrolls inside itself, so the bills, payments and account managers are always on the first screen, however long the customer's history is.

search.heading: Changing who looks after an account
search.text: Tick the accounts, or open one record. On the list, tick rows and press Update account manager . On a record, use the Account managers card. Pick the new sales and/or back-office person. Leave a seat untouched to keep it as it is. Unassigned empties it. Say why. Pick a reason from the list. It is kept with the change. Save. Both the person who gains the accounts and the person who loses them are told — once each, not once per account. Moving the sales or back-office seat is an accounts or admin action, because it moves whose numbers the account counts towards. The sales manager — who the salesperson answers to — can be set by a CRM manager.

search.heading: Moving a whole book of sales managers
search.text: When somebody leaves, filter the list to everything they managed, press Transfer sales manager , pick the new person and confirm. The accounts that move are exactly the accounts the filters match. If the count changed between your review and the save — say an import landed — it stops and asks you to look again. With no filters at all it says, in red, that this is the whole book.

search.heading: Converting a shop to third party
search.text: From the row menu or the record: Convert to third-party customer , then name the distributor who bills them. A shop cannot be marked third party without somebody billing it. No longer a third-party customer undoes it and keeps the record of who used to bill them. An account we invoice ourselves cannot be converted.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Where are the leads?. In Lead Management. The customers list is accounts we invoice or deliver to. Why is the Update account manager button greyed out?. Moving the sales or back-office seat is an accounts or admin action. The button says so when you hover it. I changed the salesperson and the old name came back.. A change made here is marked as a decision and the sheet sync keeps its hands off it. If the old name came back, check whether the change saved — the history on the record lists every move. Export only gave me 25 customers.. Export writes the rows on the page you are looking at. Raise the page size, or ask accounts for a full extract. Next call is blank for most customers.. It shows what the last call said would happen next. A customer nobody has called yet has nothing to show. Why does the Activity tab say 1,204 but show ten?. The counts are the whole history; the list loads ten at a time so the page stays fast. Press Load older , or pick a kind.

The customer table is the centre of MahekOne: every app reads the same customers rows. This tab explains the rules the CRM's customer list and record follow — which accounts are on the list, what each kind of account means, who may move an account between people and why that is narrower than it looks, and why a record is the same height however old the account is.

search.heading: Which accounts are on the list
search.text: A lead is not on the customer table. The list, its tiles, its total and both bulk actions are narrowed to accounts that are not leads , and to accounts not in the lead trash. It is not a filter anybody can switch off. A lead's record is still reachable from Lead Management. Leads were most of the rows — more than half the real book — and were worked from a screen that offered none of the controls for working them. Enforced in one place, a bulk "Transfer sales manager" over a filtered list cannot move thousands of leads nobody saw on the screen they pressed it from.

search.heading: What an account is
search.text: Type Decided by Means Direct customer kind = customer and not marked We sell to them and invoice them Third-party customer The third-party mark — wins over the kind A shop we deliver to; a distributor bills it Lead kind = lead Has never ordered The mark wins over the kind, on a list. A third-party customer is still a lead or a customer underneath — that is what lets us bill one when it starts ordering — but "Lead · Third party" is two facts fighting over one glance. The list says how the account is worked; the record says the kind underneath. A lead becomes a customer at its first order. kind flips when the first order is taken, and about thirty parts of the product read it that way. The lead funnel's own "customer" rung is a separate statement about the relationship.

search.heading: Third-party customers and who bills them
search.text: The mark and the distributor are written together. Converting a shop names at least one distributor in the same save. A shop with the mark and nobody billing it is not a state the screen can create; the Third party, nobody billing filter exists for accounts converted before that was true, and should be empty. - Only a lead is converted. An account we invoice cannot be said not to bill with us; the option is absent and the server refuses it. - A distributor must be an unmarked direct customer — somebody has to hold the invoice. - A shop may have several distributors , one marked primary. The last one cannot be removed from a marked account. - Reverting keeps the links — who used to bill a shop is a fact about it. - A marked account is never prospected on the Call Log. Its own orders, debts and promises still reach it.

search.heading: The seats on an account
search.text: Seat Answers Moves numbers? Who may move it Sales Whose book the account is in, and who is credited with its orders Yes Accounts and admin ( customer.reassign ) Back office Who handles dispatch, billing and paperwork Sees the account; credited only where there is no salesperson Accounts and admin ( customer.reassign ) Sales manager Who the salesperson answers to No CRM managers ( customer.assignSalesManager ) Relationship Who runs the relationship after a lead converts No — sight only Managers ( customer.handOver ) Lead owner Whose lead it is, before the first order Yes, for a lead Lead Management Why moving the sales seat is narrower than a manager. Whose book an account is in decides who is credited for its orders and whose target it counts toward. A manager reassigning accounts would be moving numbers between their own people, including themselves — the same conflict that keeps order approval off managers. The sales-manager and relationship seats move no rupee, which is exactly why a manager can set them.

search.heading: A reassignment is a decision, and it is kept
search.text: Moving the sales seat. - Why is a column, not a sentence. Each move stores a reason code from , the from and to (with names, so the history reads after a person leaves), and who did it. - The sheet keeps its hands off. A decided account is skipped by the order sheet's party projection and by the nightly rebuild of salesperson names; a disagreement is written down as a sync conflict instead of silently restated. - Untouched seats are not sent. Changing only the back-office person does not stamp a decision on the sales seat. - An emptied seat means nobody — not whoever ran the import. - A change that changes nothing notifies nobody.

search.heading: Moving a sales manager by filter
search.text: The question this seat answers is asked hardest on the day somebody leaves, and the answer is "everything they had" — far more accounts than anybody would tick by hand. So Transfer sales manager sends the filters , and the server runs the same clause the list ran. The count on the screen is sent too, and the save refuses if it no longer matches. A tick-list is reviewed row by row; a filtered move is reviewed as the count, the destination and the filters said back in words.

search.heading: The customer record
search.text: A record is a fixed-length page. Every panel is the same height and scrolls inside itself, and every read behind it is capped — the timeline at ten entries a page, messages at fifty, the rest at two hundred. The accounts with the most history are the ones somebody most needs to read before ringing, and they used to be the ones whose orders and bills sat a hundred screens below the fold. A capped list says what it is a slice of. The timeline's pills are counted in the database over the whole history. Load older pages backwards by a cursor on (time, id) — never by an offset, so an entry never appears twice or not at all — and picking a kind asks the server for that kind's newest page rather than filtering what the browser happens to hold. The record shows the next call as it stands today , worked out live — compare with Call History, which shows what each call said at the time.

search.heading: Health and status words
search.text: Word From Deactivated A manager closed the account — the one status no rule writes Inactive The customer has gone × their own buying cycle without an order New Never ordered Slow payer The slow-payer flag (see Payment Follow-up) Active None of the above Inactive outranks slow payer on the list; the record still shows both.

search.heading: Importing customers
search.text: Import CSV brings customers in from a spreadsheet. Re-importing the same sheet updates rows it already knows rather than duplicating them. Rows with no telecaller named go to the owner you pick. It needs sheet.import .

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Export writes only the page on screen , and is allowed for any CRM manager rather than for the right to export customers. Elsewhere in the CRM, exports write the whole filtered set. - The Import CSV link is drawn for every CRM manager , but the page needs sheet.import ; a manager without it is sent back to the list. - The record works out its type label itself instead of using the one shared wording; they agree today. - The health score words used elsewhere in MahekOne (strong, watch) are not shown on the CRM's customer list or record; the CRM shows the status words above.

The Dashboard is one server page, src/app/crm/dashboard/page.tsx , that paints its header immediately and streams the figures behind a Suspense boundary. The figures come from three places: rangeActivity / teamRange in lib/queries.ts (both wrapping eodMetricsForRange in eod-service.ts ), today's work from the queue, payment and worklist services, and two private queries in the page file for the manager's red flags.

The Dashboard is the first screen you see. For a telecaller it greets you by name and shows the shape of your day: how far through the Call Log you are, what is waiting for you, your target for the month and whether you can submit your end-of-day report. For a manager it becomes the Team overview : red flags, the team's figures and a table comparing every telecaller. Every number on it opens the records behind it.

Good morning Start calling 1 Work the queue · 28 2 Close reminders · 4 3 Chase payments · 9 4 Clear complaints · 2 5 Submit EOD Today Yesterday This week This month 12 Aug · vs 11 Aug The queue and the list below always show today's work Calling progress. 12/40 Calls connected. 18 Orders taken. 4 Missed calls. 6 Needs you today. search.text: Step Ticked when Opens Work the queue Every customer on today's Call Log has been worked Call Log Close reminders No reminder due today or earlier is still open Reminders Chase payments Nobody is left on the collections worklist Payment Follow-up Clear complaints No complaint is open, in progress or awaiting the customer Complaints Submit EOD Never ticked here — it lights up once the queue is worked and reminders are closed EOD Report

search.heading: What each figure means
search.text: Figure What it counts Note Calling progress Customers on today's Call Log you have worked, out of how many were on it Always today, whatever period you picked Calls connected Calls you made that were answered, out of calls you made. Calls that rang your phone are counted separately underneath. Connect rate is connected ÷ placed. The team's rate is shown beside yours. Orders taken Orders you logged in the period, whether or not accounts have approved them Underneath: how many are still awaiting approval, and the approved value so far Missed calls Calls you made that nobody answered Fewer is better — a fall shows green An order you took counts as taken the moment you save it. Its value only counts once the accounts desk approves it — that is why the line under Orders taken can say "2 awaiting approval".

search.heading: Picking a period
search.text: Pick Today, Yesterday, This week or This month. The buttons sit above your figures. The choice is in the page address, so you can bookmark it. Read what it is compared with. Beside the buttons: the dates covered and what they are measured against — vs 11 Aug for a day, vs the previous 7 days for a span. Remember what does not change. The progress bar, the five steps and Needs you today are always today's work. A month of waiting work is not a thing — only the activity figures follow the period. Period Covers Compared with Today Today The previous working day Yesterday The previous working day (Saturday, on a Monday) The working day before that This week Monday to today The same number of days immediately before This month The 1st to today The same number of days immediately before

search.heading: For managers: the Team overview
search.text: A manager's Team overview, this week. RED FLAGS · 14 missed calls this week, up from 9 · 3 reminders overdue more than 3 days · Overdue balance grew ₹42,000 this week Review collections Team calls this week. 412 · 301 connected Orders booked. ₹8.2L · +12% vs the previous 5 days Outstanding. ₹14L · ₹2.1L over 60 days Team target. 61% Red flag Raised when Missed calls Anybody on the team missed a call in the period. Says whether that is up or down. Reminders overdue A reminder is still open more than days past its date Complaints unresolved A complaint is still open more than days after it was raised Overdue balance grew Bills that fell due in the last seven days are still unpaid

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Why does my Calling progress not change when I pick This month?. The Call Log is today's list. Its progress is always today's, so it has no month to show. The activity figures beside it do follow the period. Yesterday shows Saturday's figures on a Monday.. Yesterday means the previous working day. Sunday is not a working day, so on a Monday it is Saturday. The dates are printed beside the buttons. Orders taken says 5 but the value is lower than I expected.. The value underneath counts only orders accounts have approved. The line above it says how many are still waiting. Why do inbound calls not count towards my connect rate?. You cannot fail to connect a call that rang your own phone. Counting them would push your connect rate up on a day you made fewer calls. They are shown separately. The Missed calls card says 'retry after 4 pm'.. That line is fixed text on the card, not a rule. When to try again is decided by the Call Log's no-answer ladder. Where did the Inactive Watch go?. Customers who have gone quiet are worked from the Call Log now. The Customers gone quiet row opens the Call Log filtered to exactly those customers.

The Dashboard answers two different questions and keeps them apart. What is waiting for me right now? — the day's stages and Needs you today — is always about today, because work waiting is a present-tense thing. How have I been doing? — calls, orders, missed calls, the team table — can be read over a day, a week or a month, and is always compared with an equally long stretch just before it. Every figure is read from the same function the EOD report and the other screens read, so the dashboard and the screen a number opens cannot disagree.

search.heading: One definition of a day's work
search.text: The dashboard and the EOD report share one query. Calls, connects, orders, promises, reminders closed, complaints logged and WhatsApp messages sent are all counted by one function over a window of business days. A single day and a one-day range cannot answer differently, and a month costs the database what a day costs: the span is a wider window on the same twenty-odd counts, not a loop over days. Two copies of those counts is how the dashboard and the EOD report came to disagree about how many calls somebody made. The telecaller submits the EOD report on the same figures they watched all day.

search.heading: What is counted, and what is deliberately not
search.text: Figure Counts Does not count Calls placed Outbound calls Inbound calls, and "Order Received" (an order that arrived without a call) Calls connected Outbound calls with any outcome other than No answer Inbound calls — you cannot fail to connect a call that rang your phone Missed Outbound calls logged No answer — Inbound Calls that rang the telecaller — shown on its own line Orders taken Every order the telecaller logged, except cancelled ones — Orders approved / value Orders accounts approved Orders waiting for approval or declined Queue worked Distinct customers called from the Call Log Calls made from other screens Why inbound is kept out of the connect rate. Counting inbound calls as "placed and connected" moves the connect rate towards 100% on a day the telecaller made fewer calls, not more. Placed and connected are both outbound-only; inbound is counted and shown separately. Taken is not sold. Orders taken is the telecaller's own work and counts from the moment the customer says yes. The value beside it, Orders booked on the team view and the monthly target count approved orders only, because only an approved order is money.

search.heading: The period and its comparison
search.text: From the period button to two windows. Yesterday means the previous working day. The working week is . On a Monday, Yesterday is Saturday, and Today is compared with Saturday rather than with a Sunday of zeroes. The screen prints the dates so nobody has to guess. A span is compared with an equally long span. This week (Monday to today) is compared with the same number of days immediately before; this month (the 1st to today) likewise. Never against a whole previous month. A month-to-date of twelve days beside a full previous month reads as a collapse every time — on the 1st of the month worst of all. An equal span is the only comparison that is fair on every day of the period. The period never runs into the future. Week and month end today. A month-to-date figure beside a whole-month target is a comparison somebody can make; a range that is mostly days that have not happened is not. Where the day boundary sits is o'clock: a call made after midnight but before that hour counts on the previous day, for the dashboard exactly as for every other screen.

search.heading: How a change is drawn
search.text: - Counts move by a number: "+2 vs yesterday". Nothing is drawn when the two periods match, because a change of zero is noise. - Money moves by a percentage: "+12% vs the previous 5 days". A rupee difference is too big a number to read at a glance. Where the earlier period had nothing, the card says so instead of a percentage. - Missed calls are better when they fall, so a fall is drawn green.

search.heading: Needs you today
search.text: These five rows are today's work and do not follow the period: Row Counts Colour Reminders due today Pending reminders due today or overdue, with how many are already overdue Red if any are overdue, otherwise amber Payment follow-ups open Customers on the collections worklist, and the total overdue on it Amber Complaints unresolved Open, in progress or awaiting the customer Red Customers gone quiet Customers the inactivity rule has flagged, and the business at risk Grey Queue still to work Customers on today's Call Log not yet worked Brand The reminders and complaints numbers are the same two the sidebar badges show, read from the same function in the same request — a badge and the dashboard row beside it cannot disagree.

search.heading: The monthly target
search.text: A target is set for a calendar month, so it is read for the month the period ends in , whatever the period. A week's progress against the month's target is the honest reading; a target cut down to the length of the span would be a number nobody set. Working days left are counted on the configured working week.

search.heading: The manager's red flags
search.text: A red flag is something wrong, so the strip only alarms when there is something. Each flag appears only when it is raised. A clean day reads All clear — Nothing overdue, unresolved or growing. in plain colours, rather than a yellow band of red zeros. The strip used to draw every figure in warning colours with a red zero in front of each. An alarm that fires on every good day is one people learn to skim — and then it fires on a bad one and gets skimmed too. Flag Threshold Reminders overdue More than days past their date Complaints unresolved Raised more than days ago and still open Missed calls Any, with the change against the comparison period Overdue balance grew Only growth is a flag; a shrinking balance is the opposite and is not drawn

search.heading: The comparison table
search.text: One row per person on the manager's team, over the same period. Overdue reminders are counted as at the end of the period, never summed: a reminder overdue on Monday and still overdue on Friday is one overdue reminder. Connect rates are always computed from summed calls, never averaged, so somebody who made four calls does not weigh the same as somebody who made ninety.

search.heading: Who sees what
search.text: - A telecaller sees their own figures, with the team's connect rate beside theirs for comparison. - A CRM manager on team scope sees the Team overview. Switching to My book shows their own day in the telecaller layout.

search.heading: Every setting that shapes the Dashboard
Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - "Orders approved" and the value leave out delivered goods. The dashboard's counts list three approved statuses by hand; the product's one list of "statuses that count as a sale" also includes in transit and delivered . An order that has been marked delivered stops counting towards the dashboard's value and the monthly target. - "Collected" on the team table counts payments that were only reported. It adds up every payment line recorded by the person, including money still waiting for accounts and money accounts rejected. Every other money figure counts confirmed receipts only. - The target achieved is counted against the account owner , not against whose book the account is in. - "Overdue balance grew" always covers the last seven days and the Outstanding card's "over 60 days" figure is company-wide, whatever period or scope is chosen; both include bills the system treats as not stated. - Red-in-the-table thresholds are fixed numbers — overdue reminders above 3 and missed calls above 5 — not settings, and the Missed calls card's "retry after 4 pm" is fixed text. - The complaints flag and "overdue grew" read the account owner rather than whose book the account is in.

Submitting is one action that re-checks the reminder gate and upserts eod reports ; a nightly step writes reports for anybody who did not. The same metrics function feeds the Dashboard, which is where the span-before comparison lives. Everything below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

The EOD Report is your day in figures — calls, orders, payments, reminders, WhatsApp — worked out from what you logged, plus a ready-made message to paste into the team's WhatsApp group. At the end of the day you submit it. You can also look back at yesterday, the last seven days, this month, last month or any range you choose. A manager additionally sees the whole team side by side. Nothing on this screen is typed in. Every figure is derived from the calls, orders, payments and reminders you recorded — so a thin report means thin logging, not a thin day.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: EOD report — today, before submitting. EOD report Due today. 2 reminders due today are still open. Close or carry them forward before finalising. Customer A — call after stock-take · Customer B — confirm cheque date Today's numbers. WhatsApp message. Copy Submit EOD

search.heading: Submitting at the end of the day
search.text: Clear the reminders due today. Each one must be called, carried forward to another day, or closed. Until then the button reads Close or carry forward the reminders due today first . Read the figures. If something looks low, check that every call was logged — the report can only count what is recorded. Copy the WhatsApp message. Press Copy and paste it into the team group. The message is built for WhatsApp: short lines, no tables. Press Submit EOD. The report is saved with the time. If you submit again later the same day it replaces the earlier one ( Resubmit EOD ). If you forget, a report is generated for you overnight — a day with no activity still produces a report, so nobody has to wonder whether you worked.

search.heading: What each figure means
search.text: Figure What it counts Customers called from the queue Different customers you called from your Call Log. Calls attempted Outbound calls you logged. Inbound calls and orders logged without a call are not counted here. Connected Outbound calls with any outcome other than no answer. Inbound received Calls the customer made to you. Missed Outbound calls logged as no answer. Orders Orders you took (not cancelled), how many accounts approved, and the approved value. Orders received without a call Orders you logged with no call behind them — real work, kept separate. Payment follow-ups Follow-up attempts you made on money owed. Promises obtained Payment promises you got, and their total. Payments confirmed Payment amounts you recorded, by the payment date. Reminders closed / created / carried forward Your reminders that were completed, the ones you created, and the ones moved to a later day. Complaints logged Complaints you raised. WhatsApp sent Messages confirmed as sent. A message copied and never confirmed does not count. Monthly target Approved order value this month against the customer targets on accounts you own.

search.heading: The team roll-up
search.text: A manager sees a table of the team for the same period — calls, connected, missed, orders, order value and target % per person — and on today's view a Team roll-up message to copy. Somebody who has not logged anything still appears.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I made 40 calls but it says 32 attempted.. Only outbound calls you logged count. Inbound calls are counted separately, and orders received without a call are on their own line. My orders show a value of zero.. Value is counted only once accounts approve an order. The orders you took are still counted. Why can I not submit?. A reminder due today is still open. Call the customer, carry it forward, or close it. Can I submit for yesterday?. No — only today is submitted. Other periods are a historical view. Yesterday's report was generated overnight if you did not submit it. Does the EOD compare me with last week?. No. The comparison with the period before is on the Dashboard, which reads the same figures.

The EOD Report exists so that a telecaller's day is reported from what they recorded , not from what they remember at six o'clock — and so that the report reaches the team in the one place they already read, WhatsApp. This tab explains how a span of days is measured, what each figure counts and deliberately does not, the gate on submitting, and what happens to a day nobody submitted. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: A span of days is one window, not a loop over days
search.text: Every figure — for today, yesterday, the last seven days, this month, last month or a custom range — comes from one function that runs the same twenty-odd counts over a wider window. A day is simply a range of one. Two copies of twenty counts is how the Dashboard and the EOD report come to disagree about how many calls somebody made. One function means a day and a one-day range cannot answer differently, and a month costs what a day costs. Period Span Today Today — the live report, the only one you submit Yesterday The previous working day, so Monday reads Saturday rather than a Sunday of zeroes Last 7 days Today and the six days before This month The 1st up to today — never to a future end date Last month The whole previous month Custom range Any from–to; typed backwards, it is swapped rather than refused An unrecognised period in the address reads as today rather than as a broken page. Where the working day starts. The day runs on Asia/Kolkata, starting at :00. Every window is two instants with the zone named, so a 9am call can never fall outside "today" because a database connection happened to be set to another zone.

search.heading: The comparison with the span before
search.text: The EOD Report itself shows no comparison. The Dashboard reads the same figures and measures a span against the equally long span immediately before it — never against a whole previous month, because a twelve-day month-to-date beside a full month reads as a collapse every time. A single day is compared with the previous working day. See the Dashboard.

search.heading: What each figure counts — and what it refuses to
search.text: Calls attempted and connected are outbound only. An order logged with no call is not a call: counting it would inflate attempts, the connect rate and every per-call conversion. An inbound call is not an attempt either — you cannot fail to connect a call that rang your own phone, so counting it would push the connect rate towards 100% on a day you made fewer calls. Inbound and order-without-a-call are counted on their own lines. - Missed reads the call's outcome (no answer), not the retired connection-status field — reading that would quietly make the number zero. - Customers called from the queue is distinct customers called from the Call Log. It is deliberately not "x of y": the denominator can only be had by building the queue, and a second, cheaper count once produced "3 of 8" against the Call Log's "3 of 4". Two questions about the same orders. Orders taken — the telecaller's own work, true the moment the customer said yes; cancelled orders excluded. Orders approved — the sale, and the only figure that carries a value . The report says both, because a day's work reported as nothing because accounts have not reached it yet is the telecaller's own record being wrong. - Boxes and loose cans are worked out per line from that product's own pack; a product name the catalogue does not recognise contributes nothing. - WhatsApp sent counts messages confirmed as sent. Copied is not sent. - Monthly target is the approved order value this month against the sum of customer targets on the accounts the person owns.

search.heading: The gate on submitting
search.text: Reminders due today block finalising. A report cannot be submitted while reminders due today are still open. Each must be called, carried forward, or closed (closing needs the reminder-close permission). The gate is enforced on the server, not only by a disabled button. A reminder is a promise to a customer. The end of the day is the last moment it can still be kept or honestly moved; a report that could be finalised over it would close the day on a broken promise nobody had to look at. The gate and the "submitted" banner are always about the real today , whatever period is on screen — browsing the last seven days does not change which reminders block the next submission.

search.heading: Submitted, resubmitted, or generated
search.text: State How it happens Submitted Submit EOD saves the message and the figures with the time. Resubmitted Submitting again the same day replaces the earlier report. Auto-generated The nightly job writes a report for every active person who did not submit, for the day just ended. It never overwrites a report that exists. A zero-activity day must still produce a report. Absence must never be ambiguous — "no report" could mean a day off, a forgotten button or a broken screen, and nobody can tell which.

search.heading: The WhatsApp message
search.text: The message is built to paste: short lines, a few symbols, no tables, nothing that renders badly on a phone. It carries order calls, orders (with boxes and cans), no-answers, no-order reasons, payment calls and payment WhatsApps against the payment list, assigned and called from the day's settled Call Log, who promised to pay and when, and the month against target. All high priority customers called! appears only when there was a queue to clear and nothing high-priority is left.

search.heading: The team roll-up
search.text: A manager in the CRM with the team-report permission sees every active person in their scope for the same period, with a team message on today's view. Both conditions are required — a telecaller who is a manager in some other app is not drawn a "team" here.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Approved orders are counted with a typed list of three statuses. AGENTS.md says every "did we sell anything" read derives from PURCHASE STATUSES , which now also includes in transit and delivered ; the EOD counts ('captured','confirmed','dispatched') only, so an approved order that has been marked in transit or delivered drops out of EOD value and the monthly target line ( lib/services/eod-service.ts eodMetricsForRange ). - "Payments confirmed" is not confirmed money. It sums payment lines the person recorded, by payment date, without checking the receipt was confirmed by accounts — a telecaller's reported payment counts ( eod-service.ts , payments confirmed ). - The target line uses the account owner , not whose book the account is in or who is credited with it ( eod-service.ts , target amount and target achieved join on owner id ). - Order value is the order's total amount , while targets and performance use the net-of-GST value ( eod-service.ts vs orderValueSql ). - "Order Calls" in the WhatsApp message is attempted calls over pending queue , two numbers from different populations ( lib/engines/eod.ts aggregateEod ). - The overnight report is for the previous calendar day , not the previous working day, and is written for every active user, not only CRM users ( lib/jobs.ts auto-eod step; autoGenerateEodReports ).

The Help Center is where the CRM's SOPs and call scripts live — search it mid-call for "payment" or "short supply" and read the answer. Manager settings are the numbers and switches that decide how the CRM behaves: when a customer comes back to the Call Log, when a debt escalates, how targets default. They are changed in the Admin Console , under Telecaller CRM , by a manager of the CRM.

search.heading: Call scripts
search.text: A call script is a help article written to be read aloud. The same scripts appear in the call panel when you ring somebody from the Call Log — the panel picks the one that fits. Words in braces are placeholders. In the call panel, the CRM fills in the ones it knows for the customer you are calling, and leaves the rest in braces for you to say in your own words: Placeholder Filled with {contact name} The contact person on the account {customer} , {customer name} The shop's name {city} Their town {your name} , {my name} Your name {outstanding} , {outstanding amount} What they owe {last order date} , {last order value} Their last order {bill number} , {bill no} , {invoice number} The bill being chased {amount} , {bill amount} , {due date} , {days overdue} That bill's balance, due date and lateness A filled-in placeholder reads as part of the sentence; one still in braces is highlighted so you never say "bill number" out loud by accident. In the Help Center itself, placeholders are shown as written.

search.heading: Manager settings
search.text: Open the Admin Console. From the app launcher, open Admin Console , then Settings → Telecaller CRM . The old address /crm/settings takes you there. Pick a tab. Call queue , Collections , Targets & cycles , Interactions , Products , WhatsApp , Reminders and Complaints . Each setting shows what it does, its current value and its shipped default. Change values. Edit as many as you need on the tab. Anything that does not fit with another setting is flagged before you can save — Fix the flagged relationships first . Review this change set. You see every change, old and new, and which worklists it alters tomorrow. Confirm to apply. It takes effect at once, and can be undone in one action from the save bar. If you see You can see these settings but not change them , you hold the CRM but not as a manager, or the setting is one only a platform administrator may change.

search.heading: The lead funnel, workday and voice
search.text: The lead funnel's gates and reason lists are on Settings → Lead funnel ; the working day, attachments and sign-in on Platform ; dictation on Voice & AI . A CRM manager can change the lead funnel page too.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I cannot find the Settings page in the CRM.. It moved to the Admin Console. The old address forwards there. I changed a setting. When does it take effect?. Immediately — the CRM reads settings fresh at least every 30 seconds. Some (the Call Log's) change tomorrow's list, because today's is already settled; the review step says which. Can I write a new help article?. Not from a screen yet. Ask whoever maintains the CRM. Why does a script still show a placeholder in braces?. The CRM does not know that value for this customer — say it in your own words.

Two rules hold the CRM's behaviour together. Nothing business-critical is a constant : every threshold a manager might one day want to change is a setting, stored in the database, read through one cached function, and changed from a screen. There is one place to change it : the Admin Console's settings pages, which validate, check the whole configuration for consistency, and audit every change. The Help Center sits beside them as the one place SOPs and call scripts are written. Every table on this page shows the value in force now, its shipped default, and who last changed it.

search.heading: How a setting reaches the screen
search.text: A setting, from the console to the Call Log. A section is saved as one change set. Related settings — three escalation thresholds, a set of aging buckets — are saved together or not at all. Half-applying them would leave the system briefly describing a policy nobody agreed to. Consistency is checked across the whole configuration. Some settings are two statements of one fact: the collections quiet window and the stage-2 threshold, the aging buckets and the escalation stages, the six performance weights and the number 100. A change that introduces a contradiction is refused with the relationship named. A contradiction that was already there does not block a save — refusing would trap whoever is fixing one half of it. A wrong setting is worse than a wrong row: it is read by every engine on every request. Reading every value through one 30-second cache means a change lands everywhere at once, and an audit row with before and after means "why does the Call Log do that" always has an answer with a name and a date on it.

search.heading: Who may change what
search.text: config.write, and a standing in the app the setting belongs to. Changing a setting needs the configuration permission (managers hold it) and manager or admin level in an app that owns that settings page. A CRM manager changes the Telecaller CRM and Lead funnel pages; the Platform page — sign-in, the working day, attachments — is the platform administrator's alone, as is any setting marked admin-only. A setting that sits on no page cannot be changed by id at all. The permission is held at manager level in several apps. Without the second check, a manager of the Sales Dashboard could post a change to the CRM's collections thresholds by URL, though the console would never have drawn them that page. The write now asks the same question the console asks before drawing it. A platform administrator's write also passes the console's password re-check, which is off unless is set above zero. /crm/settings permanently redirects to the console. The module that guards it still exists.

What it cannot fill stays in braces and is highlighted, because am I speaking to {contact name}? read aloud is a stumble the system could have prevented, and dressing a real name and a placeholder alike is how somebody says "bill number" on a live call. - Audience. Call History is every call logged in your book, newest first, with what happened on it, what it produced, and what the screen told the telecaller would happen next . Use it to look back over a week, to see what a colleague said to a customer before you ring them, and to hand a customer over to somebody else.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: Call History, last 7 days. Call history Export Calls today. 24 Connected. 18 · 75% rate Missed. 6 Messages sent today. 9 Interactions in view. 132 Handover summary - Customer A. Everything someone else needs to pick up this customer Copy 132 interactions

search.heading: Reading the Next call column
search.text: Every call saved since this column existed carries the answer the telecaller saw in the window after saving: Comes back to your Call Log on … . The column shows that answer, as it was on that day . What you see It means A date in black, Promised A callback the customer asked for. Somebody owes them this call. A date in black, Scheduled The date the rules gave on that day. It moves if the customer orders, pays or asks for a callback. A date in grey The date has passed. It was what the screen said then, not a commitment now. Needs a decision Nobody could reach them — no date was given, and somebody has to decide what happens next. Nothing scheduled Marked do not contact, or nothing would bring them back within four months. - The call was logged before this was recorded. Nothing is filled in after the fact. To see when a customer actually comes back today, open their record or the Customers list. Call History shows what was said at the time — the difference between the two is the record of what changed.

search.heading: Looking something up
search.text: Pick a date range. Today, Last 7 days, This month or All time. Last 7 days is where the screen opens. Narrow it. Type a customer name or a word from a note. Managers can pick one telecaller from Everyone . Open the details. Where a call recorded why the customer rang, who rang and what was agreed, hover the details summary to read every answer. Open the customer. The customer's name opens their record. All time is not all time. The screen loads the newest 400 calls in your book and filters those. When it is holding a full 400 it says so — 132 of the newest 400 calls — and All time reaches back only as far as those 400 go. For older history, open the customer's record, whose timeline pages back to the beginning.

search.heading: Handing a customer over
search.text: Pick the customer in the Handover summary card. The list is the customers in the calls you are looking at. Press Copy. You get a short message: the customer's name, their last three interactions with date, channel, outcome and note, the last thing promised, and every open reminder with its due date. Paste it to your colleague. In WhatsApp, an email or the customer's notes.

search.heading: What the other columns mean
search.text: Column What it shows Timestamp When the call was logged Telecaller Who logged it Channel Call Status Left blank on calls logged today — the outcome says whether they answered Outcome How the call ended: Order Taken, No Order, No Answer, Payment Promised… Notes What the telecaller wrote. Hover for the whole note. Produced What the call created: Order, Reminder, Complaint

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Why are my WhatsApp messages not here?. Despite the subtitle, this screen lists calls only. Sent WhatsApp messages are on the WhatsApp screen's Message log, and on the customer's record. The Next call date is in the past and greyed out.. That is the date the telecaller was given when they saved the call. It has passed; the customer's real next call is on their record. Why can I not export?. Exporting needs the right to export customers, which a manager decides on the Access screen. I am a manager and I only see my own calls.. Switch the header to Team . On My book you see only your own.

Call History is a read of the calls ledger: every interaction a person logged, in your book, newest first. It writes nothing. Its one unusual column — Next call — is not worked out when you open the screen. It is the sentence the telecaller was shown when they saved the call, stored on that call and never changed afterwards.

search.heading: What a row is
search.text: Every save that logs a conversation writes one row in the call ledger: Path What it writes The call panel (Call Log, customer record, any screen that opens it) One row per save, with the interaction type, outcome, notes and what it produced The collections follow-up panel One row per collections call, marked as coming from Payment Follow-up Order Received on the call panel A row for an order that arrived with no call — counted as an order, never as a call placed The list is the newest 400 of those rows in your book. A telecaller's book is the calls they logged; a manager on team scope sees the calls logged by their team. Why a cap at all. A full history in one page is megabytes of HTML for a list nobody scrolls. The screen says plainly when it is holding a full page — 132 of the newest 400 calls — rather than presenting the cap as the history. Older calls are on each customer's record, whose timeline pages back with a cursor.

search.heading: The stored next step
search.text: Where the Next call column comes from. What the telecaller was told is a record, not a cache. The six next-step columns answer what did we tell the person who logged this call, on the day they logged it . A cache answers when is the next call now , and is rebuilt when the answer changes. Rebuilding these would not correct the question — it would destroy it. The current next step is worked out live on the customer's record; the two are meant to be able to differ, and the difference is the record of what changed since. A past date is drawn muted. A stored date that is before today is drawn grey, with the day it was said on hover. It was true when it was said; it is not a promise now, and sitting in a column of future dates it would read like one. No date is invented. Needs a decision (nobody can reach them) and Nothing scheduled (do not contact, or nothing within the horizon) carry no date by design and print their word instead. Calls logged before these columns existed show "-": nothing reconstructs a sentence for them, because a reconstruction would be today's answer wearing an old call's date. Working it out never fails the save. The call is in the ledger before the next step is asked for. If working it out fails, the columns stay empty and the window after saving says it could not work it out — the call itself is never lost. The same component draws the Next call cell on the Customers list, where it shows the latest call's answer for each customer. Kind Badge Has a date booked Promised Yes — a callback the customer asked for scheduled Scheduled Yes — the date the rules gave decide Needs a decision No none Nothing scheduled No

search.heading: The figures across the top
search.text: The four activity cards are today's figures, from the same function the Dashboard and the EOD report use: calls placed (outbound only), connected, missed, and WhatsApp messages confirmed sent. For a manager on team scope they are the team's. The fifth card counts the rows the filters are showing.

search.text: All filtering happens in the browser over the rows already loaded. Filter Matches Search Customer name, note text and outcome Channel All channels, Call, WhatsApp, Visit Who The telecaller's name (managers) Range Today, Last 7 days, This month, All time

search.heading: The handover summary
search.text: For any customer in the loaded calls, the card builds a message from three things: the last three interactions in the loaded rows, the most recent note as Last thing promised , and every pending reminder for that customer as Open commitments . Copy puts it on the clipboard; nothing is sent or saved.

search.heading: Exporting
search.text: Export needs the customer.export capability, checked on the screen. The file is built in the browser from what the filters are showing and says how many rows it holds against how many were loaded.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - The subtitle says "Calls and WhatsApp messages in one stream"; only calls are listed. Every row's channel is Call , so the WhatsApp and Visit channel filters always show nothing. - The Status column is always blank for current calls. It reads a connection status that nothing writes any more, and compares it with capitalised words the stored values never use. Whether a call connected is in the Outcome. - The date filters are rolling, not business days. Today is the last 24 hours and This month is the last 31 days, measured from when the page was rendered — not the business day and not the calendar month every other CRM screen means. - "Last thing promised" is the newest note, whatever it says, not a promise. - The person filter matches by name , so two people with the same name are one filter. - Export is checked only on the screen. The CSV is built in the browser, so there is no server check of customer.export . - Missed above five is drawn red by a fixed number, not a setting.

Two modules share this page. Next actions & nurture ( ) is reads over four customers columns plus a pure engine that turns events into mbos tasks rows keyed for idempotency. Handovers ( ) writes one seat — relationship owner id — with its history and timeline in one transaction. Everything below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A new nurture row is a row in NURTURE SEQUENCE. Add a trigger to NurtureTrigger if needed, then make sure something raises it — an action calling raiseNurtureTasks and an event query in runNurturePass . A row nothing raises is a promise nothing keeps. Never put a moving value in the key. Not the due date, not the title. Changing either would re-raise every outstanding task. Do not let the relationship seat leak into ASSIGNED TO SQL. That expression credits revenue. Reading the handover seat there would move money between people as a side effect of naming a relationship manager. Handover refusals are pure. Add a refusal to handoverRefusal and HANDOVER REFUSALS so the screen's disabled button and the action say the same thing.
