Every active lead should owe somebody something: what happens next, on which day, who does it, and what they should come back with . The Next actions & nurture desk shows those promises across the whole book — what is due, what is late, what nobody has promised at all — and the follow-up tasks the system raises on its own. Handovers is where a lead that has become a customer is given to the person who will run the relationship from now on. Numbers on this page are your CRM's current settings.

search.heading: Next actions & nurture: the six tabs
search.text: Tab What it lists Due Next actions falling due today, and who owes each one. Overdue Next actions past their day with nobody having said anything since. Nothing scheduled Active leads with no next action at all — the thing this desk exists to stop. On hold Parked leads, the day each comes back, and how far past that day it is. Nurture The follow-up tasks the system raised, split by whose they are — the lead manager's or the salesman's. Communication Every brochure, profile, price list and call recorded against leads, across the book.

search.heading: The Due tab at a glance
search.text: Next actions — due today. Owed today. 11 People holding one. 4 Missing an answer. 2

search.heading: Setting a next action
search.text: Press Set the next action. On the row here, or on the lead's own record. Give all four answers. What happens next, which day and who will do it are required; the person must be able to sign in. What they should come back with is optional but worth writing. If somebody else owes it, they are told. Save. The lead drops off Nothing scheduled and appears on Due on that day. Moving a lead up its ladder also asks for a next action while the rule is on ( ), so most are set as part of a move. Answer Example The action Ring the works manager about the trial The day A date, never "soon" Who A person who can sign in What they come back with (optional) Whether the trial ran, and the result

search.heading: Nurture tasks
search.text: When something happens on a lead, the system puts a dated task on somebody's list. You do not raise these yourself; you do them, and close them from your task list. When After Whose Task Lead becomes a Prospect same day Lead manager Check the customer and the salesman Lead becomes a Prospect same day Salesman Get and check GST A salesman visits 1 day Lead manager Check call after the visit Lead becomes a Prospect 2 days Lead manager Send the company profile Lead becomes a Prospect 4 days Lead manager Send the product brochure and video A sample is asked for same day Lead manager Check the sample request A sample is dispatched 2 days Lead manager Check it is moving The shop confirms the sample first day of the review ladder Lead manager Sample review call The sample is approved same day Lead manager Call about the order Lead reaches Negotiation 3 days Lead manager Follow up the negotiation Their expected order date that day Lead manager Ask for the first order An order arrives 1 day Lead manager Follow the delivery Delivery completed 2 days Lead manager Satisfaction call A payment falls due that day Lead manager Payment follow-up Their reorder is expected that day Lead manager Repeat-order call A task is only raised if there is somebody to give it to. A lead with no lead manager gets no lead-manager tasks — it shows up on the lists of leads with nobody running them instead. Each task is raised once , however many times the system checks.

search.heading: Communication
search.text: Record what went out to a lead: Call the customer , Send the company profile , Send a product image , Send the brochure , Send the video , Send the price list , Sample follow-up , Negotiation call , Ask for the first order , Payment follow-up , Repeat-order call . Press Record the send (or Log the call ). The entry goes on the lead's timeline. The tab shows the log across the book and which of the eleven are used and which are never used.

search.heading: Handovers
search.text: Handovers — converted accounts nobody runs yet. Handovers Nobody running them. 5 Longest wait. 12 days

search.heading: What a handover changes — and what it does not
search.text: Changes Does not change Who runs the relationship, and the date it changed hands Whose book the account is in Who can see and work the account Who is credited for its orders A history row with the reason, and a timeline entry Anybody's target, collections list or Call Log Both the person taking the account and the person losing it are told — one message each, however many accounts moved.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Why is a lead on Nothing scheduled when it has a follow-up date?. A date is not a next action. It needs what, who and what they should come back with as well. I did not create this nurture task. Where did it come from?. Something happened on the lead — a sample went out, a visit was made, an order date arrived — and the sequence raised it. The task names the lead. Can I hand over a lead?. No. A lead is run by its lead manager until it becomes a customer. The Hand over button explains this. Will handing over an account move its revenue to the new person?. No. Moving revenue is a reassignment, which only accounts and administrators can do.

A lead does not stall because nobody knows what to do next. It stalls because the thing to do next lives in somebody's head, and the head is busy. This desk is built on three rules that move that into the record: every active lead owes somebody something (§24), events raise dated tasks on their own (§13's nurture sequence), and a customer is handed to a named person to run (§Q) — without moving a rupee. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: §24: an active lead may not sit with nothing owed
search.text: A next action is four answers, not a date : the action, the day, the person, and what that person is expected to come back with. A date alone is what the funnel had before, and a date alone is how a lead sits for six weeks with everybody assuming somebody else is holding it. Where the rule bites How Every upward move on a lead with a sales type The gate adds "Say what happens next, on which day, and who will do it" unless the action, day and person are all present. Switched by . Setting a next action directly The action, the day and the person are required, and the person must have an active account. The expected outcome is optional — a call that has not happened does not always have a stated objective, and demanding one produces a box people type a full stop into. Closing a lead as lost The next action is cleared — a closed lead owes nobody anything — and its open follow-up tasks are cancelled. Legacy leads (no sales type) Exempt. Demanding a next action to move a four-year-old lead would freeze the book the rule exists to unstick. When the next action is owed by somebody other than the person setting it, they are notified — work arriving on a list unasked is otherwise found out by the lead going overdue against their name.

search.heading: The four windows on one column group
search.text: The Due , Overdue and Nothing scheduled tabs are three views of the same four columns, read as stored. None of them decides anything: - Due — a next action dated today. - Overdue — dated before today, with nothing recorded since. - Nothing scheduled — an active lead with no next action, then leads whose action has gone past. On a lead with a sales type this list should be empty; it is not decoration. - On hold — parked leads by the day each returns. A park needs a coded reason from , a return day and a next action.

search.heading: §13: the nurture sequence
search.text: An event happens, and some days later a task with a name and a date appears on somebody's list. The sequence is a table, not fifteen rules scattered through the code — each row names the trigger, the delay, whose task it is and the sentence: Where the nurture rows hang. Raised once, however often it is checked. Each task carries a key built from things that do not move: the trigger, whose task it is, the row's declared delay and the record that caused it. The nightly pass and the action that caused the event both raise through the same function, which reads the keys already held first — so the usual case is that the action raised it seconds ago and the nightly finds nothing to do. A scheduled pass that raised a second copy every time it ran would be worse than one that never ran: forty identical "Sample review call" rows is a list somebody stops opening, and the one real task goes with them. The key deliberately leaves out the due date and the wording — a manager editing the review ladder, or somebody improving a sentence, must not duplicate every outstanding task overnight. - Owner is a role, resolved per lead. "Lead manager" is the lead's lead-manager seat; "salesman" is the account's sales seat, falling back to its owner. A task whose person cannot be resolved is skipped , never given to whoever is handy — the lead shows up on the lists of leads with nobody running them instead. - Missed days catch up. A row comes due when its trigger day plus its delay has arrived, so a pass that did not run for a week raises the week's worth; nothing is raised ahead of its day. - The sample-received row follows the review ladder. Its delay is the first rung of , so it cannot disagree with the review chase. - The repeat-order call is dated by the Call Log's own stock-check day ( % of the customer's measured cycle), and only for accounts that have a lead manager. - Answers close tasks. Confirming a sample's receipt closes the transit chases; recording a verdict closes the review chases; losing a lead cancels its nurture tasks. Closed tasks keep their record. The pass runs once a night; its longest delay is four days, so an hourly pass would re-derive the same events twenty-four times to raise nothing.

search.heading: §14: communication actions
search.text: Eleven company-communication actions — calling, the company profile, a product image, the brochure, the video, the price list, a sample follow-up, a negotiation call, asking for the first order, a payment follow-up and a repeat-order call — are recorded against the lead and written to its timeline. The Communication tab counts them across the book and names the ones never used , which is how a manager notices that nobody ever sends the video.

search.heading: §Q: handing a customer over
search.text: The brief says "on the second order the lead becomes a customer and the relationship moves to a customer manager". Those are two independent facts joined by an "and". The first is the account's kind , decided by conversion. The second is a separate seat: who runs the relationship . A handover moves sight, and never a rupee. The relationship seat is read by the rules that decide who may see and work an account, so the person handed it can open it. It is not read by the rule that decides whose book an account is in — so no order, target, collections list or Call Log moves. Moving revenue is a reassignment, which is accounts' and administrators' only. That is exactly why a handover can be a manager's act (the hand-over permission) while reassignment cannot: moving the sales seat moves numbers between a manager's own people, and moving this one moves none. A seat that did not carry sight would tell somebody an account was theirs and then refuse them the screen. Rule Detail Only a customer can be handed over A lead is run by its lead manager — a different seat. Refused with "A lead has no relationship to hand over yet…" A reason is required From ; Other needs a note The new person must be active And the accounts must be in your scope Three writes, one transaction The seat and its date, a history row with the reason, a timeline entry Both sides are told One message each, however many accounts moved; nobody is told about an account that had no previous holder No "decided" mark The customer master never states this seat, so there is nothing to hold off — and stamping the mark would freeze the other two seats against a sync Whether a handover is outstanding is derived , never stored: converted, and nobody named yet. A flag would be a cache with nothing to rebuild it from but the two columns it would be caching. The Handovers list should be empty, and it is a list for exactly that reason.

search.heading: Who can do what
search.text: Action Who Set a next action, record a communication, park a lead Lead work — every associate in scope Hand a relationship over The hand-over permission — managers See these desks and , granted separately

search.text: - setLeadNextAction does not read leads.requireNextAction . The service header says the rule is "enforced by setLeadNextAction "; the action always requires the action, day and person and never reads the setting ( lib/services/lead-actions-service.ts header; lib/actions/leads.ts setLeadNextAction ). The setting only switches the gate condition on moves. - The handover service says kind flips on the first order. Its header ( lib/services/handover-service.ts ) says so; conversion happens on the second. - delivery completed is never raised by the nightly pass — the row exists in the sequence, but nothing records a dispatch to trigger it ( mbos-jobs.ts runNurturePass , TODO). - A next action's notification links to the CRM customer record ( /crm/customers/… ) even when it was set from the Sales Dashboard.

The Calling desk is a pure engine ( engines/lead-calling-desk.ts ) that decides where a lead stands from the desk's side, a read service that narrows and summarises, and a write module whose every action asks the desk's own module grant before it does anything. It writes no stage directly: qualification calls are calls rows, and every stage change — Prospect, Lost, reopen — goes through advanceLeadStage , the same gated move documented on All Leads.

search.heading: A qualification call, end to end
search.text: logQualificationCall. A qualification call is a row in calls , distinguished only by the CALL MARK key in outcome detail . A separate table would have put half a lead's calls where the record history, EOD counts and the customer timeline do not read.

search.heading: The engine
search.text: required means "closes the lead if still missing after Call 3" (only competitor ). prospect means "needed before Ready for Prospect " (competitor, product, monthly litres). suggestCall is a hint about order, never a rule.

search.heading: Becoming a Prospect
search.text: Both buttons share one preparation step, so neither can accept a lead the other would refuse: - preparePromotion — the lead is a working Suspect, the readiness test passes, a sales type is set (or chosen now), a coded reason from leads.prospectReasons , a dry run of the Prospect gate, and the verifier is resolved (self-raised verifier → telecaller verifier → sales manager seat → lead manager seat → org-chart candidate → refuse). - convertLeadToProspect — when leads.callingDeskDirectPromotion is on, moves the lead with advanceLeadStage({ to: "prospect" }) and gives the verifier a next action leads.verificationDueDays out. When off, it delegates to requestProspect unchanged. - requestProspect — leaves the stage alone, writes the prospect request columns with state awaiting , dates the verification the next working day and notifies the verifier. - settleProspectRequest — after a verification, re-reads the latest verification row itself and, on verified , promotes through advanceLeadStage under the manager's hat; on follow up sets followup .

search.heading: Reads and scope
search.text: The desk narrows with resolveScope → scopedToUsers , not managerScope : the latter answers "everybody" for anyone without a territory row, which would make one telecaller's desk count the country's leads. Converted leads and archived leads are left out; the query is capped at DESK LEAD CAP and the list paged at DESK PAGE , while the tiles are counted over the whole capped set.

search.text: - — off by default. The layout checks it, and every write checks it again through deskRefusal , because lead.work alone is held by every associate.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: Change the rule in the engine. Which answers are compulsory or needed for a Prospect is a flag on DESK FIELDS . The phase, the ready banner and the button's enabled state all read prospectProgress , so one edit moves all three. Keep stage writes on advanceLeadStage. A desk action that set lead stage itself would skip the gate, the transition row and the timeline. Every new write asks deskRefusal. Put it immediately after requireCapability("lead.work") . Do not store derived state. "Ready" and "which call" are derived on every read. Only the request is stored, because asking is not being.

The Calling desk is where a telecaller works online leads by phone — enquiries that arrived from the website, WhatsApp, a portal or a marketplace, and that nobody is going to visit. Each lead gets at most three qualification calls . Inside those three you collect what a Prospect needs; the moment it is all in, the lead is Ready for Prospect and you convert it. If the calls run out first, the lead is closed or left for you to finish on the record. The desk is granted to you personally. If you can open the CRM but not the Calling desk, nobody has given it to you yet — ask whoever manages access. Every other Lead Management screen works without it.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: The Calling desk, opened on today's work queue. Good morning, telecaller View pipeline New lead Total leads. 64 New online leads. 6 Calls due today. 9 Follow-ups due. 2 Overdue. 3 THE 3-CALL RULE — WHERE EVERY LEAD STANDS Call 1 pending 6 Call 2 pending 4 Call 3 pending 2 Ready for Prospect 3 Awaiting verification 1 Returned 1 With Sales Manager 5 Lost 7 1. Suspect 18 2. Prospect 4 3. Qualification 2 4. Sample / Trial 1 … 12. Customer Today's work queue. Ready for Prospect. Customer A · 2 calls used Pressing any figure filters the list on the same screen — nothing navigates. The address bar remembers the filter, so a link to "Call 2 pending" can be sent to a colleague. Back to today's work queue returns to the default list.

search.heading: What is on today's work queue
search.text: The queue holds three kinds of lead, in this order: 1. Ready for Prospect — everything a Prospect needs is in. Convert it. 2. Returned — the Sales Manager sent a request back. Read their note. 3. Due — a call or message due today or earlier, soonest first. A brand-new lead nobody has scheduled counts as Call 1 due today . A lead with the Sales Manager, or with a next step scheduled for a later day, is not on the queue.

search.heading: Working a lead, step by step
search.text: Open the lead from the list. The desk record opens. The header shows the reference (for example TC-1042 ), when it was created and its source. Read What the enquiry said — the customer's own words, if the lead came from the website. Press Start call N / 3. The call window shows which questions are worth asking on this call and which are better left to later. Anything already on file is listed as answered and is never asked again . Choose what happened. Pick one of the five outcomes (table below). If it was No answer , say which kind — no response, busy, switched off, out of network, call rejected or disconnected. Fill in what they told you. Only if you spoke to them. Leave anything they did not know blank — a blank is "Not yet captured", never an error. Say what happens next. Choose Call or Message first , write a line, and pick a follow-up date. The date is suggested two working days out and cannot be in the past. Save. The button tells you what will happen: Save call , Save call — Ready for Prospect , or Save call and mark Lost . Read it before you press it.

search.heading: The five call outcomes
search.text: Outcome When to use it What it does Spoke — information collected They answered and you captured at least one new answer. Uses a call. If you did not fill in anything new it is refused — use asked to call back . Spoke — asked to call back Reached, but a bad time or only partly answered. Uses a call. No answer Rang, nobody spoke. Uses a call. You must say which kind of no answer. Answers cannot be saved with it. Wrong or invalid number Not the business, or the number does not work. Closes the lead as Lost at once. Not interested They said no. Closes the lead as Lost at once. A no-answer still uses a call. All five outcomes count against the three. Three unanswered calls, with the competitor never captured, close the lead as No response after 3 attempts . If you only need to send something, use Message instead — a message uses no call.

search.heading: The eleven answers
search.text: Answer Needed for a Prospect? Best asked on Competitor (which brand they use now) Yes — compulsory . Missing after Call 3 closes the lead. Call 1 Product (which of ours they need) Yes Call 1 Monthly requirement (litres a month) Yes Call 1 Customer type (dealer, manufacturer, distributor, retailer, private limited user) No — asked when you convert, if still blank Call 1 Application (what they will use it on) No Call 1 Decision maker No — "ask if known" Call 2 GST No Call 2 Buyer No Call 3 Credit days No Call 3 Address No Call 3 Email No Call 3 On Call 3 every answer a Prospect still needs is asked, whatever call it was suggested for.

search.heading: When a lead is Ready for Prospect
search.text: As soon as the competitor, the product and the monthly requirement are all on the record, the lead turns Ready for Prospect — even if that happens on Call 1. No further call is offered. Press Convert to Prospect. On the green banner, or in the Move this lead forward card. Say why it is worth pursuing. Pick one of the listed reasons — for example They need it regularly (confirmed) or Wants to switch from another brand . Add what the customer said if it helps. Answer what the record is missing. If nobody has said how the lead will be sold, choose Direct customer or Third Party Customer — it is never chosen for you. If the kind of business or the contact person is still blank, you are asked for them here. Confirm. The lead becomes a Prospect and the Sales Manager is told. You see: Prospect created. Waiting for Sales Manager verification. Qualification opens once they verify it, and then it is yours to complete. If your manager has switched off direct conversion, the same button instead requests the Prospect: the lead stays a Suspect, shows Awaiting verification , and becomes a Prospect only when the Sales Manager confirms it on their verification call. You will see Prospect requested in place of Prospect created .

search.heading: What each status means
search.text: Status on the lead Means What you do Call 1 / 2 / 3 pending That call is owed. Make it. Ready for Prospect Everything a Prospect needs is in. Convert it. Three calls used Three calls made; the competitor is in but the product or monthly requirement is not. The lead is not lost. Close it, or ask the Sales Manager to fill in the rest (see the FAQ). Awaiting verification You requested a Prospect; it is with the Sales Manager. Nothing. Do not ring the customer again. Manager follow-up The Sales Manager is holding the request while they follow up. Nothing until they decide. Returned by Manager The Sales Manager sent it back with a note. Read the note. Resubmit, or mark it Lost. Prospect and beyond It has left the desk's calling. The record is read-only except where Qualification is yours. Lost Closed, with the reason. Reverse it if the customer comes back.

search.heading: Messages, next actions, closing and reopening
search.text: - Message — log a company profile, product image, brochure, video, price list or WhatsApp follow-up you sent. It uses no call . If the next step was waiting on that message, it becomes the next call, one day out. - Next action — change what happens next and when, as a call or a message. It can only be changed while the lead is a Suspect. - Mark Lost — pick one of six reasons: No response after 3 attempts , Required information not obtained , Customer not interested , Requirement not genuine , Wrong lead — should not have been raised , or Other . You cannot close a lead while the Sales Manager has it. - Reverse Lead — reopens a Lost lead with a reason. It goes back to the rung it was lost from, and if that was Suspect the three calls start again . Earlier calls stay on the record. A lead closed because the Sales Manager's verification failed can only be reversed by them.

search.heading: Leads with no owner
search.text: A lead nobody owns is on nobody's desk. If you can hand leads out, a banner tells you how many there are, and Show them lists them. Open one and press Assign to give it to somebody who holds the Calling desk. People who cannot open the desk are shown greyed out in the list, with the reason.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I pressed Start call but it says the three calls are over.. The lead has moved on from Suspect, or the Sales Manager has it, or three calls have already been made this round. There is no Call 4. It says 'Everything a Prospect needs is already in, so no further call is needed.'. The lead is Ready for Prospect. Convert it instead of calling again. I typed an answer that was already on file and it was not saved.. Answers already on the record are never overwritten by a call — the message says which ones were left unchanged. This protects the figure the Sales Manager checks on their verification call. The lead says Three calls used. Is it lost?. No. The competitor is in, but the product or the monthly requirement is not. It stays a Suspect. The desk's own Edit button is not built yet, so the remaining answers cannot be typed in here — close the lead, or ask the Sales Manager to complete it from the main lead record. My request was Returned. Can I ring the customer to fix it?. No — a returned lead cannot be rung again from the desk. Read the manager's note, then Resubmit for verification or Mark Lost . Why can I not convert even though it says Ready?. The conversion also checks the Prospect gate: a reason, a kind of business, a contact person, a next action, and a Sales Manager who can verify it. The refusal names what is missing. If it says no Sales Manager covers the lead's region, ask an administrator. A lead I expected is not on today's queue.. It is scheduled for a later day, it is with the Sales Manager, or it belongs to another telecaller. Try the search box, or press Total leads . Did the call close my reminder?. Yes, if somebody answered. A reminder due on the lead is closed by an answered call, the same as on the Call Log; a no-answer or a dead number closes nothing.

The Calling desk is where leads nobody will visit — website, WhatsApp, portal and marketplace enquiries — are qualified by telephone. It sits on top of the lead ladder rather than beside it: the ladders, the gates and the sales manager's verification all work exactly as described on All Leads. What the desk adds is one rule about how many calls a lead gets and one rule about when it is ready to become a Prospect . Settings quoted here are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: The three-call rule
search.text: A lead on the desk gets at most three qualification calls — Call 1, Call 2, Call 3. There is no fourth. The calls exist to collect the answers a Prospect needs; the moment those are in, calling stops, whichever call it was. What one call does to a lead. Every outcome uses a call. Spoke, asked to call back, no answer, wrong number and not interested all count against the three. A message sent to the lead (brochure, price list, WhatsApp follow-up) uses no call. Only the competitor is compulsory. Of the eleven answers the desk can collect, only which brand they use now closes the lead if it is still missing after Call 3. Product and monthly requirement are needed for a Prospect but are never a reason to close: a blank there is "not yet captured", and the lead stays a Suspect marked Three calls used . "Never once answered" and "answered but would not say" are different losses, and the desk records them as different reasons so they can be counted later. A competitor is the one answer without which a Prospect is not worth a sales manager's call; a missing product or litre figure is something somebody can still fill in on the record.

search.heading: No question is asked twice
search.text: What is still owed is whatever is still empty . An answer captured on Call 1 is a filled field on the record, so it is not offered on Call 2 — not because a rule hides it, but because there is nothing left to ask. Each answer has a suggested call (competitor, product, litres, customer type and application on Call 1; decision maker and GST on Call 2; buyer, credit days, address and email on Call 3). On Call 3 every answer a Prospect still needs is asked regardless. Nothing about "ready" or "which call is next" is stored. Ready for Prospect is simply the answer to "are those answers on the record", and which call is a count of the qualification calls already made. A stored flag would be a second copy free to drift the day somebody types a competitor in somewhere else.

search.heading: Becoming a Prospect
search.text: When a lead is ready, the telecaller presses Convert to Prospect , chooses a coded reason from , and fills anything the Prospect gate still needs (sales type, kind of business, contact person). What happens next depends on one switch: Switch What Convert to Prospect does On The lead becomes a Prospect at once, through the same gate as any other move, and the sales manager is given a verification next action due days out. Message: Prospect created. Waiting for Sales Manager verification. Off The lead stays a Suspect and is put forward as a request ( Awaiting verification ). The sales manager's verification call is what promotes it — due on the next working day. Message: Prospect requested. Both paths read the same readiness test and the same Prospect gate, so a lead accepted by one can never be refused by the other for something it was never asked. The switch decides only who is trusted to press the button that promotes . Turning it off sends everything back through the same verification queue with no second code path kept alive.

search.heading: The request states
search.text: A request is not a rung: the lead stays a Suspect until the sales manager acts. It is held beside the stage as one of three states. State on the desk Meaning What the desk can do Awaiting verification With the sales manager Nothing — no call is offered, and the lead cannot be closed Manager follow-up The manager is holding it while they follow up Nothing until they decide Returned by Manager Sent back with a note Read the note; resubmit or mark Lost When the sales manager records a verified verification, the request settles: the lead moves to Prospect through the ordinary gated move under the manager's own permission, and the manager takes the lead-manager seat. Not qualified closes the lead as lost through the verification's own closure.

search.heading: Who verifies
search.text: The verifier is found in this order, and the telecaller chooses nobody: 1. If a sales manager raised the lead herself , the person named in the self-raised verifier setting ( leads.selfRaisedVerifierEmail ) — nobody verifies their own work. 2. If a calling-desk worker owns the lead, the person named in the telecaller verifier setting ( leads.telecallerVerifierEmail ) — strictly: a name that matches nobody who can verify refuses the conversion with a message rather than routing it elsewhere. 3. The lead's sales manager seat, if filled. 4. The lead manager seat, if filled. 5. Otherwise the first eligible candidate from the org chart. If there is none, the conversion is refused and says so.

search.heading: The work queue
search.text: Today's work queue holds three kinds of lead, in this order: Ready for Prospect , Returned , then Due (a call or message due today or earlier, soonest first; a brand-new lead nobody scheduled counts as Call 1 due today ). Leads with the sales manager, or with a next step on a later day, are not on it. The figures across the top filter the same list without navigating, and every filter is in the address bar.

search.heading: Closing and reopening
search.text: - Mark Lost takes one of the desk's six reasons ( No response after 3 attempts , Required information not obtained , Customer not interested , Requirement not genuine , Wrong lead — should not have been raised , Other ). Each is filed under a code from . A lead cannot be closed while the sales manager has it. - Reverse Lead reopens a lost lead with a coded reason from . It returns to the rung it was lost from; if that was Suspect, the three calls start again . Earlier calls stay on the record. A lead closed because verification failed can only be reversed by the sales manager. - Next action can only be changed while the lead is a Suspect.

search.heading: Who can use the desk, and whose leads they see
search.text: The desk is granted per person. The Calling desk is its own module, off by default even on a whole-CRM grant. Every write the desk makes checks the module itself — not only the screen — because the underlying lead permission is held by every associate and the route guard alone would be a courtesy, not a door. The desk narrows the way every other CRM list does: a telecaller sees their own book , a manager their reports' books. It deliberately does not use the territory narrowing the All Leads list uses, which answers "everybody" for anyone without a territory. Leads with no owner are on nobody's desk. Somebody whose view is wider than one book sees a banner counting them and can assign each to a person who holds the desk; people who cannot open the desk are listed greyed out with the reason. Assigning notifies whoever can hand leads out.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - "Five answers" versus three. The setting description for direct promotion and the engine's header both say "the five required answers"; the code's readiness test ( prospectProgress ) needs three — competitor, product, monthly litres ( engines/lead-calling-desk.ts DESK FIELDS ). - Two verification due dates. Direct promotion dates the sales manager's verification days out; a request is dated the next working day ( actions/lead-calling-desk.ts convertLeadToProspect vs requestProspect ).

The commercial end is reads over existing columns plus a handful of actions. There is no negotiation table: the Negotiation desk reads customers on the negotiation rung and its newest transition. Commitments are three lead expected order columns judged by one pure file, lib/lead-commitment.ts . Distributor appointments are distributor profiles plus two mbos approvals rows. Everything below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: Never add forecast to fact. Anything named forecast… or read from lead expected order stays in its own total. A screen that sums the two is the bug this file was written to prevent. Change what a commitment is in lead-commitment.ts only. The record panel, the three desks and the confirm action all read it; the SQL string and the TypeScript function must change together. Never write lead stage from an order action. Rungs that read the ledger ( first order , delivery , payment , second order ) move through the gate when the ledger says so. Routing is pure. A new reason to escalate goes in approvalRouteReason , which the handset, the console and the action all read.

The commercial end of the funnel is where a lead that liked its trial is turned into an order — and, for the few leads still on the distributor ladder, where a distributor is appointed. It is two modules: Commercial , which follows every lead from negotiation to its second order, and Distributor appointments , which carries a distributor candidate through two approvals. Thresholds on this page are your CRM's current settings.

search.heading: Commercial: three tabs, one arc
search.text: Tab Question it answers Negotiation Who is being negotiated with now, for how long, and is anybody holding them? Commitments What has a customer promised — a day and a size — and did it happen? First orders Leads past their first order: delivery, payment and the second order that makes them a customer.

search.heading: The Negotiation desk at a glance
search.text: Negotiation desk. Negotiation desk In negotiation. 14 No commitment. 6 Longest here. 38 days

search.heading: Asking for the first order
search.text: Open the lead and press Ask for the first order. You get eight questions: how much, which product, when they will place it, what is stopping it today, and whether price, credit, another brand or delivery is in the way. Write down the day, and a size if they gave one. The day is required. The size is the number of cans or a value — either one. If they could not say how much, save the day anyway: it is kept as a follow-up and simply not counted as a promise. Save. You are told which you recorded: a commitment (day and size), or a follow-up (day only). A size with no day is refused — nobody can chase "two hundred cans" with no date.

search.heading: Confirming the actual order
search.text: When the customer places the order, press Confirm the actual order on the lead and give the day they placed it , the value , their reference (PO or confirmation number) and, if you have it, the cans. Rule Why There must be a commitment first Confirming an order against nothing is a sale with no forecast behind it The value must be more than zero An order nobody can value reads as zero on every target and report The day cannot be in the future It is the day they placed it If a live order already exists you are told So the same order is not taken twice The order goes to accounts as waiting for approval , like every order. The lead does not move to 1st order when you save — it moves when accounts accept the order. The card says so before you press the button.

search.heading: Commitments tab
search.text: View Lists Open A day promised that has not come round yet Due this week Promised inside the next seven days Slipped The day came and went with no order — the view that earns the screen Converted A real order arrived on the account Forecast figures and real orders are totalled separately on this screen and are never added together.

search.heading: First orders tab
search.text: Leads on 1st order , Delivery , Payment and 2nd order . Delivery and payment are read from the ledger — what the sheet and accounts recorded — never typed here. When a second counting order lands, the lead becomes a customer and leaves the funnel.

search.heading: Distributor appointments
search.text: New distributor leads can no longer be raised; this tab finishes the appointments already started. Fill the distributor profile. About thirty questions about the business: GST and PAN, address checked, business type and years, decision maker, dealer network, territory and cities, sales team, delivery, warehouse and storage, product portfolio, competitor brands, potential and commitments, credit wanted, proposed territory, whether an existing distributor was checked and any conflict, exclusivity requested, initial stock and monthly commitment. Submit for management review. The sales manager is asked to recommend the candidate. Until they do, it waits on the sales manager. Record the commercial terms. The special discount, the credit limit and whether territory exclusivity is granted. Recording terms needs the distributor-terms permission (a manager). Management decides. Every appointment then goes to management for the final approval. The record says why: exclusivity , over the discount threshold , over the credit-limit threshold , or standard review . Record the signed agreement, then the stock order. The lead climbs to Distributor agreement and Initial stock order, then Active distributor. Over the threshold when Threshold now Special discount is more than % Agreed credit limit is more than paise (₹1 = 100 paise) Territory exclusivity is granted (asking for it does not count) always A step can be sent back for correction with a note, rather than refused. The candidate is corrected and resubmitted; the note clears once it is answered.

search.heading: The distributor's own salesmen
search.text: A distributor's salesman — the person who actually visits the shops for them — is recorded by name, mobile and territory on the distributor. He has no MahekOne login and never will, so he never appears in any person picker.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I recorded a date but the lead is not on the forecast.. A date alone is a follow-up. Add how many cans or roughly what value and it becomes a commitment. I confirmed the order but the lead is still on Negotiation.. It moves to 1st order when accounts approve the order. The customer ordered once. Why are they still a lead?. The first order is the end of the trial. The account becomes a customer on its second order. Why does an ordinary distributor still need management?. Every appointment is approved by management. The thresholds only change the reason written on the request. Can a manager approve an appointment on their own?. No. A manager can recommend and agree terms; only management (the distributor-approval permission) appoints.

The commercial end of the funnel turns on one distinction the rest of Lead Management never has to make: a forecast is not a sale . What a customer said on a call — a day, a quantity, a value — is kept, shown and chased, but it is never added to anything real. This tab explains how a commitment is defined, how the first order is confirmed without bypassing accounts, how a lead becomes a customer, and how a distributor is appointed through two approvals. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: The arc from negotiation to customer
search.text: Negotiation to customer — direct and third-party ladders.

search.heading: Negotiation
search.text: There is no negotiation table. A negotiation is a lead standing on the Negotiation rung, with a reason on its newest stage move, a credit ask against the standard term, and a commitment or the absence of one. Every one of those already exists; a separate table would be a fourth place the same facts live. Entering Negotiation needs a sample sent, its feedback written down and the trial approved — see Samples. The sample review is what authorises a commercial conversation, not the salesman deciding he is ready for one. Orders below Negotiation are no longer refused. The rule "no commercial commitment before negotiation" used to mean the handset refused an order against a lead below Negotiation. Mahek reversed it: a shop that is ready to buy is a customer, whatever rung it was filed under, and a salesman holding an order must not be told to come back later. An order on a lead now goes through and counts toward converting it. The Negotiation desk still shows an old banner saying no order may be taken below this rung — see the end of this page.

search.heading: A commitment is a day AND a size
search.text: §3.4 — the definition, in one place. A commitment is an expected order date and either an expected quantity in cans or an expected value. Either size will do, never both required, because at this point there is often no pack chosen and the catalogue holds no prices to convert one into the other. - A day alone is still recorded. It shows on the record, it is chased on that day, and it is listed on the desk marked Day but no size — but it is not counted on the forecast or in "expected this week". A form that refused the save would lose the one fact the salesman did come back with. - A size with no day is refused. "Two hundred cans" with nothing saying when is a sentence nobody can chase and no view can put in a week. - Zero is refused — zero is a customer declining, not committing. The rule used to accept either half. A date alone then put a lead on the forecast board, added it to "expected this week" and escalated the sales manager's next step to "Confirm actual order" — four screens saying a customer had promised something, and not one able to say how much.

search.heading: Confirming the first order
search.text: Confirm the actual order creates a real order from what the customer placed. It refuses unless a commitment exists, the value is above zero, and the day is not in the future; it warns if a live order (anything not declined or cancelled) is already on the account, so the same order is not taken twice. The rung is not written here. The order is written waiting for accounts' approval , like every other order. The 1st order gate counts only orders accounts have accepted, so the lead moves when accounts accept — not when this is saved. Writing the rung here would walk a lead onto the book on the strength of an order accounts were about to decline. No line items are invented. The manager confirmed a value and a reference on the phone; nobody picked a product. A line made up from the lead's product answer would put litres into somebody's product mix on the strength of a guess. The money still counts as revenue and is reported as unmatched to any product — the honest answer.

search.heading: When the lead becomes a customer
search.text: On its second counting order. A first order from a shop that has just finished a trial is the tail of the trial. The second approved order makes the account a customer — on every path: a call logged in the CRM, accounts approving an order, a handset order, or a gated stage move to 2nd order . The person who owned the lead becomes its sales account manager. A distributor is the exception: there is no trial order in an appointment, so it is invoiced from Distributor approval . Delivery and payment are read from the ledger, never written here . Order status comes from the order sheet and from accounts' approval; a second status ladder would be overwritten by the sheet every half hour or fight it. Payment needs money accounts have confirmed in the bank, not money somebody reported.

search.heading: Appointing a distributor (§11, §12)
search.text: The distributor ladder is retired for new leads; appointments already started run to the end. Two approval steps. A salesman may never appoint a distributor, and a manager may not do it alone. Step 0 is the sales manager putting a candidate forward. Recording the commercial terms needs the distributor-terms permission (a manager). Step 1 is management's — the distributor-approval permission, which only an administrator holds — and it is created every time terms are agreed, beside step 0 rather than replacing it, because the sales manager is the only person who has met the candidate. The terms decide why the request reached management, written on the request: Reason on the request When exclusivity Territory exclusivity was granted — always, whatever the numbers. Requested exclusivity routes nowhere; it is an opening position. over discount The special discount is above % over credit limit The agreed credit limit is above paise standard None of the above The person carrying the target must not be the person allowing the discount that hits it — the same reasoning that keeps order approval away from managers entirely. Management used to see only escalated appointments, but the gate on Distributor approval has always demanded management's signature, so an ordinary candidate sat at Commercial discussion for ever with nothing anybody could approve. Now every appointment reaches management, and the thresholds only decide the words. A step can be sent back for correction with a note. The note is cleared when the step is next answered; the send-back keeps its own timeline entry and audit row.

search.heading: The distributor's salesman is a name, not an account
search.text: A distributor's own salesman has no MahekOne login and never will. He is recorded as a name, mobile and territory against the distributor, and the shop's distributor link can point at him — so the chain Mahek → distributor → his salesman → the shop is recorded from the first visit rather than reconstructed later. Giving him a user account would put him in every person picker in the product.

search.heading: Who can do what
search.text: Action Who Ask for the first order, record a commitment Lead work — every associate Confirm the actual order Order capture — every associate Fill the profile, submit for review Lead work Recommend (step 0), record commercial terms Distributor terms — managers Appoint (step 1) Distributor approval — administrators only

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - The Negotiation desk's banner is out of date. It reads "No order may be taken below this rung … handleOrder refuses one against a lead below negotiation" ( components/leads/commercial/negotiation-screen.tsx ). The handset's order handler no longer refuses; it converts ( actions/mbos.ts , the order handler's "AN ORDER ON A LEAD CONVERTS IT" block). AGENTS.md's "NO COMMERCIAL COMMITMENT BEFORE NEGOTIATION" section is likewise stale. - Management always reviews. AGENTS.md says step 1 is forced by exclusivity or a threshold; the code creates step 1 for every appointment and records standard when no threshold is crossed ( engines/lead-gates.ts managementRouteReason ). - AGENTS.md says kind flips at the first order ; the code converts on the second ( lead-conversion-service.ts ).

Intake and Qualification are two lead modules ( and ), each guarded by its own folder layout and each rendering a shared page from src/components/leads/pages/ . Raising a lead has one writer , captureLead , used by the form, bulk intake and the enquiry screen. Qualification's screens are reads over the gate engine; every write on them is an existing lead action, and every stage change goes through advanceLeadStage .

search.text: captureLead. The capture schema documents every field's reasoning; the two worth knowing before editing it: - monthlyLitres is litres — there is no SKU at capture. - requirement / requirementProductId both write lead requirement (a product pick writes the product's name , server-side). Neither writes lead required product id , which is the Prospect and calling-desk answer.

search.heading: The Suspect cap
search.text: The office list reads the count from mbos visits with count( ) — never a stored counter — and compares against mbos.leads.maxSuspectVisits cast ::int in SQL. decideSuspect writes lead suspect decided at after the move, so a refused move never silences the question. keepAsSuspect writes lead hold reason and does not move the stage.

search.heading: Qualifying a lead from the field
search.text: Called from actions/mbos.ts — the handset's lead handler (on reaching Prospect) and its visit-decision path — after the stage write has committed, with .catch(() = {}) . The seat is the idempotency guard. It does not set lead manager decided at .

search.heading: The verification call and validation answers
search.text: recordLeadValidationCall ( lead.verify ) writes one row per call to mbos lead validations — the same table the handset writes — using VERIFICATION COLUMNS in lead-labels.ts as the one statement of which answer lands in which column. not qualified requires a note and closes the lead through advanceLeadStage with the verification-failed code. A desk request is then settled by settleProspectRequest .

search.text: The answers live in customers.lead qualification (jsonb) under QUALIFICATION ANSWER KEYS ; saveLeadQualification drops any other key and checks each with qualificationAnswerFault . GST reads the columns gstin + gst verified , never a tick in the jsonb.

search.text: For a funnel lead, validateGstin asks gstValidatorRefusal (the lead's sales manager, an admin, or a lead.verify holder where no seat is held — never the owner) instead of lead.gstValidate ; the capability and the back-office seat still apply to accounts that were never leads.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: One way to raise a lead. Any new door (an import, an API) calls captureLead or captureLeadBatch . A second insert path would skip the duplicate guard, the foot-of-ladder rule, the distributor link and the timeline row. Never make a capture field required to fix a gate. If the gate needs something, it asks at the rung. Capture stays four fields. Validation answers are a row, not columns on the lead. Add a confirmed answer as a column on mbos lead validations , map it in VERIFICATION COLUMNS , and add it to disagreementsIn if both sides answer it. Keep counts live. Visit counts stay count( ) over mbos visits ; numbers beside parameters get ::int .

This page covers the two desks a lead passes through before it can have a sample: Intake , where a lead is raised, and Qualification , where it is checked, called and qualified. Intake is where a shop that rang the office, or a website form that landed in somebody's inbox, becomes a lead. Qualification is everything between a Suspect and a lead that is ready for a trial. Numbers on this page — how many visits, how many days — are your CRM's current settings, read live.

search.heading: Intake: the three tabs
search.text: Tab What it is for Capture a lead Raise one lead from a phone call or an enquiry. Bulk intake Paste or upload a list of leads, see what would happen to each row, then raise them. Duplicates Pairs of accounts that look like the same shop, for somebody to check.

search.heading: Capture a lead at a glance
search.text: Capture a lead. How will this be sold?. Direct customer Third Party Customer Not Decided The shop. What they want (all optional). Raise the lead

search.heading: Raising a lead, step by step
search.text: Choose how it will be sold. Direct customer, Third Party Customer, or Not Decided. Fill in the shop. Name, ten-digit mobile, town and where the lead came from are required. Everything else is optional — you are on the phone, and a lead with a name and a number is better than one never raised. Add what they told you. What they want (pick a product, or type it in their words), roughly how many litres a month, which brand they use now, what they will use it on. Press Raise the lead. If the mobile number already belongs to an account, you see That telephone number is already on the book with the account it reaches. Raise it anyway only if it really is a different shop — two separate leads cannot be merged back later. GST is not asked here. It is collected during Qualification and validated by your sales manager before any sample goes out.

search.heading: Bulk intake
search.text: Upload or paste a list. Before anything is written you see each row's verdict — will be raised, a duplicate of an account already on the book, or refused with the reason. You then raise the good rows in one go; one next action can be set for the whole batch.

search.heading: Duplicates
search.text: Pairs of accounts with the same phone number or very similar names (how similar is ). Open both, decide, and press Not a duplicate to take a pair off the list for good.

search.heading: Qualification: the four tabs
search.text: Tab What it is for Suspect decisions Suspects that have been visited enough times that somebody must decide: Prospect, or not. Verification queue Prospects waiting for the sales manager's verification call. Validation calls The calls that were made, and where what the shop said differs from what the salesman reported. Checklists Leads at Qualification and exactly which of the eight answers each is still missing.

search.heading: Suspect decisions
search.text: A field salesman gets visits to work out whether a Suspect is worth anything, and at the outside. The list shows every undecided Suspect, furthest past the cap first , with its visit count. You choose What happens Prospect The lead moves to Prospect through its gate (all seven Prospect answers needed) with a coded reason. Not a prospect The lead is closed as Lost with a coded reason. Keep as Suspect It stays a Suspect and you write why. It stays on this list so the question keeps being asked. Nothing refuses a visit past the cap — the visit is real work. What changes is that the lead now has to be decided .

search.heading: Verification queue and the validation call
search.text: When a lead becomes a Prospect, the sales manager rings the shop to check that the visit happened, that Mahek was explained properly, and that the opportunity is real. The form asks seventeen questions in four groups (about the salesman, the opportunity, any objections, and how ready they are) and ends with one of three outcomes: Outcome Means Checked. The visit happened and Mahek was explained Verified. Qualification opens. Follow-up needed. This call could not confirm the visit Needs another call; the lead waits. Check failed. There is no business here Closes the lead as Lost. A note is required. When a lead is qualified from the field, its lead manager is filled in from the org chart and a validation call lands on their list for the next working day , holidays skipped.

search.heading: Validation calls
search.text: Every call made, newest first, with the four things both sides answered set side by side: what the salesman reported on the lead and what the shop confirmed on the phone — the requirement, the monthly litres, the competitor and the potential. A row where they differ is marked. That difference is the most useful thing the call produces, so neither answer ever overwrites the other.

search.heading: Checklists: the eight qualification answers
search.text: Before a sample can go out, the lead needs all eight: The answer Who gives it 1 GST number You record it; your sales manager validates it at review 2 What they will use it on You 3 The trial: product and pack, quantity, who will test it, for how long You 4 Who decides, who places the order, who pays ( the same person is a real answer) You 5 Price and credit discussed, and how they took it You 6 Where we deliver, how long it takes, whether that suits them You 7 Still willing to test, now they know price, credit and delivery You 8 What happens if the trial goes well, and by when You Then your sales manager reviews the qualification (verified, incomplete, or needs clarification), and the figures — monthly need, product, competitor — must have been confirmed within days. A refused GST number blocks the sample. If your sales manager refuses the GST number, no sample can go out until a corrected number is validated. You do not need to redo anything else — the lead carries on from where it was the moment the corrected number is accepted.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Do I need GST to raise a lead?. No. It is asked at Qualification, before a sample. The customer said cans, not litres.. Convert roughly to litres a month. There is no pack chosen yet, so litres are the one unit everybody agrees on. Why can I not see the Verification queue?. Verifying is a manager's job and needs the verify permission. You will still see your own leads waiting there on their records. A Suspect has had five visits and nothing stops the salesman visiting again.. Correct — visits are never refused. The lead is on Suspect decisions until somebody answers Prospect, not a prospect, or keep as Suspect with a reason. The shop told the sales manager a different litre figure from the salesman.. Both are kept. Validation calls marks the row so somebody can find out which is true.

Intake and Qualification are the bottom of every ladder: Suspect → Prospect → Qualification → ready for a sample . The rules here exist to make sure that by the time a can of stock leaves the godown, somebody has established who the shop is, what they use, what they want, whether they can be invoiced, and whether the salesman's account of the visit matches the shop's. This tab is the reasoning; the ladder and gate rules apply throughout. Values shown are the ones your CRM is using now.

search.heading: From capture to a sample
search.text: The bottom of the direct and third-party ladders.

search.heading: Raising a lead
search.text: A lead is planted at the foot of its own ladder. Whatever a form or a handset claims, a new lead starts at Suspect (or New when no sales type was chosen). §28's gates are asked when a lead moves , and creating one is not a move — so a create that named a later rung would otherwise skip every gate. The only other rung a create may name is Lost , which is a closure, not a climb. - Only four things are required : the shop's name, a ten-digit mobile, the town and the source. The four Prospect facts (litres, competitor, what they want, application) are optional at capture. This is a phone call, not a visit; demanding them here loses the lead rather than improving it — the gate asks for them at the rung where they matter. - The requirement is stored in the customer's own words. "Thinner for a spray booth" is not resolved to a product while somebody waits on the phone. Picking a product from the catalogue writes its name as the requirement, never the product the Prospect gate reads; that one is answered separately. - A third-party shop says who bills it at capture , picked from accounts that may be named as a distributor (direct customers not themselves marked third-party). - Priority is a manager's judgement. It is only accepted from somebody who may set it. - A phone number already on the book stops the form and shows the account it reaches. Raising it anyway is a deliberate second click, because two rows for one business cannot be merged back. Why litres, when everything else is cans. Every other quantity in MahekOne is cans, because cans are what a customer orders. A lead has no pack yet — "about two hundred litres a month" comes long before anybody knows if that is 5-litre or 20-litre cans — so cans would be a unit nobody has agreed the size of.

search.heading: Bulk intake and duplicates
search.text: Bulk intake runs the same writer for every row, so a file cannot raise a lead that the single form would refuse. It previews first — each row's verdict, nothing written — and then raises. Duplicates pairs accounts by phone number and by name similarity above ; a pair dismissed as "not a duplicate" is recorded and never offered again.

search.heading: The Suspect visit cap: a decision is demanded, never a visit refused
search.text: Two visits to decide, a maximum before a decision is forced. After visits a Suspect starts to warn. At visits the lead becomes a single question — Prospect or not a prospect — and the visit cannot be closed on the handset without an answer. Past the cap the manager is told instead. Only undecided rungs are capped: Suspect, and the legacy New and Contacted. A Prospect is never asked again. A salesman whose visit is refused stops recording visits, and the company loses the GPS, the competitor note and the reason in order to stop a number reaching four. What the rule actually wants is that nobody keeps visiting a shop nobody has decided about — and that is bought by demanding an answer , not by blocking the work. The count is the number of real visits recorded, worked out each time rather than kept as a running counter — a visit that syncs from a handset two days late must still count in the right place. The Suspect decisions list sorts furthest past the cap first, and includes leads approaching the warning, because its job is to stop leads reaching the cap. The three answers: Answer What it writes Prospect A gated move to Prospect with a coded reason from , then a mark that the Suspect was decided Not a prospect A move to Lost with a coded reason from , then the same mark Keep as Suspect No move — a written reason, so the lead stays on the list that keeps asking

search.heading: Becoming a Prospect
search.text: The seven Prospect answers (kind of business, litres a month, current brand, which of our products, contact person, a next action, and the coded reason) are described on All Leads. Telephone leads reach Prospect through the Calling desk.

search.heading: What qualifying a lead does
search.text: When a field lead becomes a Prospect from a handset, three things happen, in this order: 1. The lead manager seat is filled from the org chart — the person the salesman reports to, read from the same employee hierarchy the nightly sales-manager pass uses, so the two can never disagree about who reports to whom. 2. That person is told : "You are running a new Prospect." 3. A validation call is put on their list for the next working day — the working week and the company's holidays from configuration, so a task never lands on a Sunday already overdue. Idempotent, and it never overrules a person. The seat itself is the guard: if a lead manager is already set — by a previous pass or by somebody's own choice — nothing is assigned and nobody new is told. A handset that retries sends the same qualification twice; the second pass does nothing. Filling the seat from the org chart does not mark it as decided, so a later org change can still move it; only a person's own pick freezes it. If the org chart names nobody, the person the salesman reports to in MahekOne is told "A Prospect has no Lead Manager" , rather than the lead sitting unowned in silence. All of this runs after the move has been saved and can never undo it.

search.heading: The verification call (§8)
search.text: The sales manager rings the shop and records the answers, not just a verdict : did the salesman visit, was Mahek explained well, what the shop thought of him, what they use now and how much, whether it could grow, objections on price, quality, delivery and credit, and how ready they are for a trial, rates and an order. Two of those questions are about the salesman rather than the sale, and they are why the call exists at all — no amount of GPS proves Mahek was explained properly. Outcome Effect Verified Qualification opens. A desk request (if any) settles and the lead becomes a Prospect under the manager's own authority. Follow-up The lead waits; a follow-up note says what is wanted. Not qualified Closes the lead as Lost through the ordinary gated move, with a written reason. Only somebody who may verify can do this — a salesman cannot close his own leads as fabrications. The shop's answers never overwrite the salesman's. What the salesman was told standing in the shop stays on the lead. What the shop told the office is stored on the validation call. A lead is often validated twice, and the first call usually matters most, so each call is its own row. The Validation calls screen compares the requirement, the litres, the competitor and the potential, case- and space-insensitively and numbers as numbers; a question one side never answered is shown as "not comparable", never as a disagreement. The two accounts disagreeing is the single most useful thing the call produces — it is how anybody finds out the report and the shop did not match. Collapsing them would destroy exactly that. The script the caller reads is configuration, so it can be improved after a bad call or translated without a release: .

search.heading: Qualification: eight answers, read from real values
search.text: To leave Qualification for a sample, a direct or third-party lead needs: - The eight answers — each read from a stored answer, never a tick: GST, application, the trial plan (product, pack, quantity, tester, duration), who decides / orders / pays, price and credit with how they took it, delivery, still willing to test, and a dated next step. - The figures confirmed within days — monthly need, how much they can buy, the product and the competitor. - The sales manager's review , marked verified. Incomplete and clarification hand it back. - For a third-party shop , the distributor who bills it. GST is collected once and validated once — by two different people. The salesman or telecaller records the GSTIN. On a funnel lead, the sales manager the lead is under validates it as part of the qualification review — or an administrator, or, where nobody holds that seat, somebody who may verify leads — and never the lead's owner , who entered it. The gate reads that validation, not a tick the salesman could set. A refused number blocks the sample while it stands and needs no separate un-blocking: the moment a corrected number is validated, the lead carries on from where it was. The refusal stays on the timeline and in the audit log. Before this, the man who typed the number into his handset was also the man certifying it was a business we could invoice. A warning would not do: by the time somebody read it, the sample would already be dispatched.

search.heading: Who can do what
search.text: Action Who Raise a lead, record qualification answers, decide a Suspect Anybody with lead work — every associate Set a lead's priority at capture A manager (the verify permission) Verification call, not qualified closure, review the qualification The verify permission — a manager Validate or refuse a GST number On a funnel lead: its sales manager, an admin, or (no seat) a verifier — never its owner. On an account that was never a lead: the back-office person or the GST-validate permission See Intake, Qualification Each is its own module, granted separately

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Qualifying fills the lead manager only from the handset. qualifyLead is called by the MBOS lead and visit handlers ( actions/mbos.ts ); a Prospect move made from the CRM record or Suspect decisions does not call it, so no org-chart seat or next-working-day validation task is raised on that path. The calling desk resolves a verifier separately ( actions/lead-calling-desk.ts preparePromotion ). - The retired setting is still listed. leads.suspectMaxVisits says "no longer read"; the cap is mbos.leads.maxSuspectVisits . - AGENTS.md says GST is asked "at the qualify transition" on the legacy qualified rung ( handleLead ). On the funnel ladders it is a condition of leaving Qualification for a sample, not of entering it ( engines/lead-gates.ts QUALIFICATION CONDITIONS ).

Four modules, almost all reads. Oversight , Lost and Funnel & conversion are services over customers , lead stage transitions , audit log and app settings that write nothing. The Sales Manager desk is the same pipeline the Sales Dashboard draws, narrowed by a different scope that travels on the request. Trash, restore and reopen are the only writes. Everything below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.heading: Overrides
search.text: The log selects transitions whose overridden conditions jsonb array is non-empty, scoped through leadsVisible(scope, BOOK OF C) , and resolves each condition id to its sentence through CONDITION SAYS (built from PROSPECT CONDITIONS , QUALIFICATION CONDITIONS and DISTRIBUTOR CONDITIONS ), so the log and the gate cannot word a condition differently.

search.heading: Thresholds are read-only
search.text: src/components/leads/pages/leads-oversight-settings.tsx deliberately has no edit control. Writes go through the Admin Console, which runs checkConsistency and audits before and after.

search.heading: The Sales Manager scope

search.heading: Lost and reopen

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: Oversight never writes. A new oversight question is a new read in the service. If it needs a stored answer, the answer belongs on the record it is about. Resolve scope inside the service. Every function here calls managerScope() itself. A scope passed in is a scope some caller will forget. Never let the Sales Manager scope leak. crmSalesManagerScopeFor applies only when the request is in that workspace. A test that needs it uses setTestWorkspace . Say legacy gaps in words. A lost lead with no closing transition shows Not recorded ; an uncoded move is counted as uncoded. Never infer.
