These are the manager's screens of Lead Management. Oversight shows the gates somebody walked past, everything done to the funnel and under whose authority, and the thresholds the funnel runs on. The Sales Manager desk is the working desk of a sales manager — every lead where they are the named sales manager, sorted into queues. Lost is the central record of every lead closed lost. Funnel & conversion shows the shape of the book, where it came from and what it is dying of. Each is a separate module. You will only see the ones you have been given. Settings on this page are read live.

search.heading: Oversight
search.text: Tab What it shows Overrides Every stage move a manager made through a shut gate: who, when, the reason they gave, and exactly what was still missing . Beside it, the conditions most often waived. Audit Everything done to the funnel — moves, reassignments, verifications, priorities — with who did it and under which app and level. Thresholds Every lead setting, its value, whether it is still the shipped default, and who last changed it. Read-only here. Oversight — the override log. Gates passed. 7 Managers involved. 2 Most often waived. Next action To change a threshold, somebody who holds the Admin Console changes it there (see Help Center and Manager settings); this tab only shows the value in force, so anybody looking at a stuck lead can read the number without needing the console.

search.heading: The Sales Manager desk
search.text: The desk shows only leads where you are the named sales manager (an administrator sees all of them), grouped by the salesman or telecaller who owns each lead. Queue What is in it Verify prospect Prospects, and calling-desk requests, waiting for your verification call Qualification review Qualifications a telecaller completed and asked you to review Sample Requests to approve, approved samples to send, samples on the road, trials nobody has reviewed Order confirmation Expected orders on file that have not become an actual order yet Overdue Leads whose next action date has passed Nurture task Leads with a follow-up task due today or late The tiles and the list are counted from the same rows, so a tile that says 14 always opens a list of 14. The other tabs — Today , List , Mine , Overdue , Pipeline , Distributors — are different cuts of the same book. Start from a queue. Press a tile to see its leads. Search by name, town, contact, owner or product. Open a lead and act. Verify a Prospect, review a qualification, approve or chase a sample, or confirm an order — each opens its own form. Leads you cannot see. A lead with an owner but no sales manager named is in nobody's Sales Manager desk until somebody names one.

search.heading: Lost
search.text: Every lead closed lost, whatever rung it was lost from. Column Means Lost date When it was closed Stage at loss The rung it was on when it was lost. Not recorded for leads lost before the stage history existed Lost reason The coded reason chosen; No reason recorded for old leads Lost by Who closed it Filter by owner, type, stage at loss, reason and dates. The tiles count Total lost , Lost this week and Lost this month .

search.heading: Reversing a lost lead
search.text: Press Reverse Lead , choose why it is being reopened (and add a note where asked), and confirm. The dialog tells you where it will go: usually the rung it was lost from . A lead lost on a failed verification goes back to Prospect to be verified again; one whose ladder has changed, or with no record of where it was lost, goes to the foot of its ladder; one lost at the rung that makes it a customer comes back one rung below. From there every ordinary gate applies again.

search.heading: Deleting and restoring
search.text: From All Leads, a manager can delete leads (move them to the trash) with a sentence saying why. A lead that has been billed cannot be deleted — deactivate it instead. Deleted leads leave every screen; an administrator can restore them.

search.heading: Funnel & conversion
search.text: Tab What it shows Funnel How many leads stand on each rung of each ladder, and how long they have been there; parked leads counted separately. Then Cohort conversion : leads raised in a period, followed forward. Sources Where leads came from, and how well each source converts. Reasons Why leads became Prospects, why customers wanted samples, why leads were lost, and why gates were overridden — by salesman and by town. Reading the cohort. Cohort conversion follows leads raised in a window for days. Converted reached the book; Lost, or past its window did not; Not yet are still inside their window and are counted but not divided. Nothing has closed its window means it is too early to give a rate — not that the rate is zero.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: A lead I manage is not on my Sales Manager desk.. The desk shows leads where you are the named sales manager. If the lead has an owner but no sales manager, nobody's desk shows it until one is named. Why does the override log show conditions as missing when the work was done?. It shows what the record said at the moment of the move. If the work was recorded later, the override reason usually says so. The Reasons tab shows fewer reasons than leads lost.. Leads lost before reasons were required carry no code. They are counted as uncoded so the totals add up. Can I change a threshold from Oversight?. No — it only shows them. Settings are changed in the Admin Console, which checks the whole set before saving; the change then appears here with the name of whoever made it.

Oversight is the set of screens that answer the questions nobody can answer from a worklist: which gates did somebody walk past, what was done to the funnel and under whose authority, what did we lose and why, and how is the book's shape changing? Every one of them is a read of something that already exists — the stage history, the audit log, the lead columns, the settings. None of them stores its own answer, because an oversight screen with its own copy of the facts is a second copy of the thing it is meant to be watching. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: Overrides: the gates somebody walked past
search.text: A manager may pass a shut gate (switched by ), but never silently. Every override writes the stage-history row with the coded reason ( ) and the exact list of conditions still missing at that moment . The override log lists every move that carried a non-empty missing list, newest first, with who did it and under which app and level, and counts which condition is waived most often across the book. A system that refuses everything is defeated in a week by people recording the work after the event. The override exists so the rule survives contact with a Tuesday — and this log exists so that it does not become the ordinary way through. A condition that is waived again and again is either a rule that does not fit the work or a habit that needs a conversation; the count says which to look at.

search.heading: Audit and thresholds
search.text: - Audit pages through every audited lead action — stage moves, reassignments, verifications, priority, trash and restore — with the actor's hat. Keyset-paged, so an action added while you read never appears twice. - Thresholds lists every leads. and handset mbos.leads. setting with its value in force, whether it is still the shipped default, and who last changed it. It has no edit control. Settings are authored in the Admin Console, which validates against the setting's bounds, checks the whole set for consistency and writes an audit row; a second form doing three quarters of that would be a way to store a value the first would refuse.

search.heading: The Sales Manager desk
search.text: Scope is the seat, and nothing else. The CRM Sales Manager desk shows a lead only if its sales manager seat is the signed-in person . An administrator is not narrowed. A lead with an owner and no sales manager, or with neither, is on nobody's desk until somebody names a sales manager. The territory-based scope the rest of Lead Management uses is national for a manager with no region, which would show a CRM sales manager every lead in the company. The reporting line is not filled for field staff. The one thing the book reliably carries is the sales manager seat on each lead — so that is the scope, for reads and writes: the workspace is named on the request, so the read that draws a lead and the action that works it resolve the same answer. A lead you can see is a lead you can act on. Every live lead in the seat is loaded once (up to five pages of 200 — past that the desk says it is truncated) and sorted into six queues on the server from the real queue readers: verify prospect, qualification review, sample, order confirmation, overdue and nurture. The browser only counts and groups, so a tile and the list it opens can never disagree. The module is off by default even on a whole-CRM grant, and independent of any Sales Dashboard access: it is a job held through the CRM, granted a person at a time.

search.heading: Lost
search.text: Lost is a read of the same lead rows, filtered to those closed lost. The one fact it adds is which rung the lead was lost from , read from the closing stage-history row — the lead row itself only says lost . A lead lost before the history existed shows Not recorded rather than a guessed rung. The reason is the code from ; older leads carry free text and still read. It is scoped exactly like the working list — a lead you cannot see there cannot be seen here.

search.heading: Reopening
search.text: Reopening is not a move along a ladder — Lost is on none — so it has its own rule for where the lead comes back, which the dialog shows before you confirm: Lost from Comes back to A rung still on its ladder That rung A failed verification Prospect, to be verified again A rung its ladder no longer has, On hold, or nothing recorded The foot of its ladder The rung that makes it a customer, or beyond One rung below Nothing opens a gate and nothing promotes: from the rung it returns to, every ordinary gate applies. A reason from is required, and reopening from this screen needs the verify permission. The reopen is a stage-history row whose note begins Reopened from Lost .

search.heading: Trash and restore
search.text: Deleting moves leads to the trash with a sentence of reason. Only a lead can be trashed — an account we have billed is deactivated instead — and only one in your book. Deleted leads leave every list for every viewer. Trashing is a manager's; restoring is an administrator's.

search.heading: By rung
search.text: Counts every lead by ladder and rung, with the median days on the rung and the potential. Every rung the ladder has is drawn, even at zero — a funnel that omits empty rungs redraws itself every time somebody works it. Parked leads are counted beside the funnel, not in it.

search.heading: Cohort conversion
search.text: Measured by cohort, never this month over this month. Leads raised in a window are followed forward for days. Dividing this month's orders by this month's leads asks a lead raised on the 29th to have converted by the 31st, and mixes in conversions from leads raised months ago. Outcome Means Converted Reached the rung that puts it on the book Lost, or past its window Closed lost, or its window ran out without converting Not yet Still inside its window — counted, never divided No sales type Raised without a ladder; outside the cohort and said so The rate on this screen is converted ÷ (converted + lost or past its window) . With nothing decided yet the screen says Nothing has closed its window — a rate over zero decided leads is not a low rate, it is no rate.

search.heading: Sources and reasons
search.text: Sources groups lead sources by a fingerprint — case, punctuation and spacing folded — so "Website", "website" and "WEB SITE" show as one source spelled three ways. It deliberately does not guess that "Referral" and "Reference" are the same; that is a judgement for whoever merges them. Reasons tallies the coded reasons for Prospects, samples, losses and overrides, by salesman and by town, and counts moves that carried no code as uncoded so totals still add up.

search.heading: Who can do what
search.text: Screen Module Note Oversight Read-only Sales Manager desk Off by default; scope is the seat Lost Off by default; reopen needs verify Funnel & conversion Read-only

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Two conversion rates. AGENTS.md says the owner's cohort denominator is every lead in the cohort ; this screen divides by decided leads only ( lib/services/lead-funnel-service.ts tallyCohort ). The owner's Reports app and this screen can print different rates for the same window. - The oversight service says thresholds are authored in the Admin Console , which is right; /crm/settings now permanently redirects there ( src/app/crm/settings/page.tsx ), though the module and its guard remain.

Lead Management is one workspace mounted twice . The screens live in src/components/leads/pages/ and take a workspace prop ( "crm" or "sales" ); the CRM routes under src/app/crm/leads/ are thin files that pass workspace="crm" . The rules live in two pure engines — the ladder (what comes next) and the gates (may we) — and every stage move goes through one service function that writes an append-only transition row. Every block below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.heading: A stage move, end to end
search.text: advanceLeadStage — one lead, one rung. expectFrom is the optimistic lock: the row is re-read for update and a lead that moved since the screen drew it throws StageAlreadyMoved rather than being moved twice.

search.heading: The ladders
search.text: LEGACY LADDER is what leadSalesType === null means. Nothing backfills a sales type; a migration that guessed one would change which gates apply.

search.heading: Bands
search.text: lead-ladder.test.ts walks every value of the stage enum through bandOf , so a rung added without a band fails the build rather than a report. on hold returns null deliberately — count parked leads with isParked .

search.heading: Where a lead becomes a customer
search.text: The stage move promotes when the destination is at or past this rung. The order paths ask a different question — has the account ordered before — through one function: Path Where it converts CRM call with an order interaction-service.ts — spreads conversionColumns into the customer update when hasOrderedBefore Accounts approving an order order-approval-service.ts → convertIfNowQualified , outside the approval transaction Handset order actions/mbos.ts → convertLeadOnSecondOrder Stage move applyLeadStageMove — promoted sets kind , lead converted at , sales am id , clears lead manager id

search.heading: The gates
search.text: gateTo adds §24's next-action condition to every upward move on a real ladder (not the legacy one, not won , and not twice where the destination already asks for it). lost is always open — the reason is demanded by the action, not the engine.

search.heading: Deciding a move
search.text: The order of its checks matters: not on a funnel → same stage → leaving on hold (judged against parkedFromRung ) → down (needs lead.override and a reason) → off ladder → lost (needs a code from leads.lostReasons ) → prospect (needs a code from leads.prospectReasons ) → gate open → override (needs leads.allowManagerOverride , the capability, and a code from leads.overrideReasons ). leads.requireNextAction off lifts only the next action condition, by id.

search.heading: The stage history
search.text: Append-only. Nothing updates or deletes a transition row. A wrong move is corrected by another move. The record's history tab ( leadTransitions , keyset-paged on (at, id) ) and the Oversight overrides list both read this table.

search.heading: Bulk moves
search.text: LEAD BULK CAP is shared with the screen's Select all , so the button and the server cannot disagree about how many. lib/lead-bulk-stage.ts ( pickableLostReasons , bulkStagePayload ) shapes the bulk bar's request and is unit-tested.

search.heading: The Call Log hold
search.text: Suppression is a return value: the lead appears in the held-back strip with this sentence. Only the prospect / order reasons are stripped; reminders, payments and order status still list it.

search.heading: Scope and permissions
search.text: - Modules: guards the book and the record (a requireModule call for the workspace's own leads module inside the page body). Every other lead module guards its own folder. - Reads narrow through leadsVisible(managerScope()) . A telecaller sees their own leads and unowned leads no sales manager holds; managers see unowned leads too; the CRM Sales Manager workspace reads sales manager id only. - Writes ask requireCapability("lead.work") first, then assertLeadInScope : if the lead is on your list you may work it, otherwise the CRM's seat check answers.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A new rung goes in the ladder, the enum and the band map together. Add it to LeadStage and mbos lead stage (hand-written migration), to the right ladder array, and to bandOf . The band test fails until you do. Its conditions go in conditionsToEnter, keyed by destination. Read a stored value, not a tick. Write says as an instruction. The handset compiles this file, so no imports beyond lead-labels and lead-ladder . Never add a second path that writes lead stage. Every move — record, bulk, handset, calling desk conversion — goes through evaluateLeadStageMove + applyLeadStageMove . A direct update customers set lead stage skips the gate, the transition row and the timeline. Reason lists are settings. A new coded list is a structured leads. key in registry.ts with a Config type entry, defaulted from lead-labels.ts . Store the code; resolve the label with labelOf . Conversion stays in lead-conversion-service. If a new order path appears, call convertLeadOnSecondOrder from it. Count orders with orderCountsSql , never status < 'cancelled' .

All Leads is the lead book: every shop that has not become a customer yet, the rung of the ladder it is standing on, and what it is waiting for before it can climb. You use it to find the lead you need, see what is owed on it today, and move it forward — or, if it is dead, close it with a reason. The same screens are open to the field sales team on the Sales Dashboard. What you see here in the CRM is your own book (leads you own, plus unowned leads nobody has taken). A manager sees the team's. The numbers on this page — how many visits, how many days — are the settings your CRM is using right now, read live. If a manager changes one, this page changes with it.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: All Leads, for a telecaller working their own book. Leads Export 12 archived leads All My leads Today's actions Overdue Nobody is working these On hold Suspect decisions Handovers My leads. 18 Today's actions. 4 Overdue. 2 New suspects. 9 In sample. 3 Lost (30 days). 5 3 leads nobody has touched in 14 days State Owner Sales type Stage Next …

search.heading: Other tabs of All Leads
search.text: Tab What it shows List The screen above. Board The same leads drawn as columns, one per rung, so you can see where the book is bunching. Dashboard Seven queues across the funnel — what is waiting on somebody — each opening the list behind it. Under the table, Other desks links to the lead screens that have left the sidebar (Qualification, Samples & trials, Commercial, Next actions…), but only the ones you have been given.

search.heading: The views
search.text: View What it lists All Every active lead in your book. My leads Leads where you hold a seat: you own it, you coordinate it as lead manager, or its paperwork is yours. Today's actions A next action falling due today, or a parked lead whose day has come. Overdue Past its day, with nobody having answered it. Nobody is working these Active leads with no next action at all, then leads whose next action has gone past. On hold Parked leads, by the day each comes back — those with no day named first. Suspect decisions Suspects visited at least times and still undecided. Handovers Converted accounts with nobody named yet to run the relationship. Distributors & third-party Who sells our goods on, and the shops the goods go to. Tiles add three more: New suspects , Prospects , In sample , Negotiations , Expected orders (a day and a size somebody wrote down) and Lost (30 days) .

search.heading: The order of the rows
search.text: The list is ordered by what is owed soonest : the earliest of the next action, a follow-up date or a parked lead's return date. Leads with nothing owed come after, longest-quiet first. The manager's priority badge does not change the order — use the Priority filter to see the high ones.

search.heading: The Next column
search.text: It says It means A date and an action Somebody owes this lead something on that day. Overdue N days The day has gone and nobody has answered it. Nothing owed No next action. On an active lead this is the problem the "Nobody is working these" view exists to show.

search.heading: Lead and customer: which is which
search.text: A lead is an account that has not yet become a customer. A customer is on the book. A lead becomes a customer on its second order. One order from a shop that has just finished a trial is still a lead. When a second approved order lands, the account becomes a customer — automatically, whether the order came from a call or from a salesman's handset. Moving a lead up to the 2nd order rung does the same. When it converts you will see "… is on the book — they are a customer from today." The person who owned the lead becomes its sales account manager.

search.heading: The three ladders
search.text: Every lead has a sales type , asked first when it is raised. The sales type decides which rungs it climbs. Sales type Who gets the bill What the ladder is working towards Direct customer We bill them Their first order, then the second that makes them a customer Third-party customer A distributor bills them; the goods come to them The same, but somebody else invoices Distributor (no longer offered for new leads) They buy from us and sell on Appointing them as a distributor Not set — Leads raised before the funnel existed climb the old six rungs

search.heading: Direct customer
search.text: Direct customer — Mahek to the shop.

search.heading: Third-party customer
search.text: The same climb without Sample received — the sample goes through the distributor. Before a sample can go out you must say which distributor bills this shop . Third-party customer — Mahek to a distributor to the shop.

search.heading: Distributor (retired for new leads)
search.text: Leads already on this ladder keep their place and can still move. New leads cannot be started on it, and the list shows a note saying the distributor ladder is closed. Distributor — appointing one.

search.heading: No sales type (older leads)
search.text: The original six rungs. Lost can be reached from any rung on any ladder. On hold is a pause, not a rung — see below.

search.heading: Moving a lead forward
search.text: Open the lead. Press its name. The Overview tab starts with What happens next — the next rung, and either a Move to … button or the list of what it is still waiting for. Read what is missing. If the gate is shut you see each missing condition as an instruction, for example "How many litres a month do they use?" or "Your sales manager must check this customer first" . Many come with a link to the tab where you fix it. Do the work, then move it. When nothing is missing, press Move to … . The move is written to the stage history with your name. Always leave a next action. On a lead with a sales type, every move up needs what happens next, on which day, and who will do it . A lead with nobody owing it anything is the thing this rule exists to stop. You cannot jump rungs, and you cannot move a lead down its ladder yourself — that is a manager's, and needs a reason.

search.heading: What each rung asks for
search.text: To enter You need Prospect What kind of business, litres a month, the brand they use now, which of our products they need, who to ask for, a next action, and a reason why it is worth following (one of a fixed list) Qualification Your sales manager's verification call has been made and passed Sample / trial The eight qualification answers (GST, what they use it on, the trial plan, who decides/orders/pays, price and credit, delivery, still willing to test, a dated next step), your sales manager's review marked verified , the figures still current, and — for a third-party shop — a distributor named Sample received The sample has been sent Sample review They have actually got it Negotiation A sample was sent, their feedback is written down, and the trial was approved 1st order A date they expect to order, and an order placed Delivery The goods have reached them Payment Accounts have seen the money in the bank 2nd order / Customer A second order The Intake & qualification and Samples pages explain those rungs in detail.

search.heading: When a manager moves a lead anyway
search.text: A manager can pass a shut gate. They press Move it anyway , see the list of conditions not met, and must choose why — for example "It was done. Written down later" or "Customer will not wait" . The override is recorded with exactly what was missing, and appears on the Oversight screen.

search.heading: Closing a lead as lost
search.text: Choose Lost and pick a reason: price, quality, stayed with another brand, they do not need it, credit terms, delivery or service, not interested, wrong lead, check call failed, clash with a distributor or area, or other. A lost lead's next action is cleared and its follow-up tasks are cancelled.

search.heading: Putting a lead on hold
search.text: On hold is for a lead that is real but not moving — a shutdown, a budget quarter, the decision maker away. You must give: - why it stopped (one of six reasons; Other needs words), - the day it comes back , and - what happens when it does . It then waits in the On hold view. Resuming it moves it back to a named rung through the same gate.

search.heading: Doing things to many leads at once
search.text: Tick leads (or select everything the filter found, up to 200) and the bulk bar offers: Action What happens Change stage Each lead goes through its own gate. Leads missing a condition do not move and come back named, with what they are waiting on. Moving to Lost asks for one reason for all of them. Change the owner Managers who can assign. Each new owner gets one message naming how many. Chase the owners One nudge per owner. Unowned leads are named back to you. Archive them Needs a sentence; every owner losing a lead gets it. Delete them — move to trash Managers only. They leave every screen; an administrator can restore them.

search.heading: Leads and your Call Log
search.text: A lead that has a sales type is being worked on the funnel, so the Call Log does not ring it for a first order or a reorder — that would be two people chasing one shop. It appears in the Call Log's held-back strip as "On the sales team's lead funnel (Direct customer) - they are asking for the order, so the Call Log does not" . Reminders, money owed and order status still reach the Call Log.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: A lead I expected is not in my list.. In the CRM you see leads you own and unowned leads nobody has claimed. A lead owned by somebody else, or held by a sales manager, is not in your book. Archived and deleted leads are not on the working list either — try the archived link at the top. The Move button is grey.. Either there is no rung above this one, or the gate is shut — the conditions it is waiting for are listed above the button. A grey button with a list is "not yet", not "not allowed". It says 'Prospect is not a rung on this lead's ladder'.. The lead has no sales type, or its sales type has a different ladder. Set the sales type on the record first. The customer ordered once. Why is it still a lead?. A first order is the tail of the trial. The account becomes a customer on its second approved order. Why can I not choose Distributor when raising a lead?. That ladder has been retired for new leads. Existing distributor leads still work. Bulk 'Change stage' moved only some of them.. Each lead goes through its own gate. The message names the ones that did not move and why.

Lead Management answers one question for the business: is this shop worth more of our time, and what has to be true before it gets it? Every lead stands on one rung of a ladder, and it climbs only when the work behind the next rung has actually been done. This tab explains the ladders, the gates between the rungs, who may pass a shut gate, and why each rule is the shape it is. The screens are shared between the CRM ( /crm/leads ) and the Sales Dashboard ( /sales/leads ). They are one set of screens mounted twice, with the same rules on both. What differs is whose leads you see , explained in Who sees which leads. Every value quoted on this page is the one your CRM is using right now. Amber means a manager has changed it from the shipped default.

search.heading: Three ways to sell, three ladders
search.text: Mahek sells three ways, and they are not the same job. A direct customer is worked towards a first order we invoice. A third-party customer is worked towards an order a distributor invoices. A distributor is worked towards an appointment. So every lead carries a sales type , and the sales type picks the ladder. One list of rungs for all three would put "Distributor agreement" on a paint shop's funnel and "Sample review" on a distributor's, and every screen would need its own idea of which rungs to hide. Three ladders means each lead only ever sees rungs that mean something for it. Direct customer — Mahek to the shop. Third-party customer — the same climb, minus Sample received. The third-party ladder drops Sample received because the sample goes through the distributor: the date we can stand behind is the review, not the arrival. Distributor — appointing one (no longer offered for new leads). The distributor ladder has no sample rungs at all. What replaces the trial is two approvals — a sales manager may recommend a distributor and may not appoint one. See Commercial and distributor appointments. New leads can no longer be raised on this ladder; leads already on it keep climbing.

search.heading: Leads with no sales type climb the original six rungs
search.text: The legacy ladder — a lead with no sales type. Nothing backfills a sales type. A lead raised before the funnel existed has no sales type, and it carries on climbing the six rungs it was always on. Nobody guessed which of the three ladders each one "really" belonged to. The ladder decides which gates apply. A wrong guess would not just mislabel a record — it would block the person working it behind conditions that were never asked of that lead. Leaving the old book alone is the only reason the funnel could ship without moving a single row.

search.heading: Two states that are not rungs
search.text: - Lost is reachable from every rung of every ladder, and always needs a coded reason. - On hold is a pause. It takes the place of the rung while the lead is parked, so the rung it was parked from is remembered in the stage history. Coming back is a move to a named rung, through that rung's gate as normal. Why On hold is not Lost. Folding a stalled lead into Lost made every lead that was waiting for a plant shutdown or a budget quarter look dead, and the staleness sweep then archived real prospects. A parked lead is alive, so it keeps its place and says when it comes back.

search.heading: The four funnel bands
search.text: Owner reports and the funnel screen do not count leads rung by rung. They count four bands , and every rung on every ladder maps onto one: Band Rungs that fall in it New New, Suspect Contacted Contacted, Prospect Qualified Qualified, Qualification, Sample / trial, Sample received, Sample review, Management review Negotiation Negotiation, Commercial discussion, Distributor approval, Distributor agreement, 1st order, Delivery, Payment, 2nd order, Initial stock order (no band) Won, Lost, Customer, Active distributor — they have left the funnel. On hold — it cannot be placed without reading its history When seventeen new rungs arrived, a funnel counting by rung would have dropped every lead on a new rung out of every report — a pipeline that silently shrinks as the team works it. The band map is why adding rungs moved no figure. A parked lead has no band because its band is genuinely unknown; screens count parked leads separately rather than guess.

search.heading: The gates: no lead moves because somebody pressed a button
search.text: Every rung has conditions to enter it . A move is allowed when all of them are met; otherwise the screen lists exactly what is missing, written as instructions ( "How many litres a month do they use?" , "Your sales manager must check this customer first" ). A refusal that does not say what is missing teaches somebody to press the button again rather than to do the work. And a checklist that can be completed without answering anything is a checklist people learn to complete — so where a condition has a real field (litres, product, competitor, GST), the gate reads the value , never a tick beside it. The same rules run in three places: the handset draws the next rung disabled with the missing list underneath, the server refuses on the same rules before it writes, and the console shows a manager what a lead is stuck behind. They are one piece of code, so they cannot disagree. To enter What has to be true Prospect What kind of business; litres a month; the brand they use now; which of our products they need; who to ask for; a next action; and a coded reason it is worth pursuing Qualification The sales manager's verification has been made Sample / trial The eight qualification answers (GST validated by the sales manager, application, trial plan, who decides / orders / pays, price and credit, delivery, still willing to test, a dated next step); the figures confirmed recently; the sales manager's qualification review marked verified; for a third-party shop, the distributor who bills it Sample received The sample has been sent Sample review The shop has confirmed it arrived Negotiation A sample was sent, feedback was written down, and the trial was approved 1st order An expected order date, and an order placed Delivery The goods reached them Payment Accounts confirmed the money in the bank 2nd order / Customer A second order Management review (distributor) The distributor profile: GST, PAN, address, network, territory, warehouse, commitments and the rest Commercial discussion The sales manager recommended them Distributor approval Discount, credit limit and area agreed; management approved Distributor agreement The signed agreement is on file Initial stock order The stock order they promised has been placed The intake and qualification rungs are detailed on Intake and qualification; the sample rungs on Samples. A next action is owed on every upward move (§24). On any

search.heading: Passing a shut gate: the manager's override
search.text: A manager may move a lead even though conditions are missing. They must pick a reason from a coded list, and the move is recorded as overridden together with exactly which conditions were still missing . A system that refuses everything is defeated in a week by people recording work after the event — and then the record says the process was followed when it was not, which is worse than an open gate. So the gate can be passed, but never silently: the Oversight screen lists every override with its reason and its missing list. A team that would rather be stuck can switch overrides off.

search.heading: Every move is a row, and rows are never edited
search.text: Each stage change writes one row to the stage history : from, to, the ladder, whether it passed, was overridden or was reverted, the reason code, the note, the missing conditions, who did it and under which app and level. Append-only. A move recorded wrongly is corrected by a further move, never by editing the old one. The history records what somebody decided on a day; rewriting it destroys the question rather than answering it. The record's timeline and the customer's shared history are drawn from these rows. A move also stamps the lead's stage since and last activity dates, writes any next action it carried, and — for Lost — clears the next action and cancels the open follow-up tasks chasing the lead (a closed lead owes nobody anything further).

search.heading: Reasons are codes, never labels
search.text: Why a Suspect became a Prospect, why the customer wants a trial, why a lead was lost, why it is on hold, why a manager overrode a gate — each is picked from a coded list in configuration: The lists are configuration so a manager can reword one without a deploy, and codes are stored so a reworded label never breaks an old row. It is also what makes "how many did we lose on credit terms this quarter" a question somebody can ask rather than a search through free text. Where the code is Other , words are required.

search.heading: Moving many leads at once
search.text: The bulk bar on All Leads moves a selection to one rung — up to the same cap the screen offers for Select all . There is no second path : each lead is sent through the same gate, one at a time, exactly as if it had been moved from its own record. - Leads whose gate is shut do not move , and come back named with the gate's own sentence ( "3 did not move: Customer A — …" ). - A move to Lost asks for one reason for the whole selection. - A lead you cannot reach is never named in the refusal. A bulk button is the most tempting place in a product to quietly skip the checklist on twenty leads at once. Running each lead through its own gate means the rule holds even here. The moves run one after another rather than together so a busy database cannot leave half a batch written with nobody able to say which half.

search.heading: Lead and customer: when the word changes
search.text: An account is either a lead or a customer ( kind ). The code converts a lead to a customer on its second counting order — an order that is not declined or cancelled, judged by the same definition every money report uses. The second order converts — on every path. 1. A call logged in the CRM with an order, when the account has ordered before. 2. Accounts approving an order , when the account has ordered before — so a shop whose first order was still waiting for approval is not left a lead until a third. 3. An order from the handset , by the same rule. 4. A stage move to 2nd order (or, for a distributor, to Distributor approval), through the gate. On conversion the account becomes a customer, its converted date is set, and the person who owned the lead becomes its sales account manager . The back-office seat is left for somebody to decide. A first order from a shop that has just finished a trial is a few cans to try in their own booth — the tail of the trial, not the start of a relationship, and it often does not repeat. Counting it as a customer inflated every conversion figure with shops that ordered once and were never heard from again. A distributor is not held to this: there is no trial order in an appointment, and they are invoiced from approval.

search.heading: Working leads are held back from the Call Log
search.text: A lead that has a sales type is being worked on the funnel. The Call Log does not prospect it for a first order or chase a reorder, because that would be two people chasing one shop with neither knowing about the other. It is not dropped silently: it appears in the Call Log's held-back strip with the sentence "On the sales team's lead funnel (Direct customer) - they are asking for the order, so the Call Log does not" . Reminders, money owed and order-status calls still come through. A lead with no sales type is prospected as before. See the Call Log.

search.heading: Who sees which leads
search.text: Where What a telecaller sees What a manager sees CRM /crm/leads Leads they own, plus leads nobody owns that no sales manager has taken Their team's leads, plus every unowned lead — managers assign, so they must see what nobody holds Sales Dashboard /sales/leads — (telecallers are redirected out of /sales ) Leads in their territory, plus every unowned lead CRM Sales Manager desk — Only leads where they are the named sales manager Leads in the trash are on nobody's list. Who may act on a lead follows the same rule as who sees it: if it is on your list, you may work it. Every write still needs the lead.work permission, which every associate holds — a funnel only a manager can advance is a funnel nobody updates.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - AGENTS.md still says a lead becomes a customer on the first order. Its "§22" section describes kind flipping at the first order. The code converts on the second, everywhere ( lead-ladder.ts promotesToCustomerAt , lead-conversion-service.ts ). This page documents the code. - The conversion service names two callers; there are four paths. Its header says "the CRM's interaction save and the handset's order handler", but order approval ( order-approval-service.ts ) and the stage move ( lead-service.ts applyLeadStageMove ) also convert, and the interaction save spreads conversionColumns rather than calling the shared function. - Two settings for the Suspect visit cap. leads.suspectMaxVisits is retired and no longer read; the live cap is mbos.leads.maxSuspectVisits . The old key still appears on the settings list.

Opportunities are rows in call opportunities , inserted by saveInteraction inside the call's transaction and worked through opportunity-service.ts . The screen is a server page reading listOpportunities() and a client screen that calls setOpportunityStatusAction . lib/engines/opportunity.ts is not this feature. It is the pure arithmetic for a shop's estimated potential against its current sales ( opportunity , annualise ) used by the field product. The call-opportunity worklist has no engine.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: Keep it off customers.kind. An opportunity must never promote or demote an account. If a won opportunity should create something, create an order or a reminder through their own services. Add a status to the constant and the screen together. OPPORTUNITY STATUSES , STATUS LABEL , STATUS TONE . The column is text, so the database will not refuse a typo — the constant is the only guard. Page in SQL before the list outgrows 500. Move the counts to a count( ) / sum query so the cards describe every opportunity, not the loaded page.

An opportunity is something a customer said on a call that they might buy — "we may need PU sealer next month", "send me a rate for 20-litre thinner". Opportunities is the list of those, with who is expected to follow each one up, so that what a call turned up is worked rather than forgotten on the customer's timeline. An opportunity is not a lead. It can be on a customer who has bought from us for years.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: Opportunities, on the Being worked tab. Opportunities Being worked. 7 Past their expected day. 2 Estimated value open. ₹1,85,000 Won. 3 Customer A Open Past its expected day PU Sealer · about 20 cans a month · ₹40,000 · expected 5 Aug They rang about a price · Owner · logged by Telecaller A on 1 Aug Start working it Won Lost Customer B Being worked Nano Thinner – 20 Liter (Loose) · expected 22 Aug They rang about an order · logged by Telecaller B on 9 Aug · for Telecaller A "Sent the rate, waiting for their purchase person" Won Lost

search.heading: Where opportunities come from
search.text: Opportunities are raised from the call panel, when somebody answers Yes to: Did this call turn up a sales opportunity? Field Required Example Product Yes What they might buy Estimated quantity No About 20 cans a month Estimated value No In rupees Expected order date No Must be today or later The question is asked on every call the customer made to us . On a call we made, it appears only when the call assistant heard a "maybe" in your notes and filled it in for you to check. Answering No is recorded too, so a manager can tell "nobody asked" from "asked, and there was nothing". An opportunity lands on the list of the person whose book the account is in , not necessarily whoever took the call. If that is somebody else, they get a notification: A call turned up an opportunity on your account .

search.heading: Working one
search.text: Open Being worked. Everything open or being worked, newest first. Check Past due first — the expected order day has gone. Start working it. Moves it from Open to Being worked , so the team can see somebody has picked it up. Close it as Won or Lost. Won asks What came of it? (optional) . Lost asks Why was it lost? — and will not save without an answer, because the next call to that customer needs it. Reopen if you closed it by mistake. A won or lost opportunity shows Reopen . The note written when it was last worked is kept.

search.heading: Statuses
search.text: Status Badge Means Open Open Raised on a call, nobody has picked it up In progress Being worked Somebody is following it up Won Won It turned into business — your judgement, nothing is worked out from their orders Lost Lost It did not, and the reason is on the card Won is what you say, not what the system checks. Marking an opportunity won does not look for an order. Mark it won when it became business, and say so in the note.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Is an opportunity the same as a lead?. No. A lead is an account that has never ordered and is worked in Lead Management. An opportunity is one thing a customer — new or old — might buy, raised from a single call. Why did the opportunity box not appear on my call?. It is asked on calls the customer made to us. On a call we made, it only appears if the call assistant picked up a possible sale in your notes. I raised one and it says 'for' somebody else.. It went to the person whose book the account is in. You can still see it and work it, because you raised it. Can I change the product or the value?. Not from this screen. Write what changed in the note when you close it. Does Lost stop the customer being called?. No. It only closes the opportunity. The Call Log decides calls from the customer's own buying pattern.

An opportunity is the CRM's record of something a call turned up that a customer may buy . It used to be a line on the customer's timeline and nothing else, which meant whether anything came of it depended on somebody happening to read that account. The Opportunities screen turns the same record into a worklist: an owner, a status, and a sentence about what came of it.

search.heading: Deliberately not a lead
search.text: An opportunity never changes what an account is. A lead in MahekOne is an account that has never ordered , and about thirty parts of the product — the Call Log's prospect cadence, sales attribution, the buying cycle, the owner's funnel — are built on exactly that. An opportunity spotted on a call with a four-year customer cannot be a lead without making every one of them wrong. So an opportunity is a separate record; where the account already is a lead, it is already in Lead Management and the opportunity simply names what this call turned up.

search.heading: How one is raised
search.text: From a call to the list. Three answers, kept apart. Nobody asked , asked and No , and asked and Yes are three different facts about a call. A No used to leave no trace and read as a call nobody asked on. A No sent together with an opportunity is a contradiction and the save refuses it, as it refuses an opportunity on an Order Received (nobody was on the phone to ask). It goes to whoever will be asked about the account. The owner is the person whose book the account is in — the same single definition every list and every target reads — falling back to whoever took the call. A call taken by one telecaller on another's customer lands on the right list, with a notification. The estimated value is typed in whole rupees and stored in paise. No value and zero are different answers: no value is nobody having put a figure on it; zero would read as an opportunity judged worthless. Estimated value open adds up only the opportunities that have one.

search.heading: Who sees a row
search.text: The owner's people, plus whoever raised it. A row is visible to the people in scope for its owner , and to the people in scope for whoever logged the call . The telecaller who raised an opportunity is never left unable to see what became of it. A telecaller sees their own; a manager sees their team's. Anybody who can see a row can work it. Asking about a row you cannot see answers That opportunity is not on your list — the same as one that does not exist, so the screen cannot be used to find out what is on somebody else's.

search.heading: Statuses
search.text: An opportunity's life. Rule Why Lost needs a sentence Nobody will look again, and the next call to the account needs to know why. Won takes an optional note , and is the person's judgement Nothing compares it with the customer's orders; the dialog says so. Reopening is always allowed and clears the closing mark Closing something by mistake must never be harder to undo than to do. A reopen keeps the old note What was written the last time it was worked is still worth reading. Every change is audited opportunity.status , with before and after.

search.heading: Past its expected day
search.text: An opportunity that is open or being worked and whose expected order date has passed is past due : it gets a red badge, its own tab, and a count at the top. Nothing chases it automatically — no reminder is created and the Call Log does not read it.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - The list is the newest 500. The counts and Estimated value open are computed over those 500, not over every opportunity in scope. - The team view is drawn for anybody who manages any app , not only a manager in the CRM — the screen uses the widest level held anywhere to decide whether to show whose each row is. - The audit row does not record which hat allowed the change , unlike other audited actions. - An opportunity cannot be reassigned or edited. Its owner is set once, when the call is saved; if the account changes hands, the opportunity stays with the old owner. - Past due raises nothing. No reminder, no notification and no Call Log reason follow an opportunity whose day has gone.

Outstanding answers who owes us money, and for what . It is one row per customer — what they owe, how old the oldest of it is — and every row opens to show the bills behind the figure. Use it to decide who to chase and to have the bill numbers in front of you when you do. It covers every open bill, whatever financial year it is from , because the oldest debt on an account is usually last year's.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: Outstanding, one customer opened. Outstanding Export Outstanding. ₹9,40,000 · 38 customers Past due. ₹6,10,000 · 24 past a due date Not stated. ₹1,20,000 · 5 customers · nothing recorded either way Past due only Expand this page Open record WhatsApp

search.heading: Chasing from this screen
search.text: Sort by Oldest debt. The customer whose debt is oldest is usually the one closest to going bad. Open the row. The bills are listed with what is owed first, oldest due date first — the bill that has to clear before the customer leaves the collections list is at the top. Chase. WhatsApp opens a reminder for this customer. To log a call, use Payment Follow-up, which is where calls are recorded and dated.

search.heading: What each figure and word means
search.text: On the screen Means Outstanding What the customer owes on bills that are stated as owed, after confirmed payments Open bills How many stated bills still have a balance Oldest Days past the due date of their oldest stated bill, or Within terms N disputed Bills the customer has disputed — a billing complaint is open Not stated Bills with a balance that are not counted as owed — see below Status: Nd overdue Nothing paid, N days past due Status: Part paid · Nd late Something paid, the rest N days past due Status: Partly paid Something paid, the rest not yet due Status: Open Nothing paid, not yet due Status: Disputed Disputed Status: Not stated Not counted as owed Only confirmed money reduces a balance. A payment a customer says they made, or that is waiting for accounts, does not reduce what is shown here. The balance moves when accounts confirm the money.

search.heading: "Not stated" bills
search.text: Some bills are shown with their balance but not added up as debt. They are listed under the customer, counted in their own column and total, and drawn as Not stated rather than as an amount owed. Today these are bills the order sheet's Payment Status tab marks as received but for which no receipt has been confirmed — the office has written down that the money came, so the bill is not chased, and accounts still have to confirm it. A customer whose only open bills are not stated sorts below everybody who owes something.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Why is a bill from last year here?. Outstanding is not cut by financial year. An unpaid bill from last year is still owed, and is usually the first one to chase. The Sales Bills screen is the one cut by year. The customer paid yesterday. Why do they still owe the full amount?. The payment is reported or on hold with accounts. It reduces the balance when accounts confirm it. What is the difference between this and Payment Follow-up?. Outstanding shows everybody who owes anything. Payment Follow-up is today's work: who to message or call today, and why some are being left alone. Why does this figure match the Accounts app?. It is the same reading in both apps, through the same scope. A customer cannot be quoted two balances. Export gave me more customers than the page shows.. Export writes everybody your filters match, not the page. The screen shows 25 at a time.

The bill ledger answers what did we bill . Outstanding answers the question a telecaller and an accounts clerk both start their day with: who owes us money, and against what . One row per customer; the bills behind the figure on the same row, because the follow-up to "how much" is always "against which bills", and making somebody move to another screen for it is what makes a chase call go quiet.

search.heading: What is counted
search.text: From bills to a row. Paid means confirmed. A bill's paid amount is rebuilt from confirmed receipts only. Reported and held money, and money accounts rejected, leave the balance where it was. A bill nobody has stated is shown, counted and never added up. A bill with payment position unstated is not debt, so it stays out of the outstanding figure exactly as the customer's stored outstanding leaves it out. It is still listed, given its own column, its own total and a sentence, and its balance is drawn as "Not stated" rather than as a figure. Hiding such a bill would make a bill that is open on the ledger and absent here read as a screen that lost it. Adding it would put money we have a record of receiving on a collections list. Rendering an unknown beside real balances is the original mistake in different clothes. Past due means a stated bill past its due date. An unstated bill cannot make somebody overdue. The due date is the bill's own, or the bill date plus the credit period — the order's term, then the customer's, then days.

search.heading: Not cut by financial year
search.text: The Sales Bills ledger is cut by financial year because ten thousand bills across three years is not a list anybody scrolls. Outstanding deliberately is not: the oldest debt on an account is usually last year's, and that is the first row anybody works.

search.heading: One reading, two apps
search.text: The CRM and Accounts read the same function through the same scope. Both apps' Outstanding screens are built from one paged read and one grouping, so the two can never quote a customer two different balances. What differs is where a name leads: the CRM opens the customer record and WhatsApp, where a chase happens; Accounts opens the customer's account statement. The customer's balance here is also the same figure as customers.outstanding on every other screen — both count stated bills only, after confirmed payments.

search.heading: Paging, sorting and the totals
search.text: - The page shows 25 customers; the totals above it describe every customer the search and past-due filter match, counted in the database, not the page. - Sorting is done in the database with a final tie-break on the customer, so a customer never appears on two pages or on none. - Most owed is: what is owed, then what is merely not stated, then name. Somebody who owes nothing stated is work of a different kind — somebody has to go and state those bills — not work of no kind, so they sort below, not out. - Inside a row, stated bills come first, oldest due date first.

search.heading: Aging
search.text: The Oldest column is coloured by the aging band of the customer's oldest stated bill. Bands are , the same bands the Sales Bills ledger and Payment Follow-up use.

search.heading: Who sees what
search.text: A telecaller sees the customers in their own book; a manager on team scope sees their team's. The book is the single definition every CRM list uses, including the back-office seat — an account somebody works as back office is on their list.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: 'Not stated' now means 'the sheet says received'. The screen's words — nothing recorded either way , bills nobody has spoken for — describe the old rule, under which every bill the order sheet imported was neither paid nor owed until a person spoke. In October 2026 that was reversed: a sheet bill now lands owed from its due date, and is held not stated only when the Payment Status tab says Received . The figures are right; the sentences describe a different set of bills. - Export ignores the sort and the scope check of the screen's module. The file is written in "most owed" order whatever sort was chosen, and the export address belongs to the Accounts app: it checks only that the reader holds the CRM or Accounts, not that they were given the Outstanding screen or the right to export customers. - Two screens, not one. The CRM and Accounts render separate screen components over the same read; they agree on figures today but can drift in what they show.

The CRM is a Next.js App Router subtree at src/app/crm . One layout gates the app and builds the shell; one layout per module gates each screen; every page is a server component that calls reads from lib/queries.ts or a lib/services/ file and hands plain data to a client screen, and every button calls a server action in lib/actions/ that delegates to the same services. Pure rules live in lib/engines/ and never touch the database.

The CRM is where the office team rings customers, takes orders over the phone, chases money that is owed, and keeps a record of every conversation. It is one app inside MahekOne: you sign in once, and if the CRM is the only app you have been given, you land straight in it. This page is the map. It tells you who the CRM is for, what a normal day looks like, what every screen in the sidebar is for, and what the words the CRM uses actually mean. Each screen has its own page with the details — follow the links.

search.heading: Who uses the CRM
search.text: Telecaller. Rings customers from the Call Log every day, logs what happened on each call, takes orders, sets callbacks and chases payments. Sees only their own book of customers. Manager. Runs a team of telecallers. Sees the whole team by default and can switch to their own book. Reads the team overview, sets targets, decides close/reopen requests and can close a reminder by hand. Accounts. The ledger desk mostly works in the Accounts app. Somebody on that desk who has also been given the CRM reads customers, bills and outstanding here, and approves orders back in Accounts. What you can open inside the CRM is decided by your manager on the Access screen. If a screen in this guide is missing from your sidebar, you have not been given it — ask your manager.

search.heading: A telecaller's day
search.text: Open the Dashboard. It greets you by name and shows the shape of your day as five steps: Work the queue → Close reminders → Chase payments → Clear complaints → Submit EOD . Each step is ticked when there is nothing left in it. Press Start calling to begin. See Dashboard. Work the Call Log from the top. The Call Log lists today's customers in the order you should ring them, each with the reason. Call, log what happened, move to the next row. Keep your promises. Any callback you promised shows on Reminders and jumps to the top of the Call Log on the day it is due. Making the call closes it. Chase money. Payment Follow-up is the collections list: who owes money, how late, and what was last promised. Deal with complaints. Open Complaints and mention any open complaint before anything else on the next call to that customer. Submit your EOD report. At the end of the day, the EOD Report adds up what you did. It will not let you submit while a reminder due today or earlier is still open.

search.heading: A manager's day
search.text: Read the team overview. The Dashboard shows Team overview instead of a greeting: today's red flags, the team's calls, orders booked, outstanding, and a comparison table of every telecaller. Switch the period to Yesterday, This week or This month. Look for what is stuck. Overdue reminders by telecaller (on Reminders), opportunities past their expected day (on Opportunities), and Unassigned rows on the team Call Log. Decide what is waiting for you. Requests to close or reopen an account are on Close/Reopen. Monthly targets are on Monthly Targets. Switch between team and your own book. The My book / Team switch in the header changes every list in the CRM at once. It is a view, not a permission — it never lets anyone see more than they are allowed.

search.heading: How the screens fit together
search.text: Almost everything in the CRM starts with a call and ends with the CRM telling you when that customer comes back. The main loop of the CRM. A few things to know about this loop: - An order you take is not yet a sale. It waits for the accounts desk to approve it. Your Dashboard counts it as taken straight away; the money only counts once it is approved. - A payment the customer says they made is not yet money. It waits for accounts to find it in the bank. Until then the customer is left alone for a few days rather than chased. - Every save tells you when the customer comes back. That sentence is kept on the call, so Call History can show you later what you were told.

search.text: Link The number means Reminders Reminders due today or overdue that are still open. Complaints Complaints still open, in progress, or waiting on the customer. Close/Reopen Requests nobody has decided yet. All Leads Leads past the day something was owed (red), otherwise leads with something due today.

search.heading: Words the CRM uses
search.text: Word What it means Book The customers that are yours. A lead belongs to whoever owns it; a customer belongs to their sales account manager. Every list in the CRM is cut to a book. Scope Whose book you are looking at — your book or the whole team . A telecaller is always on their own book. A manager can switch. Held back A customer the Call Log deliberately left off today's list. The held-back strip says why for each one — nobody disappears silently. Buying cycle How many days a customer usually goes between orders, worked out from their own approved orders. The Call Log times its calls from it. Stock check A call partway through a customer's buying cycle to ask what is left on the shelf. Stage floor On a late payment, the lowest follow-up stage a customer can be at. A customer who refuses to commit or cannot be reached is kept at a higher stage even if their bill dates alone would put them lower. Reported money A payment the customer says they made. It stops the chasing for a few days but does not reduce what they owe. Confirmed money A payment accounts have found in the bank. Only this reduces outstanding. Lead An account that has never ordered. Customer An account we have invoiced — they have placed an order. Third-party customer A shop we deliver to but do not bill; a distributor buys from us and sells to them. The CRM never asks them for a first order. Reminder A promise somebody made to a customer — a callback, a payment to check, information to send. Opportunity Something a customer said on a call they might buy. It is not a lead. Next step The sentence you see after saving a call — Comes back to your Call Log on … — and the badge saying whether it is a promise or a scheduled date.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I cannot see a screen my colleague can see.. Your manager has given you a narrower set of screens. The Access screen decides it per person. Typing the address of a screen you were not given takes you to the first screen you do have. Why does my manager see more customers than I do?. A manager sees their whole team's books. A telecaller always sees only their own. The My book / Team switch is only drawn for managers. I took an order but my Dashboard says it is 'awaiting approval'.. Orders wait for the accounts desk to approve them. It counts as taken at once; it counts as money only once approved. The customer says they paid. Why do they still show as owing?. Money a customer reports is not counted until accounts confirm it reached the bank. Until then the customer is held back from chasing for a few days, and the screens say so. Where do I change a setting like how many days of quiet after an order?. Settings are changed by a manager in the Admin Console. The Help Center has a link for managers.

The CRM is one loop with many screens around it. A customer is put in front of a telecaller for a reason, the telecaller rings and logs what happened, the call produces work for somebody else — an order for accounts, a reminder for the telecaller, a complaint for a desk, a payment claim for the ledger — and the CRM then says when that customer comes back. Every screen in the sidebar is either a door into that loop or a view of what it produced. This tab explains the rules that hold the screens together: whose book a customer is in, what scope means, why some numbers count straight away and others only after accounts decide, and why every screen reads and writes the same way.

search.heading: The main loop
search.text: How the screens feed each other. Three things are true at every box in this picture. A save is one transaction. Saving a call writes the call, any order, reminder, complaint and opportunity it produced, the timeline entries and the customer's rolled-up dates together, or not at all. The collections panel does the same for its attempt, promise, receipt, complaint and stage floor. A half-saved call leaves a customer's record describing something that never happened. Evidence closes a promise, not a button. A reminder is closed by the call that got through, the order that was taken, or the money accounts confirmed. Closing one by hand is a capability ( reminder.close ) and is recorded as that person's decision. See Reminders. Every save says what happens next, and the sentence is kept. After the work is written, the CRM asks the Call Log engine when this customer next appears and stores the answer on the call. It is a record of what the telecaller was told on that day, never rebuilt. Call History and the Customers list both show it.

search.heading: Two questions about every order and every rupee
search.text: Did the customer say yes?. True the moment the telecaller saves. An order taken stops the Call Log chasing the customer for one; a payment reported stops collections ringing them for a few days. The dashboard counts orders taken straight away. Did the business get it?. True only after accounts decide. Approved orders are what EOD value, targets, the buying cycle and the product history count. Confirmed receipts are the only money that reduces a bill, outstanding, aging and the slow-payer flag. Only confirmed money moves the ledger. A payment a customer says they made is a reported receipt. It is written down with the bills it would settle, but paid amount on a bill is rebuilt from confirmed receipts only, and a customer's outstanding is rebuilt from bills. Until accounts find the money in the bank, the customer still owes it — the CRM just stops chasing them for a while and says why. Before this split, a telecaller's word reduced outstanding on the spot. A transfer that never landed erased real debt from every screen, with nobody's name against the decision. And an order that accounts later declined had already been counted as a sale. Two questions, two answers, and the screens say which one they are showing.

search.heading: Whose book a customer is in
search.text: Every list in the CRM — the Call Log, Reminders, Payment Follow-up, Outstanding, Sales Bills, Complaints, Customers, Call History — is cut to a book . There is one definition of it, used everywhere: The account is It is in the book of A lead (never ordered) Its owner A customer Its sales account manager, falling back to the owner only while nobody has decided the seat A customer can carry up to five seats — sales, back office, sales manager, relationship and the lead owner — but only the first two decide who sees and works an account day to day, and only one is credited with its orders. The Customers page explains each seat. Why one definition. Reading the owner alone once dropped every customer whose sales manager had been set — including off the collections list while they still owed money. A team list also says whose call each row is, from the same definition, and says Unassigned in words: a row nobody owns is the one a manager most needs to see.

search.heading: Scope: your book or the team
search.text: Person What they see Can they switch? Telecaller (CRM associate) Their own book No. The switch is not drawn, and the server ignores a cookie that asks for more. CRM manager Their team by default — their direct reports and themselves Yes, My book / Team in the header changes every list at once Admin Everybody The switch still narrows to their own book Scope narrows, it never widens. The switch is a view. Each list asks the server for the people in scope and filters by them; nothing on any screen can widen what a person is allowed to see. A manager "of the CRM" means a manager level held in the CRM — managing a different app does not draw the switch here. The accounts desk is deliberately outside this narrowing. In the Accounts app the approval queue and the ledgers are every book, because the person approving an order is never the person who owns it.

search.heading: Access: the app, then the screen
search.text: 1. The app. Somebody without the CRM granted is sent to the launcher, whatever URL they typed. 2. The screen. The CRM is split into modules — one per sidebar entry. A manager can narrow a grant to some of them on the Access screen. A screen not held is not drawn in the sidebar, and its address redirects to the first screen the person does hold. 3. The action. Some buttons need a capability as well — closing a reminder by hand, reassigning an account, confirming money. The button is drawn disabled with a sentence saying who can, and the server checks again on save. WhatsApp is the one screen with two levels: read the chats, or reply and send . They are granted separately.

search.heading: Numbers beside the sidebar links
search.text: Link What the number counts Reminders Pending reminders due today or overdue Complaints Complaints open, in progress or awaiting the customer Close/Reopen Requests to close or reopen an account that nobody has decided All Leads Leads past the day something was owed, otherwise leads with something due today These are read from the same functions the dashboard and the launcher tile read, so a badge and the screen behind it are meant to agree.

search.heading: The working day
search.text: Every "today" in the CRM is the business date in Asia/Kolkata. Where the day starts is o'clock, and which days are working days is . "Yesterday" on the dashboard means the previous working day, and a reminder set for a Sunday rolls to Monday when is on. A server that counts days in GMT puts a 1 am call on the previous day. Every date in the CRM is cut in the business zone on purpose, and the screens print the dates a comparison covers rather than implying them.

search.heading: Nothing business-critical is a constant
search.text: Thresholds that a manager might want to change — how many days of quiet after an order, when calling opens on a late bill, how long a reported payment buys, what counts as slow paying — are settings, changed in the Admin Console. Each page in this guide shows the value your CRM is using right now.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - A manager's Reminders badge counts the whole company. The badge counts every pending reminder for anybody on team scope, while the Reminders list beneath it is narrowed to the manager's own team. - The Complaints badge and the dashboard's complaint counts read the account owner , not the one definition of whose book an account is in. A complaint on a customer whose sales manager differs from its owner is counted against the owner. - The dashboard's "Collected" figure and Payment Follow-up's "Collected this month" add up every payment line, including reported money accounts have not confirmed and money they rejected. Every other money figure in the CRM is confirmed-only. - Some screens still decide "manager" from the widest level held anywhere rather than the level held in the CRM — the Opportunities team view is one.

Collections is three pure engines wired to three services. E3 ( engines/escalation.ts ) turns a customer's bills into a stage, cached in follow up states by recomputeFollowUpState . E7 ( engines/payment-followup.ts ) turns those states into today's calls, messages and held-back list. engines/allocation.ts spreads an amount over bills. The services are payment-service.ts (worklist, metrics, ledger reads), payment-followup-service.ts (logging a collections call) and receipt-service.ts (recording and deciding money).

search.heading: The cadence (E7)

Payment Follow-up is the collections list. It shows who owes money that is past its due date , how late it is, what they last promised, and whether today is a day to message them or call them. You work it the same way as the Call Log: open the customer, chase, log what they said, move on. The day counts on this page — when calling opens, how often a reminder goes, how long a reported payment buys — are the settings your CRM is using right now.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: Payment Follow-up, Call today tab. Payment follow-up Send stage 1 reminders Export To call today. 6 To message today. 11 Outstanding. ₹9,40,000 · 38 customers Collected this month. ₹3,10,000 of ₹7,00,000 due More details — ageing, promises, reminders ▾ Slow payers Sort by amount 4 customers kept off today's list, and why

search.heading: The three stages
search.text: Every customer on the list sits at a stage, worked out from how late their oldest unpaid bill is: Stage Badge How you chase 1 1 · Nudge WhatsApp only. You cannot log a call at stage 1. 2 2 · Call Calls and messages alternate. Get a dated promise. 3 3 · Urgent Call, and be firm. Stage 2 starts at days overdue and stage 3 at days. A customer who refuses to commit or cannot be reached is moved up a stage and kept there, even if their bill dates alone would put them lower.

search.heading: Message first, then call
search.text: A bill a few days late is usually paperwork, not refusal. So: The bill falls due. For the first days nobody rings. The customer gets a WhatsApp reminder every days instead — they appear on Message today when one is due. Calling opens. The day after that window closes, they appear on Call today . After each call. They rest days before coming back to Call today. Messages carry on alongside.

search.heading: Logging a collections call
search.text: Open the follow-up. Press Call & log , or open the follow-up from the ⋯ menu. The panel shows what they owe, the oldest bill, when they were last chased, their credit terms, every open bill and every promise so far. Ring them, then answer: What did they say?. Pick one of the outcomes below. Quick-pick phrases are offered for each; you can type your own note. Save. Everything the outcome produces is saved in one go. The window afterwards says when this customer comes back to your Call Log , the same as after any other call. Outcome You must fill in What saving does Payment promised Amount promised, Promised by (today or later) Records the promise and creates a reminder for the working day after, so a broken promise is chased Already paid Amount already paid; a payment proof photo is optional Records the money as reported — waiting for accounts. The customer is not chased for it for a few days. Nothing they owe changes yet. Call back later Call back on Creates a callback reminder for that date Dispute raised — Raises a billing complaint and marks their oldest bill disputed. The account is held where it is until the complaint is closed. Refused to commit — Moves the account up a stage and keeps it there Not reachable — Moves the account up a stage and keeps it there. Closes no reminder. 'Already paid' does not reduce what they owe. A customer saying they paid is not the money arriving. It sits with accounts as reported until they find it in the bank. Until then the bills stay open, the customer stays on the list, and the row shows Paid ₹…? — but nobody chases them for days.

search.heading: Recording a payment from the list
search.text: From the ⋯ menu, Record a payment opens a form against one open bill: amount received, how it came (mode), the reference, the date received and — for a cheque — the date written on it. - If you hold the accounts desk's right to confirm money, it is recorded as confirmed . - Otherwise it is recorded as reported and waits for accounts, exactly like Already paid . Record a promise writes a dated promise without logging a call outcome.
