Not chased until they decide. ₹X cheque dated … - not chased until it can be banked A post-dated cheque. Quiet until its date, then the usual window. ₹X reported paid N days ago - waiting for accounts to confirm it Reported money buys days of quiet Paid today / yesterday - not chased about money until … They paid something recently; quiet for day(s) Payment promised by … - not chased until it passes A live promise Already contacted today One contact a day Only N days overdue - messages only until … Still in the message-only window Called N days ago - due again on … Resting after the last call

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: The customer says they paid. Why are they still on the list?. The money is reported, not confirmed. They stay on the list with a Paid ₹…? flag and are not chased for a few days. Once accounts confirm it, the bills close and they leave the list. Why can I not log a call for a stage 1 customer?. Stage 1 is a WhatsApp nudge only. Send the reminder, or wait for the account to reach stage 2. They promised to pay on the 20th. What happens on the 21st?. A payment-promise reminder falls due on the working day after the 20th. If the money has been confirmed by then, the reminder closes on its own. They gave a cheque dated next month.. Report it with the cheque date. They are not chased until the date on the cheque, and then only after the usual window for it to clear. What is a slow payer?. A customer who has paid at least bills more than days after their due date in the last months. The flag appears beside their name everywhere. Somebody I expected is missing.. Open kept off today's list . If they are not there either, they owe nothing past its due date, or their bills have not been stated as owed.

Payment Follow-up turns the bill ledger into a day's collections work. Three rules decide it: how late a customer is (their stage), whether today is a day to message or call them (the cadence), and what holds them back (a promise, a dispute, money they say they paid). Underneath all three sits the rule the whole money side of MahekOne turns on: money a customer says they paid is not money the business has seen . Every value quoted is the one your CRM is using right now.

search.heading: Who is on the list
search.text: A customer is on the collections worklist when at least one of their bills is stated as owed , has a balance, and is past its due date. Five overdue bills make one row — the list is grouped by customer, never by bill. Paying everything removes them the moment the money is confirmed; there is no separate "close" step. A bill's due date. The bill's own due date, or else the bill date plus the credit period in force: the term agreed on the order, then the customer's standing term, then days. A customer on 45 days never quietly becomes 30 because nobody typed a date onto the bill.

search.heading: The stage
search.text: How a stage is decided. Setting Now Stage 2 begins at days overdue Stage 3 begins at days overdue Which bill drives the stage A part payment restarts the clock A dispute holds the stage Stage 1 is WhatsApp only. A call cannot be logged against a stage 1 account — the server refuses it with Stage 1 is a WhatsApp-only nudge . Stage 2 alternates channels so a customer is not messaged twice running; stage 3 is a call.

search.heading: The floor: what a refusal earns
search.text: The stage has a floor, and only a person raises it. Refused to commit and Not reachable raise a floor one stage above where the account sits (at most 3), with the reason and who set it. The stage still rises with the age of the debt; it simply never reads below the floor. A customer who refuses to commit has told you something their bill dates have not. The floor leaves with the row when nothing is overdue any more, because it described a debt that no longer exists. A floor a nightly rebuild erased would not be a floor — there is a test saying so.

search.heading: The cadence: message before call
search.text: One overdue bill, day by day. Rule Setting No calls for the first days past the due date A reminder message every days, from the last one sent (or from the due date) After a logged call, rest days A bill a few days late is usually paperwork rather than refusal — a cheque in the post, an accounts department that pays on Fridays. Messages do not stop when calling starts; the two run alongside. The quiet window and the stage 2 threshold are two statements of one fact, so the settings screen refuses values that would let the list offer a call on a day the server still calls stage 1. Within each list, the oldest debt comes first, then the largest.

search.heading: What holds a customer back
search.text: Whatever stops the chasing stops both channels, and the strip says so once per channel the customer would otherwise have appeared on. The first matching reason wins: Order Held because Expires? 1 Marked do not contact No — a standing instruction 2 A bill is disputed When the dispute is resolved 3 Money on hold with accounts No. Only a person in accounts ends it 4 A post-dated cheque not yet at its date On the cheque's date, then the ordinary window runs from there 5 Money reported paid After days 6 Paid something recently After day(s) 7 A live promise The day after the promised date 8 Already contacted today Tomorrow Why reported quiet expires and a hold does not. A bare report is nobody's decision. If it did not expire, a customer could take themselves off the collections list for good by saying they had paid, and the account would simply stop appearing. A hold is a named person in accounts saying I am looking for this in the bank statement — chasing through that is worse than any call not made. What replaces the expiry is visibility: the hold ages on accounts' own list and is flagged after days.

search.heading: The six outcomes, in one transaction
search.text: One outcome, one transaction. A collections call can produce a promise and its reminder, a payment spread over bills, a billing complaint and a raised floor. All of it — plus the attempt, the call in the interaction log and the timeline entry — is written together or not at all. The outcomes and what each requires are declared once, so the form and the server cannot disagree about which fields are mandatory. Outcome Requires Writes Payment promised Amount, date (today or later) Attempt with the promise; reminder (payment promise) for the next working day after the date Already paid Amount A reported receipt, allocated across the oldest open bills; proof photographs bound afterwards Call back later Date Callback reminder Dispute raised — Billing complaint at the default priority and deadline; oldest open bill marked disputed Refused to commit — Floor raised one stage Not reachable — Floor raised one stage; the call counts as unanswered Part payment promised is retired: it is never offered and never accepted, but attempts recorded against it still read back with their label. After the transaction, the follow-up state is rebuilt, and the CRM works out when the customer comes back to the Call Log and stores that sentence on the call — exactly as on the routine calling path. An answered collections call closes the customer's reminders that were due; Not reachable closes none.

search.heading: Money: reported, held, confirmed, rejected, reversed
search.text: A receipt's life. Only confirmed money counts. A bill's paid amount is rebuilt from confirmed receipts only , every time — never incremented — so confirming, rejecting and re-confirming all land on the same answer. Outstanding, aging, the slow-payer flag and this worklist all read from that. A reported or held receipt moves no rupee anywhere. Status Means On the customer's statement reported Somebody says it was paid; nobody has looked "waiting for accounts" held Accounts are checking it "on hold with accounts, being checked" confirmed Found in the bank Counts rejected Accounts looked and it never arrived The reason — the row stays reversed It counted and then failed "reversed — reason" Who can confirm. Confirming, holding, rejecting and reversing need payment.confirm — the accounts desk. Somebody holding it who records money is believed as they write it (confirmed at once), except on a collections call, which is always reported. Everybody else reports. Reversing refuses a reported receipt: nothing has counted yet, so rejection is the honest answer.

search.heading: Cheques
search.text: A cheque has two dates: when we got it, and the date written on it. Modes that carry the second are . A post-dated cheque buys quiet until it can be banked; once its date passes the ordinary reported window runs from the cheque's date , not from when it was written down.

search.heading: The slow-payer flag
search.text: Late means past the due date plus a grace. A confirmed payment counts as late when it landed more than days after its bill's due date. A customer with or more late payments in the last months is a slow payer. The flag is rebuilt nightly and shown beside the name everywhere. A payment a day or two past its term is ordinary business. Counting those flagged customers who pay perfectly reliably, just not to the calendar. The grace is on the date , not the count: three payments a fortnight late is still a slow payer.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: 'Collected this month' counts money nobody has confirmed. The figure adds up every payment line dated this month in your book — including money only reported on a call, money on hold, and money accounts rejected. Every other money figure is confirmed-only. Its "of … due" companion and the Outstanding card also include bills that are not stated as owed. - The "Already paid" outcome's own description is out of date. It says the amount "is applied to the oldest bills first, and the outstanding figure updates everywhere". The amount is allocated, but recorded as reported: outstanding does not move until accounts confirm. - The slow-payer count is of payment lines, not bills. A bill paid late in two instalments counts as two late payments; the lookback is 30 days per month rather than calendar months. - Raising the floor needs a call, and stage 1 refuses calls. A stage 1 customer who refuses or cannot be reached cannot have their floor raised from the panel. - The collections audit row records no hat. It is written without the role and app that allowed it.

My Performance is a server page over one service read , readingsForPeriod , narrowed to the signed-in user. The arithmetic is a pure engine ( engines/performance.ts ); the actuals and their attribution are SQL in performance-service.ts through one crediting rule ( sales-attribution.ts ); the stored score cache ( sales performance ) is rebuilt hourly and nightly for the handset and the Sales Dashboard. Everything below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.heading: A reading, end to end
search.text: GET /crm/performance.

search.heading: Attribution
search.text: One person per account, never both seats, never owner id for a customer. unattributedForPeriod reports what landed on nobody.

search.heading: The engine
search.text: Everything is in basis points ( BP = 10 000 ) and integers; division happens only on the way to a screen.

search.heading: Actuals
search.text: - Day windows in SQL carry +05:30 ; a bare bound reads in the session zone. - Order value is orderValueSql (net of GST, after discount) over orderCountsSql rows. - Litres = cans × products.millilitres per can ; an unmatched product name adds revenue, no litres, and unmatched revenue paise . - Collection reconstructs each bill's balance as of the window start from confirmed allocations received before it ( bills.paid amount is current, not historical), excludes unstated bills, and skips receipts keyed creditnote:% . - Activity reads tasks by assigned to user id , due inside the window.

search.heading: Targets and mix bands
search.text: bandsForTargets reads both keys; isFormulation (from the target's own bands) picks which bucket of actuals is scored, because scoreMix totals whatever it is handed and one map holding both would halve every share.

search.heading: The cache
search.text: sales performance is a cache — rebuilding it is a correction. It is not the same kind of column as calls.next step , which records what somebody was told and must never be rebuilt.

search.heading: Permissions
search.text: The CRM screen checks no capability: it reads only the signed-in user and has no id parameter. Setting a target needs target.set (managers and accounts).

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A seventh component touches four places. COMPONENT KEYS , a weight key in the registry (and the total-100 consistency check), the actual in actualsForWindow , and a column in sales performance . Credit through one rule. Any new actual is grouped by creditedToSql . Never by ASSIGNED TO SQL (it ends at the importer) or scopedToUsers (two people). Null is not zero. Keep achievementBp returning null for no target, and keep the dropped component named. Never reinterpret a stored target. New target shapes get new columns; old rows keep scoring the way they were written.

My Performance is your own month: the target your manager or accounts set for you, what you have actually done against it, a score out of 100, and — first on the page — what is short , in rupees, litres and customers. It always shows you , and nobody else. If you carry customers in the CRM, you have a number here, even if you never go into the field. Numbers on this page are your CRM's current settings.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: My performance, part way through a month. My performance ‹ Month › Export Overall. 72.4 / 100 · Good Revenue excl. GST. ₹8.2L · of ₹13L Volume. 2,140 L · of 3,500 L New customers. 1 · of 3 Collected. ₹2.1L of ₹4.0L overdue Tasks done. 18 of 22 What is short. ₹4.8 lakh short on revenue · PU is below its minimum share · 2 new customers to go ₹43,600 a day over the 11 working days left would reach the revenue target. At the rate so far the month lands at 98%. Product mix.

search.heading: The six things you are measured on
search.text: Component What counts Revenue The value of approved orders from customers credited to you, excluding GST . Volume The litres in those orders, worked out from each product's pack. A price rise moves revenue; it cannot move litres. Product mix Each product's share of your sales value, against the minimum, target and stretch share you were asked for. New customers Customers whose first counting order landed this month. Raising a lead does not count. Collection How much of the money that was already overdue on the 1st you collected this month — confirmed by accounts. Activity Of the tasks given to you that were due this month , how many you completed. A component nobody set a target for is left out , and its weight is shared among the others. The score is always out of 100 against what was actually asked of you . The screen names any component that was left out.

search.heading: How the weights are set now
search.text: Component Weight Revenue Volume Product mix New customers Collection Activity

search.heading: Reading your month, step by step
search.text: Read What is short first. It says what you are behind on in your own units — rupees, litres, customers, a product's share — worst first. Everything else on the page is the working-out. Check the per-day figure. "₹X a day over the N working days left" is what it would take to reach the revenue target. Sundays and company holidays are not counted. Look at the mix. A product below minimum costs you the most. Selling more of what already sells well does not make up for it. Check where your customers are short. Your per-customer targets are on Monthly Targets.

search.heading: Whose sales are yours
search.text: Every rupee belongs to one person: 1. The account's salesperson , if it has one. 2. Otherwise its back-office person . 3. A lead counts for its owner (that is how a lead's first order becomes your new customer). Nobody else. Two people can both see an account; only one is credited with what it bought.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: It says no target has been set for me.. You see what you have done, but no score — a percentage against a target nobody set would be invented. Targets are set by your manager or by accounts. I took an order this morning and Revenue has not moved.. Orders count once accounts approve them. Why is my collection figure lower than what I collected?. It only counts money against bills that were already overdue on the 1st, and only once accounts confirm it. A bill that fell due mid-month and was paid is ordinary business, not collection. Can my manager see this screen for me?. This screen only ever shows the person signed in. Managers compare people on the Sales Dashboard. It is the 1st and the forecast is missing.. With no working day finished yet there is no projection — one day multiplied by thirty is not a forecast.

"₹10 lakh billed" is not a measure of selling. A price revision raises every rupee figure without one extra can leaving the godown, and somebody who works only the products that sell themselves bills well and grows nothing. So a person's month is measured on six components , scored out of a hundred against what was actually asked of them. This tab is how that score is built, why each piece is shaped as it is, and why the CRM — not only the Sales Dashboard — shows it. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: Why a telecaller has a performance screen
search.text: Whose number it is falls through, to exactly one person. An account's sales are credited to its salesperson ; where it has none, to its back-office person ; a lead's to its owner . Neither seat filled means nobody — the figure is reported as unattributed, never handed to somebody. Back-office people carry a large part of this book under that fall-through, and they are redirected out of /sales . Without this CRM screen they would be measured against a number they had no way to read. It shows one person, always the signed-in one , and takes no id — a manager comparing people has the Sales Dashboard, and an id here would let anybody read anybody's appraisal. Why the importer is not in the chain. Whose book an account is in ends with its owner, but on an imported customer the owner is whoever ran the import — one person on over a thousand rows. Ending the credit chain there would hand them the whole company's revenue the day they were given a target. An unattributed customer is a fact worth surfacing; a wrongly attributed one is a number somebody gets appraised on. Two people may both see an account; only one may be credited , or the team adds up to more than the company.

search.heading: The six components
search.text: From actuals to a score. Component Actual Weight now Revenue Value of approved orders, excluding GST Volume Litres, from each product's millilitres per can × cans Product mix Each target product's share of sales value, scored against its bands New customers Customers won this month (basis: ) Collection Confirmed money collected against bills already overdue on the 1st, as a share of that overdue Activity Tasks due this month that were completed, as a share of tasks due this month The weights must total 100 — the settings screen refuses a set that does not, because a score presented out of 100 and computed out of 95 is a different number wearing the same label. A component nobody set is dropped, not scored. A target of zero is not a target. Scoring it 0% marks somebody down for a question never asked; scoring it 100% pays them for it. So it leaves the score and the remaining weights are restated out of a hundred, and the screen names what was dropped. With nothing targeted at all there is no score — the screen says no target was set and shows the actuals only. Achievement is capped for scoring, never for display. One extraordinary component cannot carry a score past everything else being wrong: achievement is capped at % when it is weighted. The screen still prints the real figure.

search.heading: What each actual deliberately excludes
search.text: - Revenue and volume count orders accounts have approved — the same "did we sell anything" every report uses. Money whose product name matches nothing in the catalogue still counts as revenue, contributes no litres, and is reported as unmatched so a mix computed over 94% of the value says so. - Revenue is not derived from the catalogue. The product master holds no prices; the value of a line is what was billed. - New customers counts a customer once, the month their first counting order (or bill) lands. Creating a lead never counts — the one definition that cannot be worked from a desk. - Collection counts confirmed receipts only — reported or held money moves no figure anywhere in the product — and not credit notes , which are money given back, not collected. It measures old debt worked down: a bill that went overdue on the 15th and was paid on the 20th is ordinary business. - Activity counts tasks assigned to the person, due inside the month. A task with no due date counts nowhere; a task due on the 5th and done on the 20th still counts. Using one population for both sides stops somebody clearing an old backlog and showing 300%.

search.heading: The product mix
search.text: Weighted by what was asked, never by what arrived. Each product on the target carries three shares — minimum , target , stretch — and is weighted by its target share. Weighting by the actual share would let somebody who sold nothing but the easy line score a perfect mix. A product that came in at nothing drags the score down by exactly what it was meant to contribute. - The mix is measured on value , not litres; litres are shown alongside. - Between the anchors the score is a straight line, so 24.9% and 25.0% are not a whole band apart. What each anchor pays is configuration: %, %, % of the product's points. - A target is now set on formulations — the liquid a salesman actually sells (one liquid sells under several brand names). One formulation is the residual , Other , which catches everything nobody classified and every line whose product matched nothing, so the shares always total 100%. - A target written before this, against the three broad categories , goes on scoring as categories. Nothing already set is reinterpreted.

search.heading: Revenue against volume: the alert the module was built for
search.text: Revenue at or above target while volume is more than points behind it means the money came from the price list, not from selling more — exactly the month somebody would otherwise be congratulated. It is raised beside the score. Other alerts: behind pace (projection below %), a mix product below its minimum, no new customers, collection behind, activity behind.

search.heading: The forecast: working days, never dates
search.text: The month-end projection is the actual so far ÷ working days completed × working days in the month. Sundays (per the configured working week) and company holidays are excluded; today is not counted as elapsed , because dividing by a day still being worked makes everybody look behind every morning. With no completed working day there is no projection at all.

search.heading: The rating word
search.text: The word beside the score comes from — a list of bands, each a minimum score and a word, read highest first. A list that does not reach the bottom returns its lowest band rather than nothing, because a score with no word reads as a screen that failed.

search.heading: Where the score is kept
search.text: The CRM screen computes the reading live on every load. A stored copy (the score cache) is rebuilt hourly for this month and nightly for this month and the last ; that cache is what the handset and the Sales Dashboard read, with the time it was computed printed beside it. The score is a reading of the present, so rebuilding it is a correction, not a loss.

search.heading: Targets: draft, published, revised
search.text: A person's target is set on the Sales Dashboard ( /sales/targets ) or by accounts on /accounts/targets , with the target-setting permission. It is a draft until published — nothing reaches anybody until then — and a published target changes only with a coded reason from , one revision row per figure that moved, and the person is told.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Activity is tasks, not visits. AGENTS.md says a visit's activity is counted on the server's clock; the component now measures tasks due in the month and completed ( lib/services/performance-service.ts actualsForWindow , activity block). - Collection and activity are shares, not counts. The target carries collection target bp and activity target bp ; the older count column activity target is retired in place, and the cache still names its collection target in paise ( collection target paise , derived from the base × the share). - The Overall tile's colour uses fixed thresholds — green from 80, red below 60 — rather than the configured rating bands ( src/app/crm/performance/page.tsx ). - The empty state says targets are set "on the Sales Dashboard" , though accounts set them on /accounts/targets too ( src/app/crm/performance/page.tsx ).

Price lists are one feature mounted in four apps — the CRM, the Sales Dashboard, Accounts and the Founder Dashboard — through shared components in src/components/pricing/ and one service, price-list-service.ts . The CRM mount is read-only for everybody : priceListDoorCanManage(user, "crm") answers no before it asks any capability. Which list applies to a shop is the pure resolvePriceList ; the money arithmetic is price-math.ts ; every write is in lib/actions/price-lists.ts behind requirePriceDesk() — the capability and the desk module it was worn at.

Price lists tell you what each shop pays . In the CRM you can open every list, see which one applies to a customer and why, print or export it, and ask for a special price when a customer wants to pay less. You cannot change a list here — the Accounts desk and the Founder Dashboard make, publish and retire them. Figures on this page that come from settings — the GST rate, how long a list stays valid, how much discount you may give — are the values your CRM is using right now.

search.heading: The five tabs
search.text: Tab What it answers Lists Every price list and its status. Documents Price-list files (PDFs and photos) that have arrived and are being read into lists. Waiting files show first. Requests Special prices that have been asked for, what the shop pays now, and what was decided. You see the ones you asked for; managers see everybody's. Coverage Which shops a published list names — and which shops no list names at all. Variance For a chosen month, every billed order line from the order sheet beside what the list says that shop should have paid.

search.heading: What a list's status means
search.text: Status Meaning Draft Being prepared. Prices nobody. Published In force from its start date. Shops it names are priced from it. Superseded Replaced by a newer version. Kept so old orders can still be explained. Withdrawn Taken out of force, with a reason. Expired A published list past its validity — days from its start unless the list says otherwise. Nobody has replaced it yet, so the office may not honour its rates. expires in Nd Runs out within a week. The Transport column says who pays freight: To Pay (the shop pays the transporter on delivery, prices are ex-freight), Paid (we pay transport, built into the price up to the transporter's godown) or Not stated . Applies to lists who the list is for — a state, a city, a salesman, one customer, or Everybody . A published list that names nobody says Nobody — prices no shop in amber.

search.heading: Opening a list
search.text: One price list. Region A price list PDF / Export / Print Rates. Who it applies to. Discounts on this list. 2% for advance payment · 3% above a quantity Below these are Where it came from (the original file), Versions , Lists built on this one and Terms and notes .

search.heading: Finding the price for one customer
search.text: The quickest way is the customer's record: Open the customer. From the Call Log, the customer list or search. Open the Prices tab. It shows the list that applies to this shop today, every rate including GST (switch to Ex GST if you need it), the price per litre, and the discounts printed on that list. Check the badges. Expired means nobody has replaced the list yet — check before you promise a figure. Changed since their last order means their last order was priced from a different list: say so before they read it off the invoice. Press Why this price? if the customer asks. It walks you through how the list was chosen — no list for them by name, no list for their salesman, matched on their state, freight to pay — in order. Copy price list to send it on WhatsApp. It copies the customer's name, the list, every rate (incl and ex GST) and the discount terms, ready to paste. If no list applies you see: No price list applies to this shop. That means no list in force today names their city, state, salesman, or everybody. Tell a manager — the Coverage tab lists every shop in this state.

search.heading: Prices on a call
search.text: When you log an order on a call, each product you add shows the rate per can and the name of the list it came from . The rates are the same ones on the customer's Prices tab. - If the order form is set to price orders from the list (currently ), each line shows what it comes to, and the order shows Ex-GST , GST and Total . A line whose product is not on the shop's list is left out, and the form says N lines are not on this shop's list, so the total is short by them . - If it is not, you see Rates are from …, shown for reference — an order is still worth what accounts bill for it. - If no list applies, the form shows quantities and no money.

search.heading: Giving a discount
search.text: A % box appears on each priced line only if you are allowed to give a discount at all. Your level in the CRM You may give on your own Telecaller (associate) Up to basis points (100 = 1%) Manager Up to basis points Admin Any discount The discount is taken before GST. If you type more than you are allowed, the save is refused with a sentence like You may give up to 3% on your own. Above that a manager has to authorise it. — or, when your limit is zero, You cannot give a discount on your own. Ask a manager to authorise it. Save the order without the discount and ask, or ask for a special price.

search.heading: Asking for a special price
search.text: When a customer wants to pay less than their list for a product: Open the customer's Prices tab. Press Ask for a special price . It is greyed out if the shop has no rates to ask against. Pick the product and type the price they want. Type the price including GST — the figure the shopkeeper says out loud. The form shows the ex-GST figure underneath and how far it is from today's rate in percent. Say why. The reason is required. Whoever decides is not on the call and has nothing else to weigh it on. Send it. You see Asked. Whoever decides prices has been told. The request appears under Asked for on the Prices tab with the status Waiting .

search.heading: What happens next
search.text: A special price request. - Approved — the customer now has a list of their own (named Customer A — agreed prices ) and that rate is what the order form uses from then on. A second approved special price for the same shop is added to the same list. - Refused — nothing changes. You get a notification with the decider's note so you can ring the customer back. - Withdraw — only you, and only while it is still waiting. Use it from the row menu on the Requests tab.

search.heading: Coverage and variance
search.text: Coverage shows how many shops are on a list, how many are on no list, and how many have no freight term recorded (a list of either term can still name them). The On no list table shows up to 200 of those shops with their region, freight term and salesman — these are shops being priced from memory. Variance shows, month by month, every priced line billed on the order sheet beside the list price for that shop. The figures at the top count lines at , below and above the list, lines where no list resolved , and the total given away below the list . Sort is biggest discount first.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Why can't I edit a price here?. Prices are set by the Accounts desk and the Founder Dashboard only. The CRM and the Sales Dashboard quote prices; the person chasing a number must not also set the price it is measured in. The customer says they were quoted a different price.. Open their Prices tab. If it says Changed since their last order , their last order came from a different list — tell them. If the list is Expired , check with accounts before confirming. Are the prices including GST?. The Prices tab shows Incl GST by default with the ex-GST figure beneath. Lists are stored ex-GST and printed inclusive at the list's own GST rate; where a list does not say, basis points (1800 = 18%). Inclusive figures are rounded to the rupee, as the office prints them. Two lists seem to cover the same shop. Which wins?. The narrowest one: a list for the customer by name, then their salesman, beat, area, city, district, state, customer type, and finally everybody. Press Why this price? to see it. I asked for a special price and heard nothing.. Check the Requests tab. A request stays Waiting until somebody at the Accounts desk or the Founder Dashboard decides it; you are notified either way. The discount box is missing on my order lines.. Your discount limit is zero, so the box is not drawn. Ask a manager, or ask for a special price.

A price list answers one question for every shop: what does this customer pay for this can, today? The CRM is where that answer is quoted — on a call, on the customer's record, in a message. It is deliberately not where the answer is set . This tab explains how a list is chosen for a shop, how GST and discounts are worked out, how a special price becomes a shop's own list, and who may do what. Every value quoted from a setting is the one your CRM is using right now.

search.heading: Two jobs, two desks
search.text: Reading a price. Every signed-in person who opens the CRM's Price lists. A telecaller pricing an order and a salesman standing in a shop both need the customer's list in front of them — a price they cannot see is a price they guess. Setting a price. The Accounts desk (both levels) and the Founder Dashboard (both levels), plus administrators. Importing, editing, publishing, scoping, duplicating, assigning a list to a shop and deciding a special price. Why the CRM is read-only for everybody. The person chasing a number must not also set the price that number is measured in — the same reasoning that keeps order approval away from managers. Setting prices was first given to CRM and Sales Dashboard managers too; Mahek's instruction was that lists are added, changed and deleted by the accounts team or from the founder's desk only. So the CRM's Price lists screens draw no control that writes , even for somebody who also holds the Accounts desk and could change the list from there. A control drawn on a telecaller's screen because the person happens to wear a second hat is a control a telecaller's screen should not have. Who In the CRM they can Telecaller (CRM associate) Read every list, see which list applies to a shop and why, export and print, ask for a special price, withdraw their own request, give a discount up to the associate ceiling CRM manager All of that, see everybody's special price requests, give a discount up to the manager ceiling Admin Any discount; but the CRM screens still draw no editing controls Accounts desk / Founder Dashboard Make and change lists — on their own Price lists screens, not the CRM's

search.heading: Which list applies to a shop
search.text: A list says who it is for through scope rules . A rule names one of nine kinds of thing: a single customer, a salesman, a beat, an area, a city, a district, a state, a customer type, or everybody . A shop usually matches several — it is in a state, in a city, on a beat, and its salesman may have a list of his own. Narrowest wins. The kinds are tried narrowest first , and the first kind with any match decides: customer → salesman → beat → area → city → district → state → customer type → everybody. Inside one kind, three things break a tie, in order: the freight term that fits the shop exactly, then the rule's priority , then the list with the newest start date . Resolving a shop's list. Why the answer carries its reasons. A price a telecaller cannot explain is a price the customer argues with. So the answer is never just a list name: it is the ladder that was walked — no list for this customer by name, no list for their salesman, matched on the city Thane under Maharashtra, freight to pay . That ladder is what Why this price? and Which list applies? draw. The handset compiles the same rule, so a salesman standing in the shop and the office get one answer.

search.heading: What counts as "in force"
search.text: - The list is published , its start date has arrived, and its end date (if any) has not passed. - The scope rule's own valid from / valid to dates include today. - Drafts, superseded and withdrawn lists price nobody.

search.heading: A shop is known by several spellings
search.text: The book's city and state columns hold whatever the order sheet typed; the place master holds what was made of it. A shop is matched on both — the resolved place and the folded raw text — so a book whose places have never been resolved still matches on what the sheet said. A city rule picked under its state does not reach a city of the same name in another state; a rule with no parent matches the place wherever it is.

search.heading: Freight: To Pay and Paid
search.text: One region often has two lists — one where the shop pays the transporter ( To Pay ) and one where transport is built into the price ( Paid ). The shop's own freight term picks between them. A shop whose freight term was never recorded is not left with nothing: a list of either term may name it, and the exact match only wins a tie.

search.heading: Lists in force, versions and validity
search.text: A published list is never edited — it is superseded. An order taken in August has to stay explainable in December. So when prices move, a new version is published. Publishing it marks the old one superseded , ends it the day before the new one starts, and — if the new version names nobody — carries the old version's scope rules across, so "publish next month's list" is one act rather than two. What may still change on a published list is what a reader sees: the name, the reference, notes and terms. Nothing is deleted. Superseded and withdrawn are states; the rows stay. Withdrawing needs a reason. The only deletes are a draft nobody published and a document that never became a list. Validity. A list is valid for its own validity period from the day it takes effect — days where the list does not say, matching Mahek's printed terms (30 days or until the next revision, whichever is earlier). A published list past that is drawn Expired on every screen, and the list index counts lists expiring within a week. Publishing checks. A list with no prices is refused. A list that names nobody is published with the warning Nobody is on this list yet, so no shop will be priced from it. A list derived from a parent by a rule (for example "the To Pay list plus a rupee amount per litre") is checked against that rule; cells more than paise per can away are counted in a warning rather than refused, because the office overrides a cell deliberately often enough that a block would be worked around.

search.heading: Where lists come from
search.text: Most lists start as a file somebody was sent — a PDF in Mahek's own layout, or a photograph. The Documents tab shows each file being read: the layout found, prices turned into paise, every row and pack-size column matched to a SKU in the catalogue, GST and the derivation checked. A document the reader is less than % sure of is marked Needs a person ; none is ever published without somebody opening it. Lists can also be built from scratch, from every active product, copied, derived from another list by a rule, or imported from a spreadsheet — all on the Accounts and Founder desks.

search.heading: GST
search.text: Stored ex-GST, printed inclusive. Every rate is stored ex-GST in paise , which is what the order sheet bills. The inclusive figure is ex-GST times (1 + the list's GST rate), rounded to the rupee — what the office prints and the shop is told. Going back from a printed inclusive figure keeps its paise rather than rounding, so a printed ₹2,281 does not turn into the wrong rupee on every billed line for a month. - Each list carries its own GST rate. Where a document does not state one, basis points is used (1800 = 18%). - A line's worth is worked out as: cans × rate ex-GST, minus the discount , then GST on what is left. - A special price is typed inclusive — the figure the shopkeeper quotes — and stored ex-GST.

search.heading: Prices on the order form
search.text: When a telecaller adds products to an order on a call, the rate is looked up on the server for the customer being billed (a shop's distributor where the goods are invoiced to one), as of today's business date. A rate that arrived from the screen would be a price the caller chose, which is the whole thing price lists exist to stop. - On : each line shows its worth and the order shows ex-GST, GST and total. Lines not on the shop's list are left out of the total and the form says how many. - Off : the rates are shown for reference only. - Either way, each order line records the list rate it was quoted at and the discount given , and the order records which list priced it — written once, so a revision next month does not rewrite what was quoted today.

search.heading: Discount authority
search.text: What somebody may take off a list price on a call depends on their level in the CRM — not the widest level they hold anywhere. A telecaller who is also a manager of Reports does not get the manager's discount on a call. CRM level Ceiling Associate (telecaller) bp Manager bp Admin No ceiling Above the ceiling, the save is refused. Not flagged — refused, with a sentence naming the way forward. The order has not happened yet, so nothing is lost by saying no; the alternative is a rate given away with nobody's name against it, which is what the order sheet already shows happening at 10%. Where somebody's ceiling is zero, the discount box is not drawn at all — a box that refuses every number teaches people the form is broken. Why the associate ceiling ships at zero. The sample lists state 3% and 2% under named conditions and nothing else, while the order sheet shows 10% being given with nobody's name against it. Zero means every discount is somebody senior's decision until a manager deliberately raises it. The manager ceiling must sit at or above the associate one, or an associate could give what a manager could not sign off. A discount above the associate ceiling records who allowed it — the person saving, whose authority it was. A discount inside the associate ceiling records nobody, because nobody's permission was needed. The discount terms printed on a list (advance payment, quantity, prompt payment) are a different thing: they are part of the list the customer reads, not what a telecaller may knock off.

search.heading: Special price requests
search.text: From a call to a shop's own price. One special list per shop. An approved request puts the shop on a list named for it, scoped to that customer by name — which beats every other scope. A second approved price for the same shop joins the same list rather than creating another. The request records what the shop paid at the time, the list it was on, who asked, who decided and when, and the resulting list. The reason is required, and travels in the message. Whoever decides is not on the call. The person who asked is told the decision with the note in the message, not behind a link, because they have to ring the shop back and say something. Only the person who asked may withdraw a request, and only while it is waiting. A telecaller sees their own requests; a manager sees everybody's.

search.heading: Coverage and variance
search.text: - Coverage resolves every active customer in your book today and counts who is on which list, who is on no list (up to 200 listed), and who has no freight term. A published list nobody resolves to is called out. A shop on no list is being priced from memory. - Variance takes every priced line on the order sheet's Order Details tab for a month (up to 2,000) and compares the billed ex-GST rate with what the list says for that shop on that order date — at , below , above , or no list resolved — and totals what was given away below the list.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: An expired list still prices shops. The setting says a list past its validity is "drawn as expired on every screen rather than silently used". It is drawn as expired — but the resolver only checks status and the start/end dates, not validity, so an expired list keeps resolving for shops and pricing order lines until somebody replaces it. - Superseding ends the old list at once, not on the new list's start date. Publishing a version that starts next month marks the old one superseded immediately, and a superseded list prices nobody — shops on it have no list until the new one starts. - A shop's "agreed prices" list does not fall through. Its note says everything not listed falls through to the ordinary list, but a customer-named list wins the whole resolution: products not on it have no rate on the order form. - "Above the ceiling a manager authorises it" has no flow. The setting describes the order form asking for a manager to authorise; the code refuses the save. Nothing lets a manager authorise a telecaller's discount. - CRM managers are notified of special price requests they cannot decide. Deciding needs the price desk; the notification sends CRM managers to the CRM's Requests tab, which is read-only. - Variance resolves past months against today's lists. Superseded lists are excluded, so last month's lines are compared with this month's prices, despite the stated aim of resolving each row as of its own date. - Variance is not narrowed to your book. Every CRM user sees every billed line for the month. - The "saved order value" is still zero. With pricing.useListForOrderValue on, the form shows a total, but the order is saved with a value of zero and the "rates not held yet" warning; the list rate lives on each line instead. - Slabbed rates are not used on the order form or in variance — only a product's flat (no quantity band) rate is looked up. - The derivation check skips per-litre rules , so a derived "plus so much per litre" list is never warned about drift.

Reminders are rows in reminders . The list is listReminders in worklist-services.ts , which derives the display status on read. Writes come from three directions: the call and collections save paths insert rows inside their own transactions, the Reminders screen calls the services through lib/actions/crm.ts , and every event that could keep a promise calls closeRemindersOnEvidence inside its transaction — a thin wrapper around the pure engine in lib/engines/reminder-closure.ts .

search.text: A call that keeps a promise. search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A new kind of evidence goes in the engine. Add a ClosureEvent kind and its closes arm and closureNoteFor sentence, and a reminder closure source value. Then call closeRemindersOnEvidence from the new write path, inside its transaction. Never close what the same write created. Stamp call id on reminders a call writes, or pass exclude . Keep hand-closing behind the capability. Any new "close" or "dismiss" path must call requireCapability("reminder.close") and write an audit row. Keep the badge and Needs action the same count. Both are pending and due date on or before today. Change one, change the other.

A reminder is a promise somebody made to a customer — "I'll ring you back on Thursday", "I'll check the payment on the 20th", "I'll send the price list". Reminders is the list of every promise in your book, which are due today, which are already late, and which are coming up. You do not tick a reminder off. You make the call , and the call closes it.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: Reminders, on the Needs action tab. Reminders Set reminder Due today. 3 Overdue. 2 · oldest by 3 days Upcoming. 11 Closed. 40

search.heading: Keeping a promise
search.text: Open Needs action. Overdue first, then due today. These are the promises the Call Log is also putting at the top of your list. Press Call. The Call Log opens with the customer's panel. The reminder shows as the reason for the call. Log the call. Save it as usual. If the customer answered, every reminder for them that is due today or overdue closes, and the row moves to Closed with the line Closed by the call logged on … . If nobody answered. The reminder stays open — a ring that nobody picked up is not a promise kept. The row says Rang on … - no answer, so this is still owed , and the Call Log's no-answer ladder brings the customer back.

search.heading: What closes a reminder by itself
search.text: Event Closes Line on the closed row A call that got through Every reminder for that customer that is due today or overdue Closed by the call logged on … An order taken from the customer Their order confirmation reminders, whatever the date Closed by the order taken on … Money accounts confirmed Their payment promise reminders, whatever the date Closed by the payment accounts confirmed on … A person, by hand That one reminder Marked done by name on … A payment the customer only says they made does not close a payment promise. It closes when accounts find the money. The call in which they told you still closes any reminder that was due that day. A call never closes a reminder it created itself. If you save a Follow-up call for tomorrow, tomorrow's reminder stays open.

search.heading: Kinds of reminder
search.text: Kind Usually written by call back A Follow-up outcome, a callback asked for on a collections call, or Set reminder payment promise Payment Promised on a call, or Payment promised on a collections call — dated the working day after the promised date order confirmation A next action on a call information to send A next action on a call stock check A next action on a call other A next action on a call

search.heading: Rescheduling, carrying forward and dismissing
search.text: From the row menu (⋯): - Reschedule — pick a new date, optionally update what was promised. The row counts how many times it has moved; after moves it says so. - Carry forward to tomorrow — the next working day. - Hold other calls until date — only offered when another reason would bring the customer back to the Call Log first. It stops the Call Log asking about orders or check-ins until the promised day. Money and reminders are never held. - Open customer record . - Dismiss reminder — needs a reason, and only appears if you may close reminders by hand. A dismissed reminder is never deleted. A date that falls on a non-working day is moved to the next working day when is on. The message after saving says the date it actually landed on.

search.heading: For managers
search.text: On team scope you see your whole team's reminders, each with the person it is assigned to, and a card Overdue reminders by telecaller showing who is sitting on the overdue pile and how old their oldest is. Managers hold the right to Mark done and Dismiss by default; that can be moved on the Access screen.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Where did the Mark done button go?. A reminder is closed by doing what was promised — the call, the order, or confirmed money. Closing one by hand is now for the cases a call cannot reach (settled over WhatsApp, shop shut, written twice) and is given to managers. It is recorded as their decision. I rang them today and the reminder is still open.. Either nobody answered, or the reminder is not due yet — a call on Tuesday does not keep a promise made for the 20th. The row says which. Will the Call Log remind me?. Yes. A reminder due today or overdue puts the customer at the top of your Call Log, and a reminder that falls due during the day is added to the top of a list that is otherwise settled for the day. What does 'An earlier reason would call this customer sooner' mean?. The customer would come back to your Call Log before the promised date — say, a stock check due on Tuesday for a promise on Friday. Use Hold other calls until … if your promise covers it. The badge says 6 but I only see 4.. The badge counts due-today and overdue reminders together — the Needs action tab. The Due today and Overdue tabs each show half of it.

A reminder is the CRM's record of a promise somebody made to a customer . It has a date, a sentence saying what was promised, a type, and a person it is assigned to. It is not a task list: the whole design is aimed at one question a manager needs answered honestly — are we keeping our promises? That is why a reminder is closed by evidence that it was kept, and why closing one any other way is a decision somebody senior makes and is recorded against their name.

search.heading: Where reminders come from
search.text: Almost every reminder is written for the telecaller, inside the same save as the call that produced it. Source Type Date Call outcome Follow-up call back The date chosen, or day(s) out Call outcome Payment Promised payment promise The promised date, or days out A dated next action on a call From the action — payment chases are payment promise , dispatch chases order confirmation , stock check stock , sending material information to send The next-action date Collections call Payment promised payment promise, set by the system The working day after the promised date — the promise is chased once it has passed Collections call Call back later call back, set by the system The date the customer asked for Set reminder on the Reminders screen or a customer record call back The date typed Non-working days roll forward. When is on, a due date that falls on a non-working day moves to the next working day. Carry forward always lands on the next working day.

search.heading: Due, overdue and upcoming are worked out, never stored
search.text: A reminder stores its date and whether it is pending , completed or dismissed . Whether it is overdue , due today or upcoming is decided every time it is read, by comparing the date with today's business date. A stored "overdue" flag needs a nightly job to move it, and a job that fails leaves the screen lying. Comparing on read cannot drift.

search.heading: What closes a promise
search.text: Closing on evidence. A call closes what was due. An answered call closes reminders due today or earlier — never one still ahead. A customer rung on Tuesday about something else has not had the conversation promised for the 20th. An order or confirmed money closes what was about exactly that. An order closes order confirmation reminders and confirmed money closes payment promise reminders, whatever their date. A payment promised for the 20th that lands on the 15th leaves nothing to ring about on the 20th. A ring nobody answered is not a promise kept. An unanswered call closes nothing. Otherwise the overdue pile could be cleared by dialling and hanging up — the very escape the manual button used to give. Reported money is not evidence. Money the customer says has arrived is not money the business has seen. The payment promise closes when accounts confirm the receipt. A save never closes what it created. A call whose outcome is "follow up tomorrow" writes tomorrow's promise; the same call must not then close it. Every reminder a call writes is stamped with that call, and the closure pass skips it. For a call or an order, the closing happens inside the same transaction as the save. A reminder closed outside it would survive a rolled-back call — the promise gone and no record of the conversation that supposedly closed it.

search.heading: The closed row says what closed it
search.text: Closed by What the row says What it means call Closed by the call logged on … There is a call to open order Closed by the order taken on … There is an order payment Closed by the payment accounts confirmed on … There is a confirmed receipt person Marked done / dismissed by name on … Somebody stood behind it personally (nothing recorded) Closed on … Closed before this was tracked — nothing is backfilled

search.heading: Closing by hand is a capability
search.text: Mark done and Dismiss both need reminder.close , which comes with the CRM manager level. Both are checked on the server, both are written to the audit log, and dismissing needs a reason. Why a telecaller cannot tick their own reminder off. "Mark done" recorded that a button was pressed and nothing about whether the call was made. The overdue pile could be cleared in a minute by the one person whose work it measured, and no screen could tell a promise kept from a promise tidied away. Dismissing is gated by the same capability because a reason typed into a dismissal clears the pile exactly as well as a tick.

search.heading: Reminders and the Call Log
search.text: A pending reminder is one of the Call Log's strongest reasons to ring: Reminder is Call Log reason Overdue Reminder N days overdue — ranked above every order reason Due today Reminder due today - A reminder outranks the quiet window after an order, the cooldown after "no order", and the WhatsApp cooldown — a callback the customer asked for is not chasing. - It does not outrank do-not-contact, a call already made today, or an open order on the sheet. - The Call Log is settled once a day, but a reminder that falls due during the day is added at the top.

search.heading: Holding other calls until the promise
search.text: When a telecaller promises a callback for Friday and the rules would otherwise bring the customer back on Tuesday for a stock check, the screen offers Hold other calls until Friday . That is the telecaller's own decision, never inferred. While it holds, order and check-in reasons are silenced for that customer; money, reminders and "unreachable" are not. It can only be set on a pending reminder whose date is still ahead.

search.heading: Who sees which reminders
search.text: A reminder belongs to the person it is assigned to . A telecaller sees their own; a manager on team scope sees their team's, with who each is assigned to, and a card ranking who has the most overdue. Reminders for a lead that has been moved to the trash are hidden and come back with it.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Rescheduling and "Hold other calls" do not check the reminder is in your book. The actions look the reminder up by its id and change it; nothing confirms the customer or the assignee is in the caller's scope. - A manager's Reminders badge counts every pending reminder in the company , while the list underneath is narrowed to their team — so the badge and the Needs action tab disagree for a manager. - "Upcoming" includes every future reminder , however far out; nothing groups this week from next quarter. - Confirmed money closes its payment promises just after the confirmation is written , not inside the same transaction — a failure between the two would leave the money confirmed and the promise open. - Rescheduling is not audited , unlike closing and dismissing — a reminder moved ten times shows the count but not who moved it or from when.

Every CRM write is in actions/lead-samples.ts and begins with one loader that checks scope and the state machine; the review chase is a pure engine run hourly; the seven feedback answers are their own table, one row per sample. Every block below is cut from the source this deployment was built from.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A new state is a new edge in ALLOWED, and nowhere else. Add it to mbos sample state (hand-written migration, cast enum literals ::text ), to SampleState , to ALLOWED , to STATE WORDS , and to the handset's own machine. Never default one date from another. received at is the shop's; delivered at the carrier's. A new date gets its own column and its own assertion. Chases close, they do not delete. Use closeNurtureTasks with a sentence. A deleted chase loses the record that the parcel was slow. Keep the rejection check and the derivation on the same three fields. If you change which fields feed rejection reason , change the validation with it, on both the CRM and the handset.

Samples & trials is where a sample's whole life is worked: somebody asks for a can to give a shop, a manager says yes or no, it is sent, the shop confirms it arrived, they try it, and somebody writes down what they thought. A sample with no feedback is stock given away , so every screen here is built around getting that answer. You reach it from Lead Management → Samples & trials in the CRM sidebar (it is also linked under Other desks on All Leads). The same four tabs exist on the Sales Dashboard; the screens are identical, only who you see differs — see Whose samples you see. The numbers on this page — which days a review is chased on, how long before a parcel is chased — are the settings your CRM is using right now, read live.

search.heading: The four tabs
search.text: Tab What it answers You use it to All samples What is out with customers, and which have no feedback yet See what is late and who owes an answer Desk Where each sample has got to, and what it is owed next Approve, record dispatch, confirm receipt, record the review, call it off Review chases Which trials are waiting on an answer, and how many times we have asked Find the shops to ring yourself Trial feedback What every trial said, across products and competitors Read patterns — "price was the problem in nine of eleven" Click any sample's customer to open the lead; open a sample itself to see its full history on the sample record .

search.heading: The desk at a glance
search.text: The sample desk, with one request waiting and one trial waiting on a review. Sample desk 2 trials chased 3 times with no answer — these are the ones to ring yourself Waiting on approval. 3 Late in delivery. 1 Delivered, not reviewed. 4 On the desk. 17

search.heading: A sample, step by step
search.text: Somebody asks for one. A sample is asked for from the lead record ( Ask for a sample ), from the call assistant, or by a salesman on the handset. You give the product , how many cans , what it will be used on , and why they want one (a choice from a list such as Wants to compare it with another brand ). For a lead on the Direct or Third-party ladder, a sample can only be asked for once its Qualification is complete and the Sales Manager has verified it . If not, you are told exactly what is still to do and nothing is created. For an older lead, a sample asked for before the lead is Qualified is allowed but marked "Lead not qualified — Manager approval required." so the person approving it knows. A manager approves or refuses. On the desk, press Approve or Refuse . A refusal must say why — "Say why — the salesman cannot work it out from the word alone." The salesman's handset hears the answer. Only managers and admins can make this decision. Record the dispatch. Press Record dispatch and give the courier , the docket number and the date they promised delivery. All three are required: a docket nobody can chase is a sample nobody will review, and the promised date is what the late flag is measured against. Confirm it was received. When the shop says they have it, press Confirm received → They have it . This is the shop's word — not the courier's website. It starts the review clock. Record what they thought. Press Record feedback and fill in the seven questions (below), then pick the verdict: Approved , Rejected or More testing . At least one answer is required, and a rejection must say why. Or call it off. At any point before the review, Call off ends the trial. Pick one of the reasons; Other needs a sentence.

search.heading: What each state means
search.text: State on the screen Stored as Meaning What it is owed Asked for requested Somebody asked; nobody has decided A manager's yes or no Approved approved Yes — it can go out Dispatch Refused rejected A manager said no, with a reason Nothing. Refused — nothing to send Sent dispatched It has left us, with a courier and docket The shop confirming receipt Delivered received The shop says they have it Their review Tried trial done They have used it Their review Reviewed reviewed Their verdict is written down Nothing — the trial is closed Cancelled cancelled Called off, with a coded reason Nothing State and verdict are two different things. The state is where the sample has got to. The verdict is what the customer thought of it — Awaiting feedback , Approved , Rejected or More testing . "Approved" in the State column means a manager said it may go out; "Approved" as a verdict means the customer liked it. The All samples list shows the verdict; the Desk shows the state.

search.heading: The three dates
search.text: The sample record shows three dates side by side, because three different people say three different things: Date Who says it What it means It left us We say The day it was dispatched It arrived The carrier says Delivery, as reported by the courier or our own man It is in our hands The shop says The confirmed receipt — the only date the review is counted from Confirming receipt on the desk records only the third date. A sample that sat in a courier office for four days and one handed over the same afternoon must not look the same.

search.heading: The seven feedback questions
search.text: Question What to write Quality What they thought of the product itself Performance How it performed in use Application How it went on — spraying, brushing, coverage Drying Drying time against what they expected Compared with what they use now The comparison against their current brand — the whole point of a trial Price What they said about the price Anything else Anything that does not fit above A rejection needs a reason. If the verdict is Rejected , at least one of Anything else , Price or Compared with what they use now must be filled in. Otherwise you will see: "A rejected trial has to say why — the price, the comparison against what they use now, or in your own words. Without it the next sample goes out exactly the same." The review is recorded once . A second opinion is a second sample.

search.heading: What each verdict does
search.text: Approved. The trial is closed and an "Call about the order" task goes to the lead manager. When the verdict comes from the handset, the lead is also moved up to Negotiation if its checklist allows. Rejected. The trial is closed with the reason on the record. The salesman and the lead manager are told why. More testing. They want to try it again — neither yes nor no. The lead stays where it is.

search.heading: Review chases
search.text: Review chases — every trial waiting on an answer, most-asked first. Review chases The review is chased on the days in after the shop confirmed receipt , and after the last of those the last gap repeats — it never stops until somebody records the verdict or calls the sample off. Each ask becomes a task for the lead manager (or the salesman, where there is no lead manager), and the third ask onward is marked high priority. A sample with no confirmed receipt cannot be chased — the screen lists those separately and tells you to confirm receipt on the desk.

search.heading: Trial feedback
search.text: The Trial feedback tab is a library: every trial's seven answers, filterable by product , competitor and verdict . The verdict counts follow your filters, so "of the trials against this competitor, how many did we lose" is one click. It writes nothing. At the bottom, Trials called off counts every cancelled sample by reason, grouped by whose problem it was: Group Reasons Whose to fix Supply Product not available · Wrong product or wrong need We could not give them the right stock Customer No longer needs it · Delayed the trial · Sample not needed any more · Not replying The shop stopped replying, delayed, or does not want it now Sales Price or terms problem The talk about price and terms stopped it (on its own) Other Always needs a sentence

search.heading: Parcels that do not arrive
search.text: - When a salesman records a dispatch from the handset, a task "Where is the sample — Customer A" is raised days after dispatch for the account's back office person . If the account has none, it goes to the lead manager , and the task says so: "This is on your list because no back office person is named on this account — naming one sends the next chase to them." - Once a dispatched sample passes the date the courier promised, a "Sample has not arrived" task is raised once for the lead manager (or the salesman). - Confirming receipt closes those chases as done — it does not delete them, so the record still shows the parcel was slow.

search.heading: Whose samples you see
search.text: Screen You see All samples, Desk As a telecaller or salesman: the samples you asked for . As a manager: your region's salesmen, or every sample if no region has been allocated to you. Review chases, sample record Samples on customers in your book (your own as a telecaller, your team's as a manager).

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I pressed Approve on All samples and it said to use the samples desk.. Decide sample requests on the Desk tab. The approval there checks the stock and the lead; the button on All samples cannot decide a sample. Why can't I ask for a sample for this lead?. On the Direct and Third-party ladders a sample needs the lead's Qualification complete and verified by the Sales Manager. The message lists exactly what is still missing — finish those and ask again. The review call is not on anybody's list.. The chase counts from the day the shop confirmed receipt. If nobody pressed Confirm received , there is no date to count from. Confirm it on the desk. Can I change the review after saving it?. No. The verdict is recorded once. If they want to try again, that is a new sample. The sample arrived, but the shop says it was the wrong one.. A sample cannot go back a step. Call it off with Wrong product or wrong need and ask for another. What does 'Asked 4 times' mean for me as a manager?. The automatic chase has asked four times and nobody has an answer. Ring the shop yourself.

A sample is stock given away in the hope of an order, so the rules around it all serve one purpose: no sample goes out to a shop nobody has established anything about, and no sample that went out is allowed to go quiet. This tab explains the sample's journey, the three dates it carries, how the review is chased, what each verdict does to the lead, and why each rule is shaped the way it is. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: State and verdict are two questions
search.text: A sample carries a state — where it has got to — and a verdict — what the customer thought. The sample's journey (state). The verdict is one of pending , approved , rejected or more testing . With one column, a sample approved three weeks ago and never dispatched looked identical to one under evaluation — when it is really stock nobody gave away and an opportunity nobody took. And more testing is a real third verdict, not a shrug: "they want to try it again on a different substrate" is neither yes nor no, and recording it as pending would lose the fact that a trial happened. A sample never goes back a step. "It did not really arrive" is not an edit; it is a fact about the delivery. The honest record is to cancel with the reason and send another. Rewinding would make the timeline read as though the first delivery never happened, on a record somebody has already been told about. Any other move is refused with a sentence naming where the sample actually is — "This sample is on its way, so it cannot be marked reviewed."

search.heading: Before a sample can be asked for
search.text: On the direct and third-party ladders a sample can be requested only once Qualification is complete and verified — the eight answers, the sales manager's review, the GST validated and the figures fresh (see Intake and qualification). Otherwise nothing is created and the screen lists what is still to do. For an older lead with no sales type, a sample asked for below the rung where a sample is normally wanted is allowed but marked Lead not qualified — Manager approval required. A real customer with no lead stage at all is never marked. Before stock leaves the godown, somebody should already know the product, roughly how much they use, what they could be worth and the brand it is up against. A trial aimed at a shop nobody has established anything about has no requirement to measure the result against and no competitor to compare it with — the commonest way a sample becomes stock given away for nothing. The request carries a product, a can count, what it will be used on, and a coded reason from .

search.heading: Approving and dispatching
search.text: - Approving or refusing needs the sample-approval permission (managers and admins). A refusal must say why, because the salesman cannot work it out from the word alone. - Dispatching needs a courier, a docket number and the date the courier promised. A docket nobody can chase is a sample nobody will review, and the promised date is what the late flag is measured against.

search.heading: The three dates
search.text: Date Who asserts it Column It left us We do dispatched It arrived The carrier, or our own man delivered It is in their hands The shop received The review is counted from confirmed receipt — never from dispatch. A review timed from the day we posted it rings a customer still waiting for the parcel, and that call teaches them we do not know where our own stock is. Confirming receipt records only the shop's date; it never fills in the carrier's, and the carrier's date never fills in the shop's. A default would assert something nobody asked the customer.

search.heading: Chasing a parcel that has not arrived
search.text: Who chases a sample in transit. The window is days after dispatch. Why the task says why it landed where it did. The back-office seat is the brief's "logistics" person. Where nobody holds it, the chase still has to happen — a sample that never arrives is the quietest way a lead dies, because the salesman assumes it is being tried and the shop assumes we forgot. So it falls to the lead manager, and says so: naming the reason turns a silent fallback into a gap somebody can fix. A chase is closed by the answer, never deleted — "we asked where this parcel was and then it arrived" is the only way anybody finds out a courier is the problem.

search.heading: Chasing the review
search.text: Once the shop confirms receipt, the review is asked for on the days in , counted from receipt. After the last of those, the last gap repeats — it never stops. Ask Day after receipt (shipped ladder 2, 4, 6) Task 1 2 Sample review call 2 4 Sample review call — ask 2 3 6 … — ask 3 , "Asked 2 times already with no answer. Worth ringing yourself." 4 8 … — ask 4 5 10 and so on Each ask is a task for the lead manager, or the salesman where there is none. The chase runs on the hourly job; two passes on one day raise one ask, and each ask is keyed on its own number, so it is never raised twice. The count of asks is kept on the sample so a screen can say "asked three times" — the number that tells a manager to pick up the phone. A trial nobody reviewed is stock given away for nothing. A ladder that gave up after three asks would quietly turn every hard-to-reach customer into a write-off with no decision recorded. Somebody ends it by getting an answer, or by calling the sample off and saying why. Recording the verdict closes every open chase on the sample.

search.heading: The verdict: seven answers, not one word
search.text: Feedback is seven fields — quality, performance, application, drying, compared with what they use now, price, and anything else — because "good" cannot be read back. The whole point of a trial is the comparison, and a note field cannot later be read as "better drying than the incumbent, price is the problem". - At least one of the seven must be filled. - The review is recorded once ; a second save of the same sample changes nothing. A second opinion is a second sample. A rejected sample has to say why. A rejection is refused unless anything else , price or compared with what they use now is filled — the same three fields the stored rejection reason is drawn from. Without it the next sample goes out exactly the same. The handset checks the same three.

search.heading: What each verdict does
search.text: Verdict Effect on the trial Effect on the lead Approved Closed; chases closed A Call about the order task for the lead manager. From the handset , the lead is moved to Negotiation through its gate (if the gate refuses, the message says what is missing). From the CRM , the lead is not moved — press Move to Negotiation on the record; the gate now passes. Rejected Closed with the reason Salesman and lead manager told why More testing Closed as reviewed No move — the trial has not finished saying anything Why approval opens Negotiation. The sample review is what authorises a commercial conversation — not the salesman deciding he is ready for one. Negotiation's gate requires a sample sent, feedback written and the trial approved, so the gate and the thing that opens it are one mechanism.

search.heading: Calling a sample off
search.text: Call off is allowed from any state before the review, with a coded reason from ( Other needs words). Cancelling closes every task raised for the sample. The Trial feedback tab groups cancellations by whose problem they were — supply, customer or sales.

search.heading: Who sees and does what
search.text: Action Who Ask for a sample, confirm receipt, record feedback, call it off Lead work — every associate in scope Approve or refuse The sample-approval permission — managers and admins See samples The same lead scope as All Leads: your own book in the CRM, your team or territory as a manager

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - An approved verdict opens Negotiation only from the handset. AGENTS.md says an approved sample opens negotiation; the CRM's recordSampleFeedback raises the order-call task and does not move the lead ( actions/lead-samples.ts ), while the handset's afterSampleVerdict does ( actions/mbos.ts ). - Two review triggers.
