Close/Reopen is a flag on the customer row , raised by two request actions and cleared by two decide actions, with one unscoped read ( listCustomerStatusRequests ) rendering both directions as one queue. There is no requests table: the pending state, the reason, who asked and when all live on customers . The status the decision writes, deactivated , is the one value of customer status that the inactivity engine reads but never writes.

search.heading: Asking to close
search.text: requestDeactivation takes ids and a reason. It resolves scope and — before writing — selects the ids through scopedToUsers(scopedUserIds(ctx.scope)) ; any shortfall refuses the whole call with not permitted . It then stamps the flag, the reason, deactivation requested by id and deactivation requested at , and inserts a notifications row per user whose users.role is manager or admin .

search.heading: Deciding a close
search.text: Approval sets status decided at , which is what keeps the party sheet's Deactive column from restating the status later. Rejection clears the flag and deactivation reason .

search.heading: Asking to reopen
search.text: Filters the selection to rows already deactivated and flags only those; returns conflict if none qualify. Notifies through notifyUsers with href: "/crm/status-requests" .

search.heading: Deciding a reopen
search.text: Approval sets active , nulls every deactivation column and the reactivation request, and also sets status decided at — clearing deactivation reason destroyed the only evidence the projection used to read, so without the mark the next sync re-closed the account. recomputeInactivity then moves a long-quiet customer straight to inactive .

It is not scoped : a request is work for whoever decides it, and narrowing to the decider's book would hide most of them. It is not aliased because ASSIGNED TO SQL names customers directly. The sidebar badge asks the same capability the route does, so a telecaller never gets a count for a screen they are refused:

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: Keep 'deactivated' out of every engine. No recompute, sync or job may write or clear deactivated . If a new automatic path needs to close accounts, route it through a request a person decides. Set status decided at on every human status write. Any new action that changes a customer's status must stamp it, or the party projection will overwrite the decision on the next pass. Gate deciding on the capability, never on isManager. The route, the sidebar, the badge and the actions all ask customer.deactivate . A screen that draws decide buttons from isManager will offer buttons the server refuses. Re-run inactivity after a decision. Both decide actions call recomputeInactivity(customerId) ; keep that, or a reopened quiet customer reads as active and a closed one keeps its watch row. Add a Journey 5 test. Every behaviour on this page has an integration test; a new rule without one is a rule nobody can tell has broken.

Close/Reopen is where requests to close a customer account, or to bring a closed one back , wait for a manager's answer. A telecaller asks; a manager decides. Nothing on this list has changed a customer's status yet — a request only changes something when a manager approves it. There are two halves to this page. If you are a telecaller , you only ever ask — from the Call Log or from the customer list — and you never see the Close/Reopen screen itself. If you are a manager , Close/Reopen is your queue: one list for both directions, oldest first.

search.heading: Asking for an account to be closed
search.text: You find out a shop has shut, a record is a duplicate, or somebody on the list is not a customer at all. You cannot close the account yourself — you ask, with a reason. Open the row menu (⋯). On the Call Log , open the menu on the customer's row and choose Request deactivation . On the Customers list, open the row menu and choose Request deactivation , or tick several customers and press Request deactivation in the bar that appears at the bottom. Say why. A window asks Request deactivation for Customer A? and will not let you continue without a reason. Write what a manager needs to decide: "Shop closed in August — owner confirmed on the phone", "Duplicate of Customer B". The manager decides on your words, so make them specific. Press Request deactivation. You see Deactivation requested - a manager decides . Every manager is told. Carry on as normal. The customer stays visible and stays on your list until a manager approves. The menu item now reads Deactivation already requested and is greyed out — hovering it says Asked for already - a manager has yet to decide . On the Customers list the row carries a Deactivation asked badge. Ticking several customers at once. A bulk request goes through only if every ticked customer is in your book. If even one belongs to somebody else, the whole request is refused with Some of those customers are not in your book. — nothing is flagged. Untick the ones that are not yours and try again.

search.heading: Asking for a closed account to be reopened
search.text: A closed customer is off every calling list, and an order from them does not reopen the account by itself. Somebody has to ask. Find them on the Customers list. Filter the status to Deactivated to see closed accounts. Choose Request reactivation. From the row menu, or tick the customers and press Request reactivation in the bottom bar. The bar only offers reactivation when every ticked customer is deactivated; a mixed selection offers Request deactivation instead. Say what has changed. The window reads Ask to bring back Customer A? — "The reason is what the manager decides on, so say what has changed." Then press Request reactivation . Wait for the decision. The row shows Reactivation asked and the menu item reads Reactivation already asked for . The customer stays off every list until a manager approves.

search.heading: The Close/Reopen screen (managers)
search.text: The queue, with one request in each direction. Customer status requests Waiting. 3 To close. 2 To reopen. 1 Owing money. 1 Waiting to be closed or reopened.

search.heading: Reading a row
search.text: Column What it shows Customer The account name (click it to open the record), and underneath, whose book it is in — or Nobody assigned . Asked for Close the account or Bring it back . Reason What the person who asked wrote. No reason recorded on very old requests. Asked by Who asked, and the day. Not recorded / date not recorded on requests raised before the system stored the asker. Outstanding What they still owe, highlighted when it is more than zero. Last order The date of their last order, or never . The list is sorted oldest first — the longest wait is the one somebody has been waiting on. Requests with no recorded date sit at the bottom.

search.heading: Deciding a request
search.text: Press Approve or Reject. A confirmation opens. Its wording depends on what you are doing. Read what it says will happen. Approving a close: Customer A is marked deactivated. Nothing is deleted — every call, order and bill stays queryable — but they leave the calling queue, the collections worklist and the inactive watch. If they owe money, it adds that the debt is not written off but nobody will be prompted to chase it. If they ordered in the last month, it says so. Approving a reopen: Customer D goes back to active and returns to the calling queue on their own buying cycle. The deactivation reason on the record is cleared. Rejecting either: Nothing changes about Customer A. The request leaves this list, and whoever asked will need to be told why. Confirm. Press Yes, do it (or Reject the request ). You see Customer deactivated , Customer brought back or Request rejected , and the row leaves the list. Tell the person who asked. The system does not notify them of your decision. If you rejected it, ring or message them. You can also decide from the Customers list: on a row with a pending request, a manager's menu shows Approve deactivation / Reject the request (or Approve reactivation / Reject the request ) instead of the request item. It is the same decision.

search.heading: What closing an account does — and does not do
search.text: It does. - Marks the customer Deactivated . - Takes them off the Call Log , the Payment Follow-up worklist and the inactive watch . - Records who closed it, when, and why. - Stops the order sheet changing this account's status from now on. It does not. - Delete anything. Every call, order, bill and payment stays on the record. - Write off what they owe. The bills and the balance stay. - Reopen itself if they order again — only a manager approving a reopen does that.

search.heading: Statuses you will see
search.text: Status Who sets it Means Active The system Buying, or not yet quiet for long enough to worry about. Inactive The system, every night Gone quiet for × their own buying cycle. An order puts them back to Active on its own. Deactivated A manager , here Closed on purpose. Nothing automatic ever sets or clears it.

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I asked for a customer to be closed. Why are they still on my Call Log?. Asking does not close anything. They stay on your list until a manager approves. If you do not want to ring them today, use Skip for today with a reason. The Request deactivation item is greyed out.. Somebody — maybe you — has already asked, and no manager has decided yet. Hover it to see Asked for already - a manager has yet to decide . A closed customer has just placed an order. Are they back?. No. An order never reopens a deactivated account; that was somebody's decision. Ask for Request reactivation on the Customers list and a manager will decide. I can't see Close/Reopen in my sidebar.. Only people who can decide requests see it — CRM and Sales managers and administrators. A telecaller asks from the Call Log or Customers list and never needs the screen. My request disappeared from the list but the customer is not closed.. A manager rejected it. The reason you wrote was cleared with it, and you are not notified — ask your manager why. The customer owes money. Should I still ask for them to be closed?. You can, but say so in the reason. The manager sees the balance on the screen, and closing the account means nobody will be prompted to chase it. Will the spreadsheet reopen a customer I closed?. No. Once a manager has decided a customer's status here — either way — the order sheet's customer master stops speaking for that account's status.

Close/Reopen exists because closing a customer account is a decision, not a measurement . Everything else about a customer's status is worked out by the system from what they buy; deactivated is the one status a person chooses. So it is split into two acts — somebody who knows the account asks , with a reason, and somebody who can decide decides — and the decision sticks until a person reverses it. This tab explains the rules, why each exists, and who can do what.

search.heading: Three statuses, two authors
search.text: A customer's status is one of three values. Two belong to the system; one belongs to a person. Who moves a customer between statuses. Inactive is derived. Deactivated is decided.. Inactive is the inactivity engine's own output: a customer who has gone × their own buying cycle without an order is marked inactive, and an order marks them active again — nobody types it. Deactivated is never written by that engine, and never cleared by it. A deactivated customer is skipped entirely when inactivity is worked out, and an order from them changes nothing. An order does not undo a deactivation because the deactivation was somebody's judgement — the shop shut, the record was a duplicate, the account was closed on purpose. If an automatic rule could reverse it, the next stray order would quietly put a closed account back on somebody's Call Log, and nobody could tell a decision from an accident. The way back is a request, the same shape as the way out.

search.heading: The two-step: ask, then decide
search.text: A close request, from the Call Log to the decision. Asking needs a reason, and nothing changes until somebody decides. Every request — close or reopen — must carry a reason; an empty one is refused. While a request waits, the customer is exactly as they were: still on the Call Log, still chased for money, still visible everywhere. Only approval changes the status. You can only ask about customers in your own book. A close request is checked against the asker's book before anything is written. A bulk request that includes even one customer outside it is refused whole — Some of those customers are not in your book. A manager's book is their team's; an admin's is everyone's. Refusing the whole batch rather than flagging the ones that match is deliberate. A bulk action that silently flags nineteen of twenty and reports success is worse than one that refuses: nobody re-reads a list they have been told went through. Only a closed customer can be asked back. A reopen request names only deactivated customers. If none of the selection is deactivated it is refused ( That customer is not deactivated, so there is nothing to bring back. ); if some are, only those are flagged and the message says how many — Reactivation requested for 2 of 5 - the rest were not deactivated .

search.heading: Who can decide
search.text: Deciding a request — in either direction — needs the Deactivate customers permission. It is a manager's power: In practice that is a manager on the CRM or on the Sales Dashboard , and every administrator . An Accounts manager does not hold it. The screen itself is the module . Two checks guard it, because they answer different questions: Check Question If it fails The module grant Was this person given the screen? Redirected to the first CRM screen they hold The permission Can this person decide what the screen queues? Redirected to the CRM dashboard Why the permission check as well as the module. A module nobody has narrowed reaches everybody who holds the CRM — "no module rows means every module". Without the second check, every telecaller would see an approval queue holding their own requests. The sidebar link and its count badge follow the same permission, so a telecaller never sees either. Withholding the module from one manager does not stop requests reaching the others — the ask still notifies everybody who might decide.

search.heading: Approving a close
search.text: - The status becomes deactivated , and the record keeps who closed it, when , and why (the asker's reason, unless the decider supplies another). - The request flag is cleared. - The status is marked as decided by a person — see below. - An audit entry records the change and which of the decider's roles authorised it. - The customer leaves the Call Log , the collections worklist and the inactive watch (their watch row is cleared on the re-check that follows). - Nothing is deleted and nothing is written off . Calls, orders, bills and the balance remain. Closing an account that owes money. The debt stays on the books and on the customer's statement. What stops is the chasing: a deactivated customer is not on the Payment Follow-up worklist, so nobody will be prompted to ring about it again. That is why the screen counts Owing money in red, and the confirmation names the amount before you approve.

search.heading: Approving a reopen
search.text: - The status becomes active and every deactivation field — date, who, reason — is cleared , along with the request. - The inactivity check runs straight away. A customer who has been quiet for months goes straight back to inactive rather than reading as freshly active — coming back does not fake activity. - The customer returns to the Call Log on their own buying cycle. Why the old reason is cleared. A stale reason left on a live account is how a screen ends up explaining a deactivation that was reversed in March. The audit log keeps both decisions; the customer record describes the state the customer is in.

search.heading: Rejecting
search.text: Rejecting a close clears the request and the reason that came with it . Rejecting a reopen clears that request and its reason. The customer's status does not change. Either way, an audit entry is written.

search.heading: The order sheet cannot overrule a decision
search.text: The customer master in the order spreadsheet has its own status column, and an account marked Deactive there is closed when the sheet syncs. Once a manager has decided an account's status here — either way — that account is marked as decided, and the sheet stops speaking for its status from then on. It used to work in one direction only. The sync already refused to reopen an account closed in the CRM, but an account somebody had deliberately brought back was closed again on the next pass, for as long as the cell said Deactive. The mark now covers both directions. Where the sheet still disagrees, the disagreement is recorded as a sync conflict so somebody can correct the spreadsheet, rather than the two fighting silently.

search.heading: Notifications
search.text: Event Who is told Where the notification leads A close is requested Every user whose highest level anywhere is manager or admin The Customers list A reopen is requested The same people The Close/Reopen screen A request is approved or rejected Nobody —

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: Found while writing this page. These are listed so nobody is surprised; each is a candidate for a fix. - The person who asked is never told the answer. Neither decision sends a notification; the confirmation itself says "whoever asked will need to be told why". - A close-request notification points at the Customers list , not at Close/Reopen; a reopen request points at Close/Reopen. - Notifications go to everyone whose widest level is manager or admin , including managers who cannot decide (an Accounts or Reports manager), rather than to holders of the deciding permission. - The request dialogs promise the reason "is kept on the record either way" — but rejecting a close clears it. - Reopen requests are not checked against the asker's book , unlike close requests. - The Accounts app's customer list draws Approve/Reject for any manager , including an Accounts manager who will be refused by the server. - A second close request overwrites the first — the reason, the asker and the date are replaced, not kept. The screens grey the item out, but the server does not refuse it.

Monthly Targets is a list of the customers in your book, each with what they are expected to buy this month and what they have bought so far. Its second tab, Top customers , is the company's best customers over the last 3, 6 or 12 months, showing which of them are in your book. A manager or accounts sets the targets; everybody else reads them. Numbers on this page are your CRM's current settings.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: Monthly targets, for a manager. Monthly targets Allocate target All sales people All sales managers All back office All statuses

search.heading: What the badges mean
search.text: Badge Means Set by hand A manager or accounts typed this target for this month. Carried forward Set by hand last month and continuing unchanged — nobody has touched it this month. Auto default Derived from what the customer bought in recent months; nobody chose this number.

search.heading: Who is on the list
search.text: Only direct customers — accounts we invoice ourselves. A lead has never bought from us, so a target against it could never be met. A third-party shop is billed through its distributor, so its sales already count on that distributor's target. Both join the list on their own once they start buying from us directly. A customer who has gone quiet keeps their target — that gap is exactly what the month has to explain. Only a deactivated account leaves.

search.heading: Setting a target
search.text: Press Change target on a row, or Allocate target. Choose one customer, or apply to every customer your filters currently match. Enter the rupees, the bills, or both. The target is the rupee amount for the month. The bill target is how many sales bills you want raised, one or more. A target has to ask for at least one of the two. Save target. The row now says Set by hand . Next month it carries forward unless somebody changes it. If you cannot see Allocate target or Change target , setting targets is a manager or accounts action. You can still read every figure.

search.heading: How achieved is counted
search.text: Achieved is the value of the customer's orders this month that accounts have approved — the same figure every sales report uses. An order still waiting for approval, or one that was declined, does not count. The figure is net of GST, after discount, the same unit a target is written in.

search.heading: Top customers
search.text: Top customers — the company list, filtered to your book. 3 months 6 months 1 year Their sales Their orders - The report is made on the 1st of each month at 10:00 , covering whole months ending with the one just finished, and is then frozen for the month. Before 10:00 on the 1st you still see last month's. - The company's top are chosen across every book first; then you are shown the ones in your book. An administrator sees all of them. If none are yours: None of the top customers are in your book .

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: Why is this lead not on the targets list?. A lead has never bought from us. It appears once it becomes a customer by ordering. The customer ordered yesterday but Achieved has not moved.. The order is waiting for accounts to approve it. Achieved counts approved orders only. Where did an Auto default come from?. From what the customer bought over recent months, with an uplift. Change it and it becomes Set by hand. Why is the top customers list missing rank 3?. Rank 3 is somebody else's customer. Ranks are company-wide. Is this my own sales target?. No. These are per-customer targets. Your own target is on My Performance.

Monthly Targets measures the month per customer : what each account we invoice is expected to buy, what it has bought, and the gap. It is a different grain from a person's target on My Performance — one asks "which of our shops are short", the other "how is this salesperson's month going" — and the two are deliberately two screens. Top customers, the second tab, is a frozen monthly report of the company's best accounts. Values shown are read live from your CRM.

search.heading: Every customer has a target, and says where it came from
search.text: Where a customer's monthly target comes from. Only a decision carries forward. A target somebody typed carries into next month unchanged. A default does not — a default is this month's guess at what somebody will buy, computed fresh, and carrying a guess forward as though it were a decision is how a customer ends up with a target nobody asked for. The default is over the last months, plus %. Those months are measured in the same unit a target is written in — net of GST, after discount — or the proposal would be about 18% above the month it came from. A customer who joined mid-month has their first month's default pro-rated while is on.

search.heading: Who is measured
search.text: A target is set on an account we invoice, and nothing else. Only direct customers are on the list, using the same definition the Customers list's type filter reads. A lead has never bought from us, so a target against it is one nobody could meet, and it dragged the whole list's achievement down. A third-party shop is billed to its distributor, so its sales already count on that account — counting them here would be the same money twice. Setting a target on either is refused by the server, not only hidden. A customer who has gone inactive keeps their target — that gap is what the month must explain. Only deactivation removes them.

search.heading: What "achieved" means
search.text: Achieved is the value of approved orders in the month, net of GST and after discount. An order waiting for accounts or declined by them does not count — "did we sell anything" has one definition across the product. The bill count is the number of sales bills raised in the month.

search.heading: Rupees, bills, or both
search.text: A target asks for a rupee amount, a number of bills, or both — it must ask for at least one. A bulk change of rupees leaves each account's stored bill target alone.

search.heading: Who sees which rows
search.text: Person Sees Telecaller or accounts user Exactly the accounts they hold a seat on — sales, back office, or sales manager Manager Their team's book, as on every other CRM list Admin The whole company Why the sales manager seat counts here, and nowhere else. The sales manager seat drives no queue, no scope and no target anywhere in the product — but a sales manager reviewing the month has no other way to find the accounts they are named on. So it widens visibility on this screen only. Accounts users, who see the whole book on the approval queue, see only their own seats here: "every account in the company" is not an answer to "which targets are mine to review". The filters (search, status, salesperson, sales manager, back office) narrow within that visibility and use the same clause the Customers list runs, so a filtered total and a filtered list cannot disagree.

search.heading: Who may set targets
search.text: Managers and accounts. Setting a customer target needs the target-setting permission, which managers and the accounts desk hold. The accounts desk is where targets are actually managed here, so Accounts has its own door onto this same screen at /accounts/customer-targets — not a second target system. It differs only in where a customer's name links: to the account statement, because Accounts has no CRM record page. The screen checks the permission itself rather than "is this person a manager", which used to be the same thing and stopped being so the day accounts were given it.

search.heading: Top customers
search.text: Ranked company-wide, then narrowed to your book. The top customers are chosen across every book first , each keeps its company rank, and only then does your scope decide which of them you are shown. "Top 60 of my own book" would put a telecaller's sixtieth-best shop on a list called Top customers. - Frozen for the month. Generated on the 1st at 10:00 IST for spans of 3, 6 and 12 whole months ending with the month just finished, and stored. A report somebody works from for a month must not move because a sheet reconcile edited an old order. - Idempotent. The 10:00 job, the hourly pass that catches a missed one, and the screen itself (if opened first) all call the same generator; a report is claimed once and cannot be written twice. - Sales and orders use the same "approved" definition as everything else; a pending or declined order never ranks anybody.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - The shortfall split is not on any screen. The engine that sorts short customers into a coverage gap (under-contacted — a telecaller problem) and a customer gap (contacted on schedule and still short — a market problem) exists and is tested, but nothing in this build calls it ( lib/engines/targets.ts classifyShortfall ). AGENTS.md names a shortfallAnalysis service that is not in the tree. - The refusal message for a lead is out of date. Setting a target on a lead says it "becomes a customer on its first order"; conversion happens on the second ( lib/services/worklist-services.ts setTarget ; lib/engines/lead-ladder.ts promotesToCustomerAt ). - Seeding reads every active row. The 1st-of-month seed loops over customers with status active, which includes leads and third-party shops, though the list hides them and the action refuses them ( lib/recompute.ts seedMonthlyTargets ).

The WhatsApp screen is shared by the CRM and the Accounts app: src/app/crm/whatsapp/page.tsx renders WhatsappPage with app="crm" . Messages are rows in wa messages , templates in wa templates , inbound in wa replies . Everything about preparing, copying, confirming and sending is in whatsapp-service.ts ; conversations are whatsapp-chat-service.ts ; the routing decision is the pure deliveryRoute in lib/whatsapp-delivery.ts ; Wati is the provider.

The WhatsApp screen is where customers' messages arrive and where payment reminders and other template messages go out. It opens on the chats , the way WhatsApp itself does. Sending a message, running a batch of reminders, editing templates and reading the message log are tools you open from the same screen. What you can do here depends on what you were given: read the chats, or reply and send as well.

search.heading: The screen at a glance
search.text: WhatsApp, with a chat open. Sent today. 14 Copied, never confirmed. 2 Replies to action. 5 Templates live. 9 Messages logged. 300 Chats. Customer A. Send New message Send run Templates Message log

search.heading: Two ways a message goes out
search.text: Automatic. Sent straight through WhatsApp's business service. You see ✓ when WhatsApp accepts it, ✓✓ when it reaches the phone, and Read when they open it. Manual: copy, send, confirm. You copy the message, paste it into WhatsApp yourself, and press Confirm once it has gone. WhatsApp gives no ticks for a pasted message, so your confirmation is the record. A message goes the manual way when sending is switched off, when no key is set up, when it is going to a customer group , when the template is not linked to an approved WhatsApp template yet, or when you edited the words. The screen tells you which.

search.heading: Sending a payment reminder or a template
search.text: Open New message. Pick the customer and the template. Templates are grouped by purpose: payment reminder, order confirmation, reactivation, routine check-in, other. Check the preview. The message is filled in from the customer's record — their name, what they owe, their open bills, the latest promise. If a field is empty the message is refused rather than sent as "Dear ,". You can edit the words; an edited message always goes the manual way. Send it. Automatic : press send; the ticks appear in the chat. Manual : press Copy , paste it into WhatsApp, send it there, then come back and press Confirm . Copied is not sent. Until you press Confirm , a copied message is Copied, not confirmed — the customer may or may not have heard from us. It does not hold the customer back from the Call Log, and it does not count as a reminder sent. A manager sees every unconfirmed copy in the top card.

search.heading: Customers reached two ways
search.text: A customer can be set up to receive messages on their own number , in their WhatsApp group , or both . - Both makes two messages — the personal one first, then the group one. Work them one at a time: each has its own copy and confirm. - Confirming either one counts as the customer having heard from us. The other is still shown as waiting until you confirm it too. - If both is set but nobody recorded the group's name, only the personal message is made, and the screen says why.

search.heading: Working a batch: Send run
search.text: Set up a send run. Choose who: Stage 1 reminder due , Slow payers with a balance or Overdue more than 60 days , and the template. Work down the list. For each customer: Copy the message , Send it from WhatsApp , Confirm and move on . Messages that can go automatically go in one press. Pause and come back. A run you leave is offered again the next time you open the screen.

search.heading: Replies
search.text: A customer's reply arrives in their chat. Replies to action counts the ones nobody has dealt with. Reply in the chat, or mark the reply handled. Photographs and documents the customer sends open in the chat.

search.heading: Message statuses
search.text: You see It means Prepared Written, not sent Copied, not confirmed Copied to paste, nobody confirmed it went Confirmed sent A person pasted it and confirmed Sending Handed to WhatsApp a moment ago Sent ✓ WhatsApp accepted it Delivered ✓✓ It reached their phone Read ✓✓ They opened it (only if they have read receipts on) Failed It did not go — the log says why Not sent Discarded before it went

search.heading: Questions people ask
search.text: I sent it from my phone but the customer is still on my Call Log.. You did not press Confirm . A copied message is not treated as sent until somebody confirms it. Why can I read the chats but not reply?. Your access is read-only. Replying and sending are given separately, on the Access screen. Why did my message go the manual way?. The screen names the reason: sending is switched off, no key is set up, it is going to a group, the template is not approved, or you edited it. It says this customer has already had several messages this week.. There is a weekly limit per customer on messages sent automatically, currently . Pasting by hand is your judgement and is not limited. A number is listed as undeliverable.. WhatsApp says that number cannot receive messages. Automatic rules stop trying it. Put a working number on the customer's record. Does a WhatsApp reminder stop the Call Log ringing them?. A confirmed message does, for a few days. A reminder falling due still brings them back.

WhatsApp is how most payment reminders reach customers and how most customers answer. The rules on this screen exist to keep one thing honest: whether a customer has actually heard from us . That decides whether the Call Log holds them back, whether collections counts a reminder as sent, and what a manager reads about the day.

search.heading: Read, and reply-and-send, are two grants
search.text: Reading the chats and writing to customers are separate. The screen is one module; reply and send is a second module beside it. Somebody given only the first can open every chat and the message log, and nothing else. The server checks the level on every write — a reply box that is not drawn is not a permission. Level Can Read Read chats and the message log Reply and send Reply in a chat, mark replies handled, send templates, work send runs, edit templates Sending a reminder from other screens — the payment follow-up panel, for example — is refused only for somebody deliberately narrowed to read . People who were never given the WhatsApp screen at all could always send a reminder from those screens, and still can.

search.heading: How a message is routed
search.text: Automatic or manual. Manual stays fully usable. Automatic sending is an addition, never a replacement. A deployment with sending switched off works entirely by copy, paste and confirm. A group cannot be reached through the API at all, and an edited message is no longer the approved wording WhatsApp allows a business to send. A message that would read badly is refused. Every merge field the template uses must have a value for this customer. "Dear ," never reaches a customer — the message is refused naming the empty field. Merge fields a template can use: customer, contact, city, phone, outstanding, last order date and value, the oldest bill's number and due date, every stated open bill as a list, today's date, the latest dated promise, and the owner. Outstanding and the bills list in a message include stated bills only. A balance nobody has stated is not something to compose a message about.

search.heading: Copied is not sent
search.text: Only a confirmed send counts. A manual message moves prepared → copied → confirmed sent . Only confirming it sets the customer's last confirmed WhatsApp date, which is what holds them back from the Call Log for days; only confirming a payment reminder records a collections attempt on the WhatsApp channel. Copying touches none of it. A copied-but-unconfirmed message is a customer who may or may not have been contacted. Treating it as sent would hold somebody back from a call on the strength of a message that never left the telecaller's clipboard; treating it as not sent would ring a customer who heard from us an hour ago. It is shown as exactly what it is.

search.heading: Copies nobody confirmed
search.text: Every hour, copies older than hours are counted for the manager. If is above zero, copies older than that are confirmed automatically; at zero nothing ever is, because asserting that a message was sent when the system cannot know is exactly the failure the confirm step exists to prevent.

search.heading: Automatic sends
search.text: Wati reports sent , delivered and read . Its updates are applied in order and only ever move forward, so a retried or late notification changes nothing. A message Wati accepts counts as sent for the Call Log and for collections, just as a confirmed paste does. A weekly limit on automatic messages. No customer receives more than messages a week through the API (zero means no limit). A person pasting by hand is exercising judgement; a button that sends is not.

search.heading: Customers reached two ways
search.text: Both is an instruction about a customer, never a message. A message goes to exactly one place. A customer set to both produces two messages — personal first, because it can complete without a person, then the group. Each has its own state; one idempotency key covers the pair, so a retried click cannot double-send either half. - One confirmed leg does set the last-WhatsApp date — waiting for the second would chase somebody who has already heard from us. - Neither leg may borrow the other's confirmation: the group can be confirmed while the personal one is still copied, and both are shown that way. - Both with no group recorded makes only the personal message.

search.heading: Payment reminders and collections
search.text: A payment reminder is a template whose purpose is payment reminder , with a stage it belongs to. When one is confirmed sent (or accepted by Wati) for a customer on the collections worklist, a WhatsApp attempt is written, keyed on the message, and the collections cadence dates the next reminder from it. See Payment Follow-up. No path that sent a reminder used to write that attempt, so a stage 1 customer came back due a message every single day.

search.heading: Replies
search.text: Inbound messages arrive from Wati and are matched to a customer by the last ten digits of the number. A reply is to action until somebody replies or marks it handled. A number that WhatsApp says cannot receive messages is listed as undeliverable, and automatic rules stop trying it rather than reporting "sending failing".

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - "WhatsApp mode" changes nothing. The setting is on the Settings screen, but whether a message goes automatically is decided by the founder's switch and whether a key exists — the setting is never read. - Copy, confirm and cancel do not check the message is in your book. They act on whatever message id they are given, for anybody who is not narrowed to read-only. - Automatic confirmation of old copies would fail if switched on. The hourly job calls the same confirm step a person uses, and that step requires a signed-in user to record who confirmed — a scheduled job has none. - The weekly limit is counted over the last seven days in the database's own clock , not the business week.

MahekOne is one Next.js 16 application (App Router, React 19, Server Components and Server Actions) over one Postgres database reached through Drizzle ORM , plus a separate Expo project in mbos-app/ for the field salesman's Android handset. Every app — the CRM, Accounts, the Sales Dashboard, HRMS, the ERP, the Admin Console, these docs — is a route tree in the same application, reading the same tables. Nothing is split into services, and nothing is synced between apps, because there is nothing to sync. This page is the map a developer needs before changing anything: where each kind of code lives, how a request travels from the browser to the database, how sign-in and access control work, how the handset talks to the server, and the rules that keep the data honest. The owner's tab explains the same shape in plain words; Local setup gets a laptop running.

search.heading: The stack
search.text: Piece What Where it is configured Framework Next.js 16, App Router, React 19 with the React Compiler lint rules on next.config.ts , eslint.config.mjs Rendering Server Components by default; client components only where there is state or an event handler per file ( "use client" ) Writes Server Actions in src/lib/actions/ , plus route handlers in src/app/api/ for anything a browser action cannot carry (audio, uploads over 1 MB, cron, the handset) — Database Postgres 17 in a container beside the app in production; 16 locally and in CI deploy/docker-compose.yml , docker-compose.yml ORM Drizzle, driver postgres (postgres-js) src/db/schema.ts , src/db/index.ts , drizzle.config.ts Migrations Hand-written SQL in drizzle/ , applied by drizzle-kit migrate (never generated here — see Local setup) drizzle/meta/ journal.json Styling Tailwind v4; every colour, radius and type size is a design token under @theme src/app/globals.css Handset Expo (SDK 54) + React Native, its own SQLite, its own package.json mbos-app/ Hosting One DigitalOcean droplet: Caddy → the app container → Postgres Deploying This is not the Next.js in your training data. Next.js 16 renamed and moved several conventions — the request interceptor is src/proxy.ts (exporting proxy ), not middleware.ts . AGENTS.md tells every contributor to read node modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing framework code, and that applies here too.

search.heading: Layering
search.text: The rule that holds the codebase together is that each layer only reaches down. Layer Lives in May do May not do Route / layout src/app/ /layout.tsx , page.tsx Read the user, gate on apps and modules, call services and queries, render Contain business rules Client screen -screen.tsx , components Hold UI state, call server actions Import server-only modules Action src/lib/actions/ .ts Check capability and scope, validate, write in one transaction, audit, call recomputes Be trusted because a button was hidden Service src/lib/services/ .ts Fetch data, call engines, compose results Hold rules an engine should own Engine src/lib/engines/ .ts Pure functions: inputs, config and the business date in, a value out Any I/O, any clock read, any getConfig() Cache rebuild src/lib/recompute.ts Rebuild buying cycles, outstanding, follow-up stages, slow-payer flags Be bypassed by a hand-edit of a cached column Data src/db/schema.ts Declare tables, enums, indexes Hold operator-class indexes (those are in the SQL migrations) Reads in queries.ts, writes in lib/actions. A figure on a dashboard and the same figure on its own screen come from the same function , so the two cannot drift. Every write is a server action (or a route handler where an action cannot carry the body) that checks permission on the server, whatever the screen drew. Engines are pure. src/lib/engines/ performs no I/O. That is what lets npm run test pin every business rule without a database, and what lets the handset compile some of the same engines ( npm run mbos:sync-engines mirrors them into mbos-app/ ).

search.heading: A request, end to end
search.text: A browser opening a CRM screen.

search.heading: The proxy names the app
search.text: src/proxy.ts runs on every request. It does not authenticate — it names which app the request is in, from the URL prefix, and writes it into the x-mahek-app header after deleting any value the client sent. Shared API routes ( /api/search and friends) have no app in their path, so appForApi takes it from a same-host Referer . That is safe because naming an app grants nothing: requestHat still requires a real grant in that app.

search.heading: The layout gates the app and the module
search.text: Each app's layout.tsx calls listUserApps() and redirects anybody without the grant; each module folder's layout calls requireModule . API routes that serve a module use canOpenModule , which asks both halves in one call. The launcher, every app switcher and the "straight into it" redirect read one function, so a mobile-only app (the handset's field ) can never become a browser tile in one place and not another:

search.heading: Sign-in and sessions
search.text: Concern How Where Identifier Work number, email, or the HRMS personal mobile (asked last, only via the explicit employee link, and only if it names exactly one account) findAccount in src/lib/services/otp-service.ts Password scrypt hash on users.password hash ; throttled per account and per address src/lib/auth.ts , auth.password. settings One-time code Sent through MiniMoth (WhatsApp, then SMS) when its key is held; otherwise a Wati authentication template if one is named otpAvailability — see Integrations Session A row in sessions , id in the mahekone session cookie, 30 days ("remember me") or browser-session createSession , getCurrentUser in src/lib/auth.ts Password reset Emailed single-use link (SHA-256 of the token stored, 30 minutes) or a code to the phone; spending it deletes every session src/lib/password-reset.ts , resetPasswordWithOtp Disabled account getCurrentUser refuses an inactive user; disabling also deletes their sessions; grants are kept src/lib/auth.ts , the Access screen Handset Its own bearer tokens (JWT signed with MBOS JWT SECRET ), bound to one device src/lib/mbos/token.ts , src/app/api/mbos/auth/ A sign-in also writes one row per person per day to attendance — a sign-in log , not attendance.

search.heading: Access control
search.text: Three layers, each narrower than the last: the app , the module inside it , and the level (associate, manager, admin) the grant carries.

search.heading: Capabilities: what a person may DO
search.text: A hat is an app plus a level. can answers whether one hat carries a capability; canFor takes the union over every hat a person wears, and requireCapability (117 call sites) does the same and returns the narrowest granting hat for the audit log. - Admin of the Admin Console is the platform administrator and holds everything. - Admin of any other app holds that app's manager list only; what else an app gives its own admins is that app's own access file. - The ledger capabilities ( order.approve , payment.confirm , creditnote.issue , customer.reassign ) live on the Accounts app, so a CRM manager cannot approve an order.

search.heading: Scope: what a person may SEE
search.text: resolveScope() (cached per request) reads the user, the app from x-mahek-app , and that app's grant, and returns mine , team or all . Lists narrow with scopedToUsers(ids) , which reads every seat a person can hold on a customer. Whose book an account is — who is credited and whose queue it lands on — is one expression: Resolving scope per app can only narrow : the account's own users.role is the widest level held anywhere, and a per-app hat is by construction no wider. The proxy strips any client-sent x-mahek-app , so a request cannot name its own app.

search.heading: The MBOS handset
search.text: mbos-app/ is an offline-first Expo app with its own SQLite schema ( mbos-app/src/db/schema.ts ). It never reads Postgres directly; it talks to src/app/api/mbos/ with a bearer token. How a handset stays in step. Concept What to know Where Bootstrap vs delta The delta must send exactly what the bootstrap sends; channels converge on one function each buildBootstrap , buildPull in src/lib/services/mbos-service.ts Outbox Everything the salesman authors is queued locally and pushed; each item carries an idempotency key mbos-app/src/sync/ , dispatchItem in src/lib/actions/mbos.ts Wire contract A column the handset's SQLite does not have would roll back the whole pull; the handset drops unknown columns and mbos-wire.test.ts pins both sides src/lib/mbos-wire.test.ts Tombstones A pull says what exists; only mbos deletions says what stopped existing mbos deletions Territory Narrows a salesman's book; no territory means no book (managers excepted) territoryClause Media Uploaded after its parent, bound when the parent is written Storage Releases APK by workflow; JavaScript over the air Handset release

search.heading: Scheduled work
search.text: There is no in-process scheduler. The droplet's cron calls /api/sheets/sync?mode=… with CRON SECRET , and that route runs a named job from src/lib/jobs.ts . Every job writes a job runs row, is idempotent, and can be run by hand with npm run jobs -- . The cadence and catalogue are on Sheets and jobs.

search.heading: Configuration
search.text: Every business threshold is a setting in src/lib/config/registry.ts , stored in app settings and read through getConfig() , which caches for 30 seconds: Credentials are separate ( app secrets , readSecret ). See Configuration.

search.heading: Time zone rules
search.text: Rule Why Guard Never cast a stored timestamp to a date without naming the zone ( at time zone 'Asia/Kolkata' ) The session zone decides a bare ::date ; a 1 am IST row lands on the previous day under GMT A test forces GMT; a grep test fails on bare casts in lib/ Never turn a stored DATE into an instant without naming midnight ( ::timestamp at time zone … ) A pooled connection's zone leaks into the result A third grep test Never toISOString().slice(0, 10) or getHours() on the server Both answer in UTC/the machine zone; use calendarDate() , stamp , clock Grep tests over src/ Bind dates as ISO strings and type integer parameters ( ::int ) postgres serialising a JS Date throws on Node 25; date - $n resolves as date - date date-arithmetic-bind.test.ts The zone is spelled once APP TIMEZONE in src/lib/business-date.ts for SQL and client code; for anything that reads config —

search.heading: Adding the next MahekOne app
search.text: Tables in the same schema. Add them to src/db/schema.ts and hand-write the migration. Reference customers and users directly — never copy them. Register the app. Add its id to app id (a rename uses ALTER TYPE … RENAME VALUE ; a new value cannot be used in the migration that adds it), its entry in APPS in src/lib/apps.ts , its URL prefix in APP ROUTES in src/proxy.ts , its modules in src/lib/modules.ts and its row in the capability matrix. Gate its layout. Call listUserApps() in src/app/ /layout.tsx the way src/app/crm/layout.tsx does, and requireModule in each module folder. Give the launcher something to say. A count and status line in launcherApps() , where the badge counts what the sentence describes. Reads and writes in their places. Reads in lib/queries.ts or a service; writes in lib/actions/ .ts , each checking a capability. Grant it from a terminal or the Access screen. npm run app:grant -- example@mahek.in , or Admin Console → Access.
