MahekOne talks to a small number of outside services: Wati for WhatsApp, MiniMoth for sign-in codes, Ola Maps for maps, Resend for email, Sarvam and OpenAI for dictation and the AI assistants, a Google service account for reading the team's spreadsheets, and Expo for push notifications to the field app. This page explains what each one is for, where its key is kept, and — most importantly — what MahekOne does when one is missing or down. The principle behind every one of them is the same: A feature that cannot work says so, rather than failing when used. Without its key, a feature is not drawn, or it says plainly that it is not set up. A microphone that fails when pressed, a map that draws a grey rectangle, or a "code sent" message for a code that never left are all worse than the feature simply not being offered. And no outside service being down ever stops somebody signing in with a password or saving their work.

search.heading: At a glance
search.text: Service What it does for MahekOne Key kept in If the key is missing If the service is down Wati (WhatsApp) Sends approved templates from the business number; brings back replies and delivery ticks Admin Console → Integrations Nothing is sent through WhatsApp's API; copy-and-confirm by hand still works Sends fail with "Wati could not be reached"; replies arrive late MiniMoth Sends one-time sign-in codes by WhatsApp, then SMS Admin Console → Integrations Codes fall back to a Wati template if one is set up, otherwise only passwords are offered The code option fails; passwords still work Ola Maps Street maps on the Live and Territory screens and the handset, snapping trails to roads, finding coordinates for addresses Admin Console → Platform → Maps (up to five keys) Each map screen says there is no key; lists beside it still work The trail stays as recorded; spare keys take over when one runs out Resend Password-reset email Server environment Mail is written to the server log, and the screen says so The reset screen says the mail could not be sent Sarvam Hears Indian languages for dictation; also writes notes Admin Console → Integrations (Voice) OpenAI does the hearing instead OpenAI is tried next OpenAI Dictation, tidying notes, reading price lists and documents, the Hire and ERP assistants Admin Console → Integrations (Voice) Sarvam handles short dictation; the AI assistants are not offered The other provider is tried for writing; assistants report they are unavailable Google Reads the order, party, employee and field-activity workbooks, read-only Server environment The sheet sync reports "not configured" That sync run fails and the next one tries again Expo push Lock-screen notifications on the field app Settings (Expo project id) and the APK's Firebase file Notifications still land on the in-app bell Same — the bell always has them

search.heading: WhatsApp, through Wati
search.text: Wati is Mahek's WhatsApp Business provider. MahekOne uses it two ways: - Sending. Templates approved in Wati — payment reminders, order follow-ups — sent from the business number. Sending is switched on and off by the founder on the Founder Command Centre's WhatsApp desk, read on every send, so "I switched it off" means the next message does not go. Holding the key switches nothing on by itself. - Receiving. Wati reports each message's delivery and every customer reply back to MahekOne, so replies show in the CRM's WhatsApp screens and a delivered message is marked delivered. Copied is not sent. A telecaller can still copy a message and send it from their own WhatsApp. That counts as sent only when they confirm it — a copied-but-unconfirmed message is a customer who may or may not have been contacted, and is shown as exactly that. The address Wati reports to is worked out from the key itself, so it changes when the key changes. Nobody has to set it up separately, and an old key's address stops working when the key is rotated.

search.heading: Sign-in codes, through MiniMoth
search.text: When MiniMoth's key is held, the sign-in screen offers a one-time code to the person's phone: WhatsApp first, SMS when WhatsApp does not deliver. MiniMoth creates and checks the code itself — MahekOne never sees the digits, it only records that a code was sent. - The code goes to the personal mobile HR holds for the person. An account not linked to an employee gets no code. - A test key sends nothing and accepts 000000 for any number. It is refused on the live system, because there it would let anybody who knows a colleague's number sign in as them. - If MiniMoth is not set up, a WhatsApp authentication template in Wati can carry the code instead, if one is named in and approved in Wati. Whatever happens to codes, the password form always works. The sign-in page checks code availability without ever being able to fail because of it.

search.heading: Maps, through Ola Maps
search.text: Ola Maps draws the streets under the Sales Dashboard's Live and Territory maps and the handset's map, snaps a salesman's GPS trail onto the roads he walked, and turns addresses into coordinates. - Up to five keys , from separate Ola accounts, are spent in order. When Ola refuses one for running out of quota, MahekOne moves to the next and remembers the refusal for hours, so a restart does not go back to a spent key. - A map key has to reach the browser and the phone , because they are what ask Ola for map tiles. That makes it the one credential that is not kept on the server. Restrict the browser key to MahekOne's own domain in Ola's console, and give the handset a separate key with a spending cap, so a key copied out of the app can be revoked without taking the office's maps down. - Pins and trails come from MahekOne's own data ; Ola is only ever asked for squares of map, never for where anybody is.

search.heading: Email, through Resend
search.text: Only password-reset links are emailed today. Without Resend set up, the mail is written to the server log instead, and the reset screen says so rather than claiming it was sent. A forgotten password can also be reset with a code to the phone.

search.heading: Dictation and AI, through Sarvam and OpenAI
search.text: Every prose box in the CRM and the field app carries a microphone when dictation is on ( ): 1. Hearing — Sarvam first, because it is built for Indian languages and Hindi with English mixed in; it refuses recordings over 30 seconds, so longer ones (and anything Sarvam fails on) go to OpenAI. Either key alone is enough. 2. Writing — what was heard is turned into faithful English (nothing dropped) by OpenAI, or Sarvam if OpenAI is not available. 3. Tighten and Rewrite are offered only when one of the two can do the writing. The recording is never stored — it is sent, transcribed and dropped. (The one exception is a visit note on the handset, where the recording is kept with the visit as the record of what the customer said.) The OpenAI key is also used by the assistants that read documents: price-list extraction, the lead business-card scan, the Hire evaluator and the ERP's assistants. Without it, those are not offered.

search.heading: The spreadsheets, through Google
search.text: A Google service account — an identity, not a person — is given view access to each workbook. MahekOne asks Google only for read permission, so nothing MahekOne does can change a cell. See Sheets and jobs.

search.heading: Push notifications, through Expo
search.text: The field app can receive lock-screen notifications once Firebase is built into the app and Expo is allowed to deliver through it — see Handset release. Until then, and whenever a push fails, the notification is still on the in-app bell. During a push is delivered silently rather than held.

search.heading: The public website
search.text: The website's own server forwards each enquiry to MahekOne with a shared secret (kept in Admin Console → Integrations). An enquiry without it is refused, so nobody else can post enquiries into MahekOne.

search.heading: Who can set keys
search.text: Only platform administrators can set or clear a key, on Admin Console → Integrations (and its Voice and Maps sections). A key is shown only by its last four characters; the audit log records that a key changed, never what to. See Configuration.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - An SMS provider key can be set that nothing uses. The Integrations list includes a MSG91 key, but sign-in codes go through MiniMoth (or a Wati template); no code reads the MSG91 key ( src/lib/secrets.ts ). - Email has no console key. Every other outside service can be connected from a screen; Resend still needs its key and sender address in the server's environment file ( src/lib/mailer.ts ). - The Google service account cannot be set from a screen either — it is environment-only ( src/lib/sheets.ts ).

MahekOne is one Next.js 16 application talking to one Postgres database, plus a separate Expo project for the field salesman's handset in mbos-app/ . Getting a laptop from a fresh clone to a running app takes four commands, and only one environment variable is required — DATABASE URL . Everything else (Google Sheets, WhatsApp, dictation, mail, file storage) is optional locally and switches itself off, saying so on the screen, when its variables are missing. This page is the whole path: what to install, what npm run db:setup actually does, how migrations are written in this repository (by hand — never generated), the test suites, the handset, and the failures that look like success.

search.heading: What you need installed
search.text: Tool Version Where the version comes from Node.js 24 Not pinned in package.json ( engines is absent) and there is no .nvmrc . 24 is what production runs: the Dockerfile builds and runs on node:24-alpine , and ci.yml and deploy.yml both use node-version: 24 . npm ships with Node package-lock.json is committed; CI runs npm ci . Postgres 16 locally (17 works) The root docker-compose.yml runs postgres:16 , CI's service container is postgres:16 , and setup-db.mjs looks for Homebrew's postgresql@17 , @16 , @15 or @14 . Production is postgres:17-alpine ( deploy/docker-compose.yml ). Docker optional Only if you would rather run Postgres in a container than install it. Java 17 + Android SDK only for a local APK The handset. Most handset work needs neither — see The handset. There is no shared development database and no cloud credential needed to develop. Every developer runs their own Postgres; CI gets its own throwaway one the same way.

search.heading: First run
search.text: From a fresh clone to a running app. Install dependencies. Start Postgres. Either natively ( brew install postgresql@16 && brew services start postgresql@16 on macOS) or with the compose file in the repository root, which is a bare Postgres for development and nothing else: The container is mahek-db , on port 5432, with the role, password and database name that .env.example 's DATABASE URL already expects — so .env.local does not change between the two. Two compose files. docker-compose.yml in the root is the development database. deploy/docker-compose.yml is the production stack (Caddy, the app, Postgres 17) and is copied to the droplet. Never run the second one locally — it needs a production .env and would try to obtain a TLS certificate. Run the setup script. What it does is described exactly in the next section. It is safe to run again. Start the app. Open http://localhost:3000 and sign in with a seeded account (see Seed data).

search.heading: What npm run db:setup does
search.text: db:setup is node scripts/setup-db.mjs . It has five numbered stages and prints each as it goes: Stage What happens When it stops 1. Environment Copies .env.example to .env.local if .env.local does not exist; otherwise leaves it alone. Reads DATABASE URL out of it. No DATABASE URL → stops with "No DATABASE URL in .env.local". A URL that is not localhost / 127.0.0.1 → warns that seeding a shared database would wipe it, and exits without touching anything. 2. Postgres Finds psql on PATH , or under Homebrew's /opt/homebrew or /usr/local for postgresql@17 down to @14 . Runs select 1 against the postgres database. Not installed → prints the brew / apt or docker run command for your platform. Installed but not listening on 5432 → prints how to start it. 3. Role and database Creates the mahek role (login, createdb ) and the mahekone database owned by it, each only if missing. No permission → suggests running the create role as a superuser. 4. Schema npx drizzle-kit migrate — every migration in drizzle/ . Whatever drizzle-kit does (see Troubleshooting: it can exit having applied nothing). 5. Demo data npm run db:seed . — It ends with "Ready. Start the app with: npm run dev". Re-running it reseeds. Stage 5 runs every time, and the seed wipes and reseeds the book (it also clears sessions). If you only want to catch up on migrations, run npm run db:migrate instead.

search.heading: Environment variables
search.text: Locally everything lives in .env.local , which is never committed. Next.js loads it itself; scripts outside Next (drizzle-kit, the seed, the job runner) either pass --env-file=.env.local to tsx / node in package.json , or call loadEnv() , which only fills variables not already set:

search.heading: Required
search.text: Variable Why DATABASE URL src/db/index.ts throws at import time without it — "DATABASE URL is not set. Copy .env.example to .env.local for development". That is deliberate, and it is why the Docker build has to set a deliberately unresolvable placeholder (see Deploying).

search.heading: Migrations
search.text: The schema is declared in src/db/schema.ts (Drizzle ORM) and changed by SQL files in drizzle/ , listed in order in drizzle/meta/ journal.json . drizzle.config.ts points drizzle-kit at both. Command What it runs Use it for npm run db:migrate drizzle-kit migrate Catching your local database up npm run db:deploy node scripts/migrate-deploy.mjs The deploy (and CI's stack job). Same migrator, but it prints the real Postgres error and counts what was applied npm run deploy:db db:deploy && catalogue:deploy && hire:deploy What deploy.yml runs over the SSH tunnel: migrations, the idempotent catalogue import, and Hire's install step npm run db:generate drizzle-kit generate Do not use — see below

search.heading: Write migrations by hand
search.text: Never run drizzle-kit generate in this repository. drizzle/meta/ holds snapshots for only a few dozen of the more than two hundred migrations, so generate diffs against a schema hundreds of migrations out of date and emits a "new" migration that re-creates tables that already exist. It also stamps when from the wall clock, which can land below the hand-written values. Write the .sql file yourself, append the journal entry yourself, and never commit a generated meta/NNNN snapshot.json . The house style is a prose comment at the top saying what the migration is for and any trap it avoids. The most recent one is a good model: Statements within one file are separated by -- statement-breakpoint .

search.heading: The journal and when
search.text: Each journal entry has an idx , a tag (the file name without .sql ) and a when . drizzle decides what is pending by comparing each entry's when with the newest created at in drizzle. drizzle migrations — it does not check that every entry was applied. Three things follow: - A new entry's when must be above every existing one . Take the last entry's value and add a small step; recent entries step by 1000. - A migration written on a branch while main moved on may carry a when below main 's newest. Once both land, it is skipped for ever and the run still reports success. When journal.json conflicts in a merge, main 's entries are authoritative: renumber your files above main 's highest index and make the when sequence strictly increasing across the whole file. - File numbers and idx can diverge (there are gaps in the NNNN prefixes). The journal, not the file name, is the order. migrate-deploy.mjs exists to make these visible. It counts drizzle. drizzle migrations before and after, prints "N applied, now X of Y in the journal", and emits a ::warning:: naming the watermark trap when fewer rows exist than journal entries. On failure it prints the driver error's code , detail , table, column and constraint (drizzle-kit's own CLI prints nothing), and for an "already exists" error it queries what is actually there:

search.heading: Enum values: add in one, use in a later commit
search.text: A value added to an existing enum cannot be used in the same run. drizzle-kit migrate applies every pending migration in one transaction , and Postgres refuses to use a value added by ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE until that transaction commits. So no later migration in the same batch may reference it either — not in an INSERT , a CHECK , or an index predicate. It passes on every developer's database (which already committed the value long ago) and fails only from scratch: CI and a fresh clone. - Compare as text instead: o.status::text in ('captured', …) needs no enum member. - Grants of a new app id go through npm run app:grant , never a migration. - Renaming an app slug is ALTER TYPE app id RENAME VALUE , never add-and-migrate. - A brand-new type created with CREATE TYPE … AS ENUM and used in the same file is fine — the restriction is only on values added to an already committed enum.

search.heading: Every migration must be additive
search.text: The deploy migrates before the new image starts, while the old code is still serving (see Deploying). New columns, new tables and backfills that match on updated by id is null are safe. Dropping or renaming a column the running code reads needs two releases: one that stops reading it, then one that removes it.

search.heading: Checking a migration before you push
search.text: 1. Apply it to a database built from nothing — npm run test:db rebuilds mahekone test from every migration, which is exactly the from-scratch case. (It drops and recreates mahekone test ; if somebody else is running integration tests against the same Postgres, use a throwaway database instead.) 2. Query information schema.columns for a column your migration adds. "Applied successfully" is not evidence. 3. CI's ci job runs db:migrate against an empty database, and the stack job runs deploy:db the way the deploy does.

search.heading: Seed data
search.text: The seed wipes and reseeds a deterministic demo book (a fixed pseudo-random seed, so a reseed produces the same customers), imports the product catalogue, creates the demo accounts with their app grants, and then runs the engines over the seeded book so the derived caches are filled. It also clears every session, so you will be signed out. Every seeded account has the same password, given in AGENTS.md , and signs in with its email or its work number. The full list is in AGENTS.md under Seeded accounts . By role: Seeded account App and level Lands on Four telecaller accounts CRM, associate Straight into the CRM A CRM associate with Reports CRM and Reports, associate The launcher The manager account CRM manager, Accounts, HRMS admin, Admin Console, Founder The launcher The field salesman account field (the handset) only /apps , which says there is nothing for him in a browser The ledger-desk account Accounts, manager Straight into order approvals npm run demo:clear removes the demo data again.

search.heading: Granting apps the seed does not give
search.text: New apps (Documentation, ERP, Hire and others added after the seed was written) are not granted by it. Grant one by hand: scripts/grant-app.ts takes an app id and an email or work number, always writes a level (associate unless --level says otherwise), re-derives the account's own level from all its grants, and is idempotent. admin granted at --level=admin is what makes a platform administrator. Related helpers: npm run user:password , npm run user:role .

search.heading: Running it
search.text: Command What npm run dev next dev on port 3000 npm run build prebuild runs docs:index first, then next build , which type-checks the whole codebase npm start Serves the built app npm run jobs -- Any scheduled job by hand, against .env.local ( npm run jobs -- nightly ) npm run check:links Crawls a running app as a seeded user (it mints a session row directly) and fails on any broken internal link. Needs db:seed first npm run docs:index Rebuilds src/docs/ generated/index.json — see below

search.heading: The documentation index
search.text: The docs pages quote code with , and production runs Next's standalone server with no source tree beside it. So scripts/docs-index.mjs cuts every quoted excerpt out of the source at build time, highlights it, and writes it with the page headings and search text to src/docs/ generated/index.json . It exits non-zero naming any whose file or symbol does not exist. A symbol must be a top-level function , const , let , type , interface , class or enum declaration. Because prebuild runs it, a page quoting a renamed function fails npm run build , not a reader.

search.heading: Lint and the React Compiler rules
search.text: eslint.config.mjs is eslint-config-next (core web vitals + TypeScript), which brings eslint-plugin-react-hooks v7 and its React Compiler rules. mbos-app/ is ignored by the root config — the handset lints itself ( cd mbos-app && npm run lint ), and CI runs both. Two rules the compiler lint enforces, and the house pattern for each: - Do not reset state in an effect when a prop changes. Give the component a key and let it remount. Every modal and drawer does this ( ConfirmDialog , CallPanel ). - Do not read the clock during render. Date.now() and new Date() are impure. Read it in a server component and pass the value down: These are lint rules. The compiler itself is not switched on in next.config.ts (there is no reactCompiler key and babel-plugin-react-compiler is not installed), so the rules keep components compiler-safe without the build depending on it.

search.heading: The test suites
search.text: Command Database What it runs npm run test none The pure suite: every src/lib/engines/ .test.ts plus a long, explicit list of other pure tests in package.json (it is not a glob — a new pure test file must be added there) npm run test:db creates mahekone test scripts/make-test-db.mjs : drops and recreates mahekone test next to your dev database, then drizzle-kit migrate into it. Run it first, and again after any schema change npm run test:integration mahekone test scripts/run-integration.mjs : the §11 journeys and every other integration suite, one file per process, one after another npm run test:accounts mahekone test src/lib/accounts.test.ts alone npm run test:owner mahekone test src/lib/owner-dashboard.test.ts alone npm run test:performance mahekone test The salesman targets and score npm run test:outstanding mahekone test The outstanding-by-customer screen npm run test:all both test then test:integration cd mbos-app && npm test none The handset's engines, sync ordering and local store

search.heading: How the integration runner finds its database
search.text: Every runner reads DATABASE URL from .env.local and replaces the database name with mahekone test , sets NODE ENV=test , and runs tsx --conditions=react-server --test . So your development database is never touched. Individual suites also assert the URL matches mahekone test in their before hook ("Integration tests must run against mahekone test. Run npm run test:db first."), and each suite truncates the tables it uses itself. Files run sequentially because they share one database and truncate the same tables: run in parallel they produced unique-key violations and a different failure count on every run. The runner keeps going after a failure and prints "N of M integration suites failed". src/lib/mbos-columns.test.ts runs first — a schema column that no migration created breaks every other suite with "column does not exist", and that one test says which table.

search.heading: Signing in inside a test
search.text: Integration tests do not go through /login . lib/auth.ts carries a seam that exists only under NODE ENV=test : getCurrentUser() returns that user when NODE ENV === "test" . Everything downstream — scope, capabilities, the audit log — is the real code. Close the pool. Each integration suite must end with after(() = db.$client.end()) . A suite that leaves the Postgres pool open never exits, and in CI that shows as a check running for an hour.

search.heading: The handset (mbos-app)
search.text: mbos-app/ is a separate npm package — its own package.json and lockfile, not a workspace of the root. It is React Native on Expo SDK 57 ( expo ~57.0.26 , React Native 0.86, expo-router ), with SQLite as its local store.

search.heading: Pointing it at your laptop
search.text: The API base is read in src/sync/api.ts and inlined at bundle time : So set EXPO PUBLIC API BASE when you start Metro, to an address the phone can reach (your LAN IP, not localhost , on a real device): The web app must also have MBOS JWT SECRET set, and the account you sign in with needs the field app (the seeded field salesman has it).

search.heading: Expo Go or a development build
search.text: The app uses native code Expo Go does not carry — MapLibre for the map and offline packs, push notifications, and three local modules in mbos-app/modules/ ( location-service , pdf-preview , phone-setup ). For quick screen work, Metro can swap the two that throw on import for stand-ins in mbos-app/dev/ : With EXPO GO=1 , metro.config.js resolves @maplibre/maplibre-react-native to dev/maplibre-expo-go.tsx (the map says it needs the full app) and expo-notifications to dev/notifications-expo-go.ts . Without the variable — every real build — resolution is Expo's default. Anything touching background location, maps or push needs a development build: npm run android ( expo run:android ), which needs Java 17 and the Android SDK.

search.heading: Engines shared with the server
search.text: Two engines run in both places — expense-policy.ts and travel-distance.ts — and the handset's copies under mbos-app/src/engines/generated/ are generated: A shared-engines.test.ts in each project fails if the copy is stale. Never edit the generated files. Building and releasing an APK is covered in Releasing the MBOS handset app. A local gradlew assembleRelease is only for trying a change on your own phone.

search.heading: tsc is quiet, exits 0, and checks nothing
search.text: tsconfig.json includes .next/dev/types/ / .ts . When that generated file is stale it can contain a syntax error; tsc then reports only those parse errors, exits 0, and never checks src/ . If npx tsc --noEmit looks suspiciously clean, or its only output names .next/dev/types/routes.d.ts : Plant a deliberate type error in a src/ file now and then to prove it is really checking.

search.heading: db:migrate says "applying migrations…" and applies nothing
search.text: Two different causes look identical: 1. The watermark. A row in drizzle. drizzle migrations carries a created at above some journal entries (often from a branch you once ran). Every entry below it is skipped, silently, for ever. 2. An enum value used in the same batch. drizzle-kit exits 1 with no error text. Run npm run db:deploy instead — it prints the real Postgres error. Either way, compare what is applied with the journal: against the number of entries and the when values in drizzle/meta/ journal.json . To catch up without wiping your data, apply each missing drizzle/ .sql yourself — split on -- statement-breakpoint , run the statements in one transaction — then insert its sha256 hash with the journal's when as created at into drizzle. drizzle migrations . Or, if the data does not matter, npm run db:setup against a freshly dropped database. Before blaming main , build a database from main alone.

search.heading: Every page returns 200 but is broken
search.text: A database missing recent migrations does not fail visibly. Next renders the error boundary inside the shell and still answers 200 with a full-size body, so a curl -w "%{http code}" smoke test over every route is all green while every page is broken. Check the migration count first, then assert on content (a string only the real screen renders) and grep the dev-server log for PostgresError .

search.heading: TurbopackInternalError: Symlink … nodemodules is invalid
search.text: Building a copy of the repository outside the working tree with a symlinked node modules fails: Turbopack refuses a symlink pointing out of the project root. Hard-link the tree instead:

search.heading: Other traps worth knowing
search.text: Symptom Cause Integration failures vary between runs Two sessions sharing one mahekone test , or test:db run while another session's tests are running. Use your own copy of the database. "Cannot find module 'server-only'" across many suites node modules was deleted or reinstalled mid-run. Infrastructure, not your change. A timeout … tsc pipeline reports nothing on macOS macOS has no timeout binary, so nothing ran. Print exit codes. A raw db.execute returns a string where the type says Date Raw SQL returns timestamps as strings; use asDate() . A sql template with prose comments fails strangely A backtick inside a sql … literal ends it. sql-backticks.test.ts guards this.

Scheduled work in MahekOne has no in-process scheduler. The droplet's crontab runs deploy/sheet-sync.sh , which calls one HTTP endpoint , GET /api/sheets/sync?mode=… , with a bearer CRON SECRET . The route maps the mode to a job name and runs it through runJob in src/lib/jobs.ts . Every job writes a job runs row; every sheet read additionally writes a sheet sync runs row and is guarded so only one run per source is in flight. The same jobs run from the Admin Console and from npm run jobs -- .

search.heading: The endpoint
search.text: Response Meaning 503 CRON SECRET is not set — the endpoint is closed 401 Wrong or missing bearer token 400 Unknown mode ; the body lists the valid ones 200 { ok: true, job, recordsAffected, detail } — for multi-step jobs, the first step's result 409 SyncAlreadyRunningError — another run of that source started less than ten minutes ago. Not a failure; callers log and move on 500 The job threw; error is the message maxDuration is 300 seconds; callers use curl --max-time 310 . Query options pass through to runJob : owner (who projected rows are created as — required by project ), bills=1 (project bills from the Payment Status tab instead of Order Details), leads=1 , reassign=1 .

search.heading: One cycle
search.text: sheet-sync.sh cycle (every :07 and :37 UTC). The order matters: the read modes land rows in staging and project publishes what has landed. One caller doing them in sequence guarantees that; five independent schedulers could not.

search.heading: runSync: one run per source
search.text: A hash over the row's cells, sorted by column name , so inserting a column in the middle of a sheet does not rewrite thirty thousand hashes. An unchanged hash is not written, which is why a quiet tab costs a read and nothing else. Mode Reads Notices append From the watermark (highest row seen) onward New rows reconcile The whole tab Edits to old rows; rows gone from the sheet are withdrawn by difference, not by stamping reparse Nothing from Google — re-reads what is stored A change in the parsing rule ; run it whenever the reading of a row changes rather than the row

search.heading: Decisions the sheet does not override
search.text: - orders.status is kept wherever approved at is set (accounts approved or declined it). - The four manager seats on a customer are kept wherever am decided at is set (a deliberate reassignment); the party projection and the nightly recomputeSalesPeople both honour it. The sheet never writes money. No path writes a receipt, paid amount , a bill status or outstanding from a sheet. New bills are inserted with payment position = 'unstated' (held out of outstanding, ageing, collections, slow-payer and reminders) and only on INSERT. A person's receipt or the receivables report states them. revert-sheet-paid exists to undo receipts an older importer wrote with source = 'sheet import' , and touches nothing else.

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A new source is a staging table plus runSync. Read with readWindows , hash with hashRow , write only changed rows, and wrap the work in runSync so the one-per-source rule and the run row come for free. Never publish from the read step. Reading lands rows; a separate projection publishes them. Keep the two as separate modes and order them in the caller. A new mode is three edits. The JOBS map in the route, a case in runJob , and the line in sheet-sync.sh (shipped automatically) — plus the crontab line on the droplet if it is a new cadence (not shipped). When a parsing rule changes, ship a reparse. Hash-driven syncs never revisit an unchanged row; without a reparse the new rule never lands. Never let a projection write money. No receipts, no paid amount , no status or outstanding — and payment position = 'unstated' on insert only.

Mahek's team still types much of its work into Google Sheets — the orders as they are billed, the payment status of each order, orders as they are first taken, the party list, the employee list, and the older field app's shop master and activity log. MahekOne reads those workbooks on a schedule and publishes what it finds into its own database, so the CRM, Accounts and the field app see the same customers, orders and bills the team is typing. Alongside the sync, the same schedule runs the jobs that keep every derived figure current: buying cycles, outstanding balances, follow-up stages, salesman scores, the next day's calling lists. This page explains what is read, how often, the rules that keep a spreadsheet from overriding a decision somebody made in MahekOne, and what runs each night. The developer tab has the endpoint, the modes and the commands.

search.heading: What MahekOne reads
search.text: Workbook / tab What it holds What MahekOne does with it Order sheet → Order Details Every billed order line Customers, orders and bills (one bill per order) Order sheet → Payment Status Whether each order was received or not Held as evidence for accounts — it never records money Order sheet → Taken Order Orders as first taken, before billing Holds a customer back from order-chasing calls while their order is still open Sales Party sheet The party list: who sells to whom, phone numbers, areas Fills in customer details and the salesperson's name Employee workbook → Employee Details The employee master The HRMS employee list (a mirror nobody edits in MahekOne) EMP 2.0 → Activity The older field app's visit log Attached to customers' histories EMP 2.0 → Customer Details The older app's shop master Run by hand only — creates shops and leads Read-only, by construction. MahekOne reads through a Google service account that has view access to each workbook and asks Google only for a read-only permission. Even a bug could not write a cell. Nothing MahekOne does changes a spreadsheet.

search.heading: How a sync works
search.text: Every read follows the same two steps. One sync cycle. 1. Read into staging. Each row of the sheet lands in a staging table, with a fingerprint of its contents. A row whose fingerprint has not changed is not written again, so a sheet nobody touched costs one read and no writes. That is what makes a run every half hour affordable. 2. Publish. A separate step turns what has landed into real customers, orders and bills. Reading always comes before publishing in the same cycle — publishing first would ship the previous cycle's data as if it were new.

search.heading: Catching up versus a full compare
search.text: Pass How often What it notices Append (the half-hourly read) Every 30 minutes New rows added to the bottom of a sheet Reconcile (full compare) Once a night Edits to old rows, and rows deleted from the sheet A row deleted from the sheet is withdrawn — marked as gone — never silently forgotten.

search.heading: The rules that keep a sheet in its place
search.text: The sheet never writes money. No sync records a payment, sets what was paid on a bill, or changes what a customer owes. Whether money arrived is for a person to record. A bill imported from the sheet starts with no payment position at all — held out of outstanding, the ageing strip, the collections list and the reminders — until somebody records or confirms a payment against it, or the accounts team's receivables report names it. Why not just assume?. The order sheet records what was billed, never what was received. Assuming everything was owed would put the whole order book — crores — on the collections list; assuming everything was paid would hide real debt with nobody's name behind the decision. The honest third answer is "nobody has said yet", and that is what an imported bill carries. The sheet wins every column except a decision somebody made. For almost everything — a phone number, an area, a bill amount — the sheet is right and overwrites. But if accounts approved or declined an order in MahekOne, or an account was deliberately reassigned to another salesperson, the next sync keeps that decision and records the disagreement in a list for review, rather than undoing it every half hour. One sync per source at a time. If a sync of one sheet is still running when the next is due, the new one is skipped and says so ("already running"). A run stuck for more than ten minutes is treated as dead, so one hung run never blocks every later one.

search.heading: When the rule changes, not the sheet
search.text: Because unchanged rows are skipped, changing how MahekOne reads a row — for example, deciding that a "Cancel" status no longer holds a customer back — changes nothing on its own: every fingerprint still matches. A reparse re-reads what is already stored, without asking Google, and applies the new rule. It is run by a developer when the reading changes.

search.heading: The schedule
search.text: All times India time. The server's scheduler runs these; an Apps Script trigger inside the order workbook can also run the half-hourly cycle, and the "one sync per source" rule makes it harmless if both fire. When What runs Every 30 minutes Read the four order-workbook tabs, publish customers/orders/bills, read and publish field activity, punch-out reminders Every hour Salesman scores for this month, handset sweeps and escalations (overdue tasks, approvals, samples), check-in selfie deletion, WhatsApp automation and delivery receipts, complaint deadline escalation, ERP alerts and inbox, the Top customers report if the 1st's run was missed 01:43 nightly Full compare of the order workbook and field activity, publish, then every recompute 02:15 nightly Database backup — after the nightly has settled (Backups) 10:00 on the 1st The Top customers report for the month just finished

search.heading: What the nightly rebuilds
search.text: Every derived figure in MahekOne is a cache rebuilt from the records underneath. The nightly pass rebuilds all of them, in order: - Field-app housekeeping: closing visits left open, marking missed check-outs, ageing leads, raising reorder follow-ups, the lead nurture pass. - The HRMS monthly leave credit (a no-op after the first run each month), ERP alerts and digest, the expense month snapshot. - Buying cycles, sales managers, places, inactivity, follow-up stages, slow-payer flags. - Sweeping uploaded files that were never attached to anything. - Tomorrow's calling lists, the month-end customer-health snapshot, salesman scores for this and last month, copying targets forward. - Automatic end-of-day reports. A figure that somebody can edit by hand is a figure that can disagree with the orders and payments behind it. A figure that is always rebuilt cannot drift — so if one looks wrong, the fix is to run the rebuild, never to type over the number.

search.heading: The employee list
search.text: The employee workbook is small (tens of rows), so it is read with a full compare every time, and it is read while HRMS is open — the screen asks every minute — rather than on a fixed schedule. A sheet edited on a Friday evening is picked up the next time somebody opens HRMS. The password column in that sheet never reaches the database, and bank and Aadhaar numbers are kept as their last four digits.

search.heading: Running things by hand
search.text: Who Where What Accounts (holders of the sheet import permission) Admin Console → Sheets Full compare of the order sheet, Payment Status read, publish Platform administrators Admin Console → Jobs The nightly, the hourly, the day-boundary pass (end-of-day reports and rolling reminders off non-working days), and the sheet passes A developer The command line Any job by name, including reparses and one-off imports Every run, scheduled or by hand, is recorded — what ran, when, how many records it touched, and whether it succeeded — and the sheet syncs keep a record per run of rows read, created, updated, unchanged, withdrawn and with problems.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - Two schedulers may be configured. The server's crontab is the documented schedule; the Apps Script trigger files in the repository still describe themselves as the half-hourly cycle. Both are safe together, but which one a deployment actually runs is only visible on the server and in the workbook ( deploy/sheet-sync.sh , scripts/sheet-sync-trigger.gs ). - The nightly endpoint reports only its first step. Running the nightly through the sync endpoint returns the result of the first job in the pass rather than all of them; the full list is in the job history ( src/app/api/sheets/sync/route.ts ). - Rolling reminders off non-working days is never scheduled. It lives only in the day-boundary pass, which no schedule calls; it runs when an administrator presses it ( runDayBoundary in src/lib/jobs.ts ). - The EMP 2.0 shop master has no schedule. It is run by hand only, so changes in that workbook do not reach MahekOne until somebody runs it.

The attachment subsystem is one service ( attachment-service.ts ) over one storage interface ( FileStorage in src/lib/storage.ts ) with two backends: Postgres ( attachment bytes , the default) and an S3-compatible bucket (Cloudflare R2 in production, signed by hand in s3-signing.ts , no SDK). The backend is chosen once, at module load, from environment variables. Bytes are only ever read back through /api/attachments/[id] , which asks canRead first. The handset has its own upload door ( /api/mbos/media ) that lands in the same table.

search.heading: Choosing the backend
search.text: Variables set Backend None of the below Postgres R2 ACCESS KEY ID , R2 SECRET ACCESS KEY , R2 ENDPOINT (already there for backups) and R2 ATTACHMENTS BUCKET R2, region auto R2 with the bucket in the endpoint's path and no R2 ATTACHMENTS BUCKET R2, bucket from the path S3 BUCKET or S3 ENDPOINT (plus S3 ACCESS KEY ID , S3 SECRET ACCESS KEY , optional S3 REGION ) That store, overriding every R2 name; region defaults to us-east-1 Bucket resolves to the same name as R2 BUCKET Refused with a console error; Postgres is used R2's two particulars. The region is the literal word auto , and R2 ENDPOINT carries the account id and not the bucket (backup.sh reads the same variable). Both mistakes produce a bare 403 or 404. Run npm run check:storage against the target environment before relying on it — it prints the backend and which of upload, read and delete failed.

search.heading: Reading falls back; removing removes from both
search.text: s3Storage.read asks the bucket and, on anything but success, reads attachment bytes — so everything uploaded before the switch keeps opening. s3Storage.remove deletes from the bucket (a 404 counts as success) and then from attachment bytes . Nothing migrates bytes between backends; attachments.stored ref is the key in whichever store it was written to ( attachments/ ). attachment bytes is created by drizzle/0011 attachment bytes.sql and is not declared in schema.ts : three columns, ref (primary key), bytes ( bytea ) and created at . It is a separate table so that listing attachments never drags bytes through the pool.

search.heading: Uploading from a browser form
search.text: Choose a file, save the form. A failed store write records a failed row so the screen can name the file that did not make it; the action returns an error for that file and the form still saves. Binding over the limit leaves the extras unbound for the sweep rather than failing a save that already succeeded. limitFor reads , or , and returns 1 for documents, courses, price-list files and payout invoices.

search.heading: Uploading from the handset
search.text: The handset queues media separately and uploads after the parent record has synced. It chooses the attachment id itself ( mbos ), which makes a re-sent upload idempotent; an id already held by another user is refused with 409. It names the parent with its own word, mapped here: Because the camera usually closes before the record exists, the parent is often pending . The handler that writes the record calls bindMbosMedia , which binds only the uploader's own file and cannot fail the write: A new MBOS parent must be added to MBOS PARENTS and to canRead. An unmapped parentType stores the file with parent id null, and sweepOrphans deletes it the next night. This has happened twice — for every MBOS photograph, and again for the odometer photographs. The enum value, the map entry and a canRead branch are one change.

search.heading: Reading a file
search.text: GET /api/attachments/[id]. Rules worth knowing before adding a parent type: - No customer behind it (feedback, documents, courses, selfies, travel legs, expenses, price lists, ERP, HRMS, payouts) needs an explicit branch. The fall-through, customerBehind , looks the id up as a call — which is how every selfie once answered 404. - Sales evidence asks the module first, then managerScope . managerScope alone is vacuous ("national") for anybody without a region row; asking canOpenModule for sales.attendance (selfies), sales.travel / sales.expenses (legs), or sales.expenses / sales.exceptions (expenses) first stops one salesman fetching another's photograph by id. - Not-allowed and not-found are identical , so ids cannot enumerate customers.

search.heading: Removal and sweeps
search.text: Sweep Runs Selects Does sweepOrphans Nightly ( sweep-orphan-attachments in runNightly ) parent id is null and uploaded before hours ago — any status Deletes bytes from both stores, marks removed sweepAttendanceSelfies Hourly (from mbosHourly in src/lib/mbos-jobs.ts ) parent type = 'mbos attendance' , available , uploaded before hours ago Deletes bytes, marks removed , keeps the parent and every reference on the attendance day Both delete bytes before updating the row, so a crash leaves a live row over missing bytes (a 502 somebody will notice) rather than a removed row over bytes nothing will ever tidy.

search.text: Suite File What it pins npm run test src/lib/s3-signing.test.ts SigV4 against AWS's published vectors npm run test src/lib/storage-s3.test.ts The S3 backend's requests, region and bucket rules npm run test:integration src/lib/storage-fallback.test.ts Reading a pre-switch file from Postgres; refusing the backup bucket npm run test:integration src/lib/activity-location.test.ts The selfie sweep: window from arrival, row and references kept npm run test:integration src/lib/expense-attachments.test.ts Travel and expense evidence binds and reads under the right rules

search.heading: Changing it safely
search.text: A new parent type is three edits. The attachment parent enum value (in its own migration — a value cannot be used in the transaction that adds it), the ParentType union or MBOS PARENTS entry, and a canRead branch. Never serve a stored URL. Objects are private; bytes go out through /api/attachments/[id] only. Do not add an ACL header to uploads. Prove the store before switching. npm run check:storage with the target environment's variables. Never point attachments at R2 BUCKET. The backup bucket's lifecycle rules delete old objects.

Photographs and documents attached to records — a damaged can on a complaint, a cheque against a payment, a bill photograph on an expense, a check-in selfie, a meter reading on a journey, a screenshot on a feedback report, a price list PDF — all go through one attachment system . It decides what a file may be, how big, how many per record, who may open it, and what "delete" means, the same way everywhere. Where the bytes physically sit is a separate, quieter question. By default they sit in the database itself. Once a deployment configures a file bucket — Cloudflare R2, which Mahek already uses for backups — new files go there instead. Nobody using MahekOne can tell the difference.

search.heading: Two places a file can live
search.text: In the database (default) In a Cloudflare R2 bucket When No bucket configured A bucket for attachments is configured on the server Good for A few complaint photographs a week Field scale — bill and meter photographs run to hundreds of megabytes a month Backups Included in every database backup and restore automatically Not in the database backup; the bucket keeps them Cost Counted as database storage, in every backup copy Ordinary file storage, which is far cheaper Keeping files in the database means no second service, no second credential, and photographs restored together with the records they belong to — simpler in every way while the volume is small. At field scale that stops being true: every photograph is copied into every backup, nine times a week. The bucket exists for that moment, and switching to it moves nothing that is already stored. Switching to a bucket never loses an old file. Files stored before the switch stay where they were. When a file is opened, the bucket is asked first and the database second, so a photograph from before the switch still opens. Attachments never use the backup bucket. Database backups go to a bucket that deletes old copies on a schedule. If attachments were pointed at that same bucket, every photograph would quietly disappear on that schedule. The system refuses that combination and keeps using the database instead.

search.heading: What may be uploaded
search.text: - A file is judged by its contents, never its name. Renaming a document to .jpg does not make it a photograph — the first bytes of the file decide what it is. A file that is not an accepted type is refused with a message naming what it actually is. - Accepted types are — photographs and PDFs. Some screens accept more for their own purpose (the ERP's test video, dictation audio). - Size limit is megabytes per file. The document library allows larger files for catalogues. - How many per record : A library document, a training course, a price list and a vendor invoice take exactly one file — the record is its file.

search.heading: A file is uploaded before its record exists
search.text: The upload starts the moment you choose the file , not when you press Save. That is what makes a form with six photographs save instantly, and it means the record the file belongs to usually does not exist yet when the bytes arrive. So every file starts unattached , and is attached ("bound") to its record when the record is saved. From choosing a photograph to it appearing on a record. A save is never blocked by an attachment. If a photograph fails to upload, the complaint, call or payment still saves, and the screen says how many files made it. Losing a call the telecaller just logged because a picture did not upload would be far worse than the missing picture.

search.heading: On the handset
search.text: The salesman's phone works offline, so a photograph is queued and uploaded after the record it belongs to — often minutes or days later. The phone says which kind of record it belongs to (a visit, a payment, a journey, an attendance mark…), and the server attaches it as soon as both have arrived. Only the salesman's own photographs can be attached to his own records, or to customers in his own book.

search.heading: Who can open a file
search.text: Anybody who can see the record can see what is attached to it, and nobody else. A file you are not allowed to see and a file that does not exist give the same answer, so file links cannot be used to discover which customers exist. Attached to Who can open it A call, complaint, payment or anything else about a customer Whoever can see that customer A feedback report or reply The person who reported it and whoever can answer it A check-in selfie The salesman in it, and managers who hold the Sales Dashboard and can see his attendance A journey's meter or ticket photographs The salesman who took it, and Sales Dashboard managers who can see him A library document Whoever it was published to; a withdrawn document cannot be opened A training course Anybody on the field app while the course is published A price list document Whoever may read price lists An ERP or HRMS file Whoever may open the screen it belongs to Not yet attached Only the person who uploaded it Files are never served from a public address. Every file is opened through MahekOne, which checks the rule above each time.

search.heading: Check-in selfies are the one file with a clock
search.text: Every check-in and check-out on the handset takes a selfie, and that photograph exists to answer one question — was the person who marked the day the person who worked it — which is asked within a day or two or not at all. Kept longer, it stops being verification and becomes a standing collection of photographs of employees. So selfies are deleted after hours, by a sweep that runs every hour . The clock starts when the photograph arrived at the office , not when it was taken — a salesman with no signal on Monday who syncs on Wednesday still gives his manager the full window to look. Deleting the image does not erase the fact. Only the image goes. The attendance record keeps the reference to it, so "a photograph was taken at 09:04 and has since been deleted" stays different from "no photograph was taken" — which is the one that would read as somebody cutting a corner.

search.heading: Removing a file
search.text: Removing an attachment from a screen marks it removed and detaches it; the row stays, so the history of what was attached is not destroyed.

search.heading: Unattached files are swept
search.text: Files that were uploaded and never attached — a form abandoned mid-call — are swept by the nightly job once they are older than hours, and their bytes are deleted from storage.

search.heading: R2 is used for three things
search.text: Use What goes there Backups Encrypted database dumps — see Backups Handset releases Every MBOS APK, under a versioned name — see Handset release Attachments (optional) Photographs and documents, once a bucket is configured Each has its own bucket.

search.heading: Where the code and the intent disagree today
search.text: - A removed attachment's bytes are deleted the next night. The intent is that a removed file (a payment proof somebody tidied off a screen) is kept, with its bytes, until a retention period says otherwise. But removing a file also detaches it, and the nightly sweep of unattached files picks up exactly those, so the bytes go after hours ( removeAttachment and sweepOrphans in src/lib/services/attachment-service.ts ). - The retention setting is not read. says how long a removed file's bytes are kept, but no code reads it. - "This file has been deleted" is never shown. The file endpoint is meant to answer that a swept selfie existed and is gone; but the permission check refuses any file that is not live first, so a swept file answers "not found" like a file that never existed ( canRead and src/app/api/attachments/[id]/route.ts ).
